findings.title: TRA and GBT are booked PER WINNER with Math.round in the ledger while levySplit computes them ONCE over the whole fee — the ledger's GBT can book ZERO on a settlement that owes it, and the ledger is the side that holds the money
findings.functionName: settlementPayoutEntries (called once per winning position from market-service.ts settleMarket:3582)
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: settleMarket computes ONE fee for the market (poolFee, market-service.ts:3266) and splits it across winners by largest remainder (allocateFeeShares, market-service.ts:3531) so the shares sum to floor(fee) exactly. It then computes the levies ONCE at market-service.ts:3278 — `const settleLevies = levySplit(settleFee.fee, settleCfg)` — but that value NEVER reaches the ledger. It is used only for the audit payload's `levies` field (:3729) and the referral/agent accrual base (:3688). The money is written by settlementPayoutEntries, which re-derives BOTH levies from THIS winner's share alone: `const traLevyAmt = Math.round(commAmt * opts.rates.traTaxOnCommissionRate); const gbtLevyAmt = Math.round(commAmt * opts.rates.gbtLevyOnCommissionRate);` (ledger.ts:367-368), where `commAmt` is that one winner's allocated slice. So HOUSE:TRA_LEVY and HOUSE:GBT_LEVY receive Σ_w round(c_w·rate) instead of round(Σ c_w ·rate). Because Math.round(x)=0 for x<0.5, a winner whose fee share is ≤9 TZS books ZERO GBT (0.05×9 = 0.45) and a share ≤4 books zero TRA.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.2: "TRA 10% and GBT 5% are levied on the fee *we* earned. Enforced in `payout.ts` → `levySplit`." The levy base named by the rule is the market's single fee, and the function named by the rule is levySplit. The ledger neither calls levySplit nor uses its result; it applies the rate to 15/60/1,000 separate fragments and sums the roundings. Σ_w round(c_w·r) ≠ round((Σ_w c_w)·r) in general, and the divergence is systematic and unbounded in the number of winners (±0.5 TZS per winner per levy). The shortfall is invisible to every existing guard because each settlement group still sums to zero — POOL −(payout+comm), PLAYER +payout, COMMISSION +comm −tra −gbt, TRA +tra, GBT +gbt — so whatever the levies are, the books balance. This is the exact self-cancelling shape that hid the 2026-08-11 commission defect the same function's own docstring describes. The defect is model-agnostic: settlementPayoutEntries never reads feeModel, so it hits loser-share polls, Up & Down, and the legacy capped-commission markets alike.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.2 (Taxes are only ever on OUR commission — levied on the fee we earned, enforced in levySplit). Secondary: §2.4 (positions per market unlimited, which is what makes small per-winner shares reachable).
findings.concreteScenario: An Up & Down round settles YES. Sixty winning positions of TZS 1,000 each (winningPool 60,000 — RULES §2.4 allows unlimited positions and each bet mints its own Position row at market-service.ts:1260, so this is 60 bets, not necessarily 60 people) against a losing side of TZS 4,000 (four min-stake bets). Every stake is inside 1,000…1,000,000. Loser-share fee = 0.13 × 4,000 = 520. allocateFeeShares(60 winners, 60,000, 520) → floor(520/60)=8 for each, remainder 520−480=40, so 40 winners get 9 and 20 get 8 (verified by running a verbatim transcription of allocateFeeShares). Ledger, per winner: GBT = round(9×0.05)=round(0.45)=0 and round(8×0.05)=round(0.40)=0 → HOUSE:GBT_LEVY credited **0**. TRA = round(9×0.10)=round(0.9)=1 and round(8×0.10)=round(0.8)=1 → HOUSE:TRA_LEVY credited **60**. levySplit(520, {0.10, 0.05}) = { traLevy 52, gbtLevy 26, operatorNet 442 }. So the ledger books TRA 60 / GBT 0 / commission-net 460, against the rule's TRA 52 / GBT 26 / operator 442. Worst case measured inside the bounds: 1,000 winning positions of 1,000 vs a 69,000 losing side → fee 8,970, every share 8 or 9, GBT booked **0** against 449 owed and TRA booked 1,000 against 897. The error also runs the other way: 200 positions of 1,000 vs a 20,000 losing side gives every winner a 13 TZS share → TRA books 200 against 260 (short 60) and GBT books 200 against 130 (over 70). The legacy capped arm is worse on the same shape: 60 winners of 1,000 vs a 1,000 loser → fee = min(0.10×61,000, ⅓×1,000) = 333, shares 5–6, GBT booked 0 against 17 and TRA booked 60 against 33.
findings.moneyImpact: The state is short-changed on GBT and the operator over-remits TRA, on the same settlement. On the 60-winner example: GBT under-remitted by 26 TZS (100% of what is owed — the account records that this market generated no GBT at all), TRA over-remitted by 8 TZS, and net 18 TZS that should have moved to the levy accounts stays in HOUSE:COMMISSION. That 18 is then reported to the owner as retained profit: house-book.ts:255 computes `netRetained: g.feeBooked - g.leviesBooked` and house-ledger.ts reads leviesBooked straight off the LedgerEntry rows, so /admin/house and /admin/house/[marketId] state the wrong liability ("Then the levies: <Amt v={g.leviesBooked} /> of the fee went to TRA and GBT", [marketId]/page.tsx:204). Per settlement the magnitude is bounded by roughly 0.5 × (number of winning positions) per levy — 449 TZS of GBT on the 1,000-winner case — and it REPEATS on every settled market, accumulating in the levy accounts the operator files from. It is also self-inconsistent inside one settlement: the referral/agent accrual is priced on settleLevies.operatorNet (market-service.ts:3688 — 442 in the example) while the ledger says the house actually kept 460, so RULES §2.10's commission base and the books disagree by construction.

findings.title: hydrateNow() closes the hydration gate on a read that FAILED — `loadConfig` swallows the DB error and returns null, so the commit's own claim "a failure leaves the flag DOWN so the next read retries" is false
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Commit 2499f324 moved `__50PICK_MARKET_CONFIG_HYDRATED = true` from before the await to after it and added a shared in-flight promise. That genuinely fixes the CONCURRENT-CALLER half of §1.2 — a second caller arriving during the round-trip now awaits instead of reading defaults. It does NOT fix the half the docblock's own first sentence names. `loadConfig` (config-store.ts:14-25) catches every query error, `console.error`s it, and returns `null`. `hydrateNow` therefore RESOLVES normally on a DB failure, `if (stored)` is false, `store.global` stays at `{ ...DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG }` (market-config.ts:426-431), `store.perMarket` stays an empty Map, and line 527 raises the flag anyway. There is no retry, because from this function's point of view a failed read and an empty table are the same event. The docblock four lines above the fix says "`loadConfig` never throws — it logs and returns `null`" and then, twenty lines later, "a failure leaves the flag DOWN so the next read retries." Both sentences are in the file; the second is contradicted by the first. The only way the flag stays down is an exception raised OUTSIDE loadConfig's try (a `new PrismaClient()` throw at prisma.ts:88-95, which is outside loadConfig's try block) or `new Map(non-iterable)` at line 518 — neither of which is the transient-blip case the fix was written for.
findings.whyItIsWrong: One transient Postgres error at first read still pins the container on DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG for the whole life of the process, exactly as before, and this repo documents that blip happening (prisma.ts:63-66: "observed 2026-07-24: a Railway internal-network blip made all pooled connections hang, cascading into P2024s — the pool was fine, the DB was briefly gone"). The two consequences the docblock itself enumerates both stand: (1) `createMarket` stamps `snapshotFromConfig(await getEffectiveConfig(id))` (market-service.ts:662-665) into an immutable feeSnapshot, so a poll created in that window settles at code defaults FOREVER; (2) `persist()` writes `{ global: store.global, perMarket: Array.from(store.perMarket.entries()) }` (line 531-533) — the WHOLE snapshot — so the next unrelated admin save overwrites the officer's live row AND erases every per-market override with an empty array. There is nothing on any screen that distinguishes a hydrated process from a de-hydrated one.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.3's recorded trap ("A code default is not a live setting") — running in the opposite direction: here the live setting silently becomes the code default. Also RULES.md §2.1 (a feeSnapshot is never rewritten, so a poll frozen at the wrong rate is permanent) and the DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG.objectionWindowHours docblock at market-config.ts:238-252, which forbids the objection window moving on anything but a recorded human act.
findings.concreteScenario: market-config.ts:238-252 states that the objection window's code default moved 24 → 1 on 2026-09-05 and that "CHANGING THIS CONSTANT DOES NOT CHANGE PRODUCTION … the flip is an audited act through /admin/config". Assume that audited flip has not yet been performed, so the persisted `SystemConfig["market.config"].global.objectionWindowHours` is still 24. A Railway container boots during a 3-second DB blip; the first `getEffectiveConfig` call swallows a P2024, `store.global.objectionWindowHours` = 1, flag up. The DB recovers 3 seconds later; nothing retries. Two hours later an officer opens /admin/config to bump the GBT levy. The Objection-window field's own hint (config-form.tsx:196) reads "Currently 1h" — a number nobody chose — and the officer, seeing nothing wrong, saves. `persist()` writes objectionWindowHours: 1 to the DB. A poll sealed the next morning with YES 1,000,000 / NO 1,000,000 stamps objectionsClosedAt at seal+1h instead of seal+24h. A player holding a 1,000,000 TZS position who believes the verdict is wrong now has 60 minutes, not 24 hours, to object before `settleDueMarkets` pays the pool out and the money is gone — and the audit records that change buried among 18 other unchanged numbers (LEAD-B.1a), so no one can see the control moved.
findings.moneyImpact: Two distinct losses. (a) IRREVERSIBLE: any poll created while the container is de-hydrated freezes DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG into its feeSnapshot and settles by it forever — on a 2,000,000 TZS pool the difference between any live rate and the code default is charged to real players and cannot be corrected, because RULES §2.1 forbids rewriting a snapshot. (b) PERSISTENT: the first admin save after the failed hydration writes the code defaults over the officer's live SystemConfig row and erases the per-market override list (see LEAD-B.2b), so the damage outlives the container. The magnitude of (a) and the direction of (b) depend on how far the live persisted values sit from the constants, which needs a production read.

findings.title: The daily wallet↔ledger trial balance runs in production, finds drift, and tells nobody — its entire alarm is one audit row and one console line, and grep finds no consumer of either
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Once every 24h on the leader-leased lifecycle pass, `maybeReconcileLedger()` calls `trialBalance()`. When `tb.ok` is false it does exactly two things: `console.error(...)` (lifecycle.ts:97-101) and `await audit({ category: "COMPLIANCE", action: "ledger.trial_balance_drift", ... }).catch(() => {})`. It then returns. Nothing else in the repo reacts.
findings.whyItIsWrong: A repo-wide grep for `trial_balance_drift` returns exactly ONE hit — the write at lifecycle.ts:104. There is no reader. notification-service.ts exposes four operational alarms that DO reach a human (`notifyAdminsAmlReview` :1446, `notifyAdminsSentinelDown` :1490, `notifyAdminsAiCreditLimit` :1533, `notifyAdminsBackupUnhealthy` :1588), each fanning out to the in-app bell + Postmark email for every ADMIN/COMPLIANCE officer. There is no `notifyAdminsLedgerDrift`. `audit()` (audit.ts:426-463) only writes a row and pushes onto a ring; it has no notification hook. Sentry never sees it either: `captureServerError` is called only from instrumentation.ts:132, admission.ts:182/198 and updown-scheduler.ts:310, and `maxBreadcrumbs` defaults to 0 (monitoring.ts:102) so a `console.error` does not travel. The console line dies in Railway's rotating buffer — monitoring.ts:137-140 records that exact loss: "we went looking for a payout failure roughly ten minutes old and Railway's buffer had already rolled past it". The only visual surface is /admin/page.tsx:44 `const recent = getAuditPage({ limit: 12 })` — TWELVE unfiltered rows off the per-container in-memory ring (audit.ts:479-485), which on a live platform writing a row per login/bet/deposit/settlement is seconds of history and empties on every deploy. `/api/health` reports `ticker`, `leadership`, `email`, `redis`, `monitoring` — and no ledger field at all. This is the backup watchdog's own stated failure mode (backup/watchdog.ts:4-10, THE ELEVEN NIGHTS) reproduced verbatim on the money books, with no watchdog written for it.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency. docs/MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION.md §3.3 raises it as a lead; RULES.md §6a warns those 59 leads are UNVERIFIED. Confirmed here in source. NOTE: the lead's wording "No production money-invariant job exists" is WRONG — the job exists and runs daily; the defect is that its alarm has no delivery channel.
findings.concreteScenario: A player deposits TZS 200,000 and stakes TZS 50,000 on a market. The wallet debit and the Transaction row commit, but `postLedgerEntries` for the STAKE group is on the non-tx path and fails three times against a blipping Postgres (ledger.ts:140-163) → `ledger.post_failed` audit row, wallet down 50,000, ledger unchanged. That night `trialBalance()` computes walletReal = 150,000 vs ledgerReal = 200,000 → realDrift = −50,000, `ok:false`. lifecycle.ts writes ONE console.error and ONE COMPLIANCE audit row. Railway's log buffer rolls past the console line within the hour; the audit row is pushed off /admin's 12-row dashboard within seconds. No bell rings, no email is sent, no page 503s. The platform's books are wrong by TZS 50,000 and the state of the platform is indistinguishable, to every human, from healthy. It stays that way until somebody happens to open /admin/finance (page.tsx:111) or /admin/house (page.tsx:148).
findings.moneyImpact: Unbounded and open-ended: EVERY wallet↔ledger divergence — a lost stake group, an unledgered credit, a mis-settled payout — is detected and then discarded. A real one has already happened: scripts/ops-clear-unledgered-credit.mjs:5-8 records "one wallet holding TZS 100,000 with no LedgerEntry". The loss is not the drift itself, it is the unbounded TIME the drift survives before a human stumbles on it — and on a licensed operator that window is also the regulator's finding.

findings.title: `maybeReconcileLedger` advances its 24-hour clock BEFORE running the check, so any throw from `trialBalance()` skips the platform's only money invariant for a full day, silently and with no counter anywhere
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Line 90 returns early if less than RECONCILE_EVERY_MS (24h) has passed. Line 91 stamps `lastReconcileAt = now`. Line 92 THEN awaits `trialBalance()`. There is no try/catch inside the function; the caller at line 443 swallows into a console line: `await maybeReconcileLedger().catch((e) => console.error("[lifecycle] trial balance:", e));`
findings.whyItIsWrong: The stamp is a commitment made before the work is done, so a throw is indistinguishable from a success as far as scheduling is concerned — and there is no retry, no backoff, no failure counter, and nothing that surfaces "the trial balance last SUCCEEDED at X". `/api/health` line 95 exposes `ticker: lifecycleTickerHealth()`, which reports only `running/runningForMs/skippedConsecutive/skippedTotal` — a pass that COMPLETED with the trial balance throwing inside it registers as a perfectly healthy tick. `trialBalance()` is not a cheap call: it does four unbounded scans (ledger.ts:812 `pc.wallet.findMany` over every wallet; :821 grouped scan over LedgerEntry WHERE account LIKE 'PLAYER%'; :839 `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM "LedgerEntry"` full table; :842 `reconcileLedger()` GROUP BY groupId + COUNT(DISTINCT groupId) over the whole table). backup-nightly.yml:37-47 records that this exact function against production data "asked for a 70,190,496-byte segment" and killed seven consecutive nightly runs — and it grows with the database. Against a 40-connection Prisma pool (prisma.ts:29) shared with the bet path, a P2024 pool timeout, a statement timeout or an OOM is an ordinary Tuesday, not an exotic failure. Worse, it is not random: the trial balance always runs at the same offset from boot, is the heaviest query in the pass, and if the contention that kills it is structural it kills it every single day while the platform reports HTTP 200.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency; it defeats the mechanism RULES §6a / MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION §3.3 assume exists
findings.concreteScenario: 03:07 EAT. A settlement burst on a 900,000-TZS pool has most of the 40 pooled connections held inside `withMoneyTx` transactions. The lifecycle pass reaches `maybeReconcileLedger`; `lastReconcileAt` is stamped; `pc.wallet.findMany()` throws `P2024 Timed out fetching a new connection from the connection pool`. The pass's `.catch()` prints one line. Meanwhile that same settlement has left a TZS 340,000 gap between the wallets and the ledger. The trial balance will not be attempted again for 24 hours. If the contention repeats at the same offset tomorrow — and it is the same query at the same point in the same pass — the invariant never runs at all, while /api/health returns 200 with `ticker.skippedConsecutive: 0` and /admin/compliance shows a green backup card. Nothing on the platform can distinguish "the books balanced last night" from "the check never executed".
findings.moneyImpact: Turns finding LEAD-G.1 from "the alarm is not delivered" into "the alarm is never even computed". Any drift — the TZS 340,000 above, or the TZS 100,000 unledgered credit already seen in production — persists indefinitely with zero evidence anywhere that the detector stopped. The one-line fix (stamp AFTER a successful run, or keep a `lastReconcileOkAt` and surface it on /api/health) is the difference between a detector and a decoration.

findings.title: The nightly production trial-balance run DOES have an alarm channel beside it — and that channel is structurally deaf: `backupHealth()` never reads `sourceWarnings`, so a drifting production ledger is reported as a healthy backup and the watchdog stays silent
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: backup-nightly.yml runs `trialBalance()` against the PRODUCTION database every night (workflow env DATABASE_URL = `secrets.BACKUP_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL`, line 65; comment line 70: "trialBalance()/verifyChainFull() run against the SOURCE"; db-backup.mts:539-541). Drift is captured into `sourceIntegrity` and re-emitted by the verifier as `sourceWarnings` on the recorded BackupRun (db-verify-backup.mts:474-481, 511). The run is recorded with `ok: true` and `verified: failures.length === 0` (lines 501-502) and the job exits 0. `backupHealth()` then classifies that run by branching on `run.ok`, `run.verified` and age ONLY. `sourceWarnings` is never read. `describeBackupAlert` (watchdog.ts:43-58) switches on `h.kind` alone, so it returns `{ alert: false }`, `runBackupWatchdog` returns `{ alerted: false }` (line 83) and `notifyAdminsBackupUnhealthy` — the one alarm on this platform that reaches an officer's bell AND their inbox — is never called.
findings.whyItIsWrong: This is the single place where a production money invariant and a live delivery channel are ten lines apart, and the wire is not connected. The decision to keep `verified: true` on a source problem is correct and well-argued (state.ts:54-65: a faithful copy of an unhealthy database is a GOOD backup) — but the argument was carried only as far as the compliance CARD, never as far as the ALARM. Worse, the compliance card renders the drift inside a card whose StatusPill is computed from `backup.kind` and therefore reads green `✓ Backup verified` (compliance/page.tsx:206-218) with the source warning as a small `text-warning-fg` block below it (lines 250-264). And `scripts/backup.test.mts:524-528` ASSERTS the silence as the intended behaviour — "a source problem still lets the run record verified=true" — which is a guard whose green tick is compatible with the alarm never firing. Apply the discriminating question to that guard: would it still pass if officer notification on source drift existed? Yes. Would it still pass if it did not? Yes — and it does not. The guard cannot see the difference it is supposed to be about.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency; the platform's own doctrine, backup/watchdog.ts:4-21 ("a tool an operator must REMEMBER TO RUN, so the failure mode was structurally unchanged") is violated by the same module
findings.concreteScenario: Production carries one wallet holding TZS 100,000 with no LedgerEntry behind it — the exact state scripts/ops-clear-unledgered-credit.mjs:5-8 records as having happened. At 00:15 UTC the nightly runs, `trialBalance()` returns `ok:false, driftingWallets:1, totalAbsDrift:100000`, and db-verify-backup.mts:475-481 pushes "trial balance fails on the SOURCE: 1 drifting wallet(s), 100000 TZS" into `sourceWarnings`. The run is written as `{ ok: true, verified: true, sourceWarnings: [...] }`, the job exits 0 and GitHub shows a green tick. Next morning the leader container calls `runBackupWatchdog()`: `backupHealth()` returns `{ kind: "ok" }`, `describeBackupAlert` returns `{ alert: false }`, and the function returns before line 89. Zero bells, zero emails. /admin/compliance shows a GREEN 'Backup verified' pill. TZS 100,000 of books-vs-money divergence is measured, written down, and deliberately not announced — every night, indefinitely.
findings.moneyImpact: The measurement already exists and is already produced nightly against the real database — this defect throws the answer away. Any divergence of any size (the observed one was TZS 100,000) is detected daily and never announced, so the discovery latency is bounded only by how often an officer opens /admin/compliance and reads a small amber block inside a green card. On a licensed operator, an undetected books-vs-money divergence is also a regulatory exposure, not just a cash one.

findings.title: /legal/terms §4 promises free cancellation with ONLY the window condition, in all three languages — the runway condition that makes it unreachable on Up & Down 3- and 5-minute rounds is absent from the binding contract
findings.functionName: content(objectionHours) — LegalSection n="4" "How price-competition markets work"
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The binding Terms of Service state a flat, unconditional 5-minute free cancellation. EN (line 120-121): "Cash-out is available for a short window after placing a bet: within the first 5 minutes you may sell for a full refund at no charge. After that the position is locked and rides to settlement — it cannot be sold." SW (line 246-247): "Kuuza dau (cash-out) kunapatikana kwa muda mfupi baada ya kuweka dau: ndani ya dakika 5 za kwanza unaweza kuuza na kurudishiwa dau lako kamili bila malipo. Baada ya hapo dau linafungwa na linaenda hadi malipo — haliwezi kuuzwa." [transliteration: "Selling a bet (cash-out) is available for a short time after placing a bet: within the FIRST 5 MINUTES you can sell and be refunded your FULL stake at NO CHARGE. After that the bet locks and rides to payout — it cannot be sold."] ZH (line 359-360): "下注后有一小段兑现（cash-out）窗口：前 5 分钟内您可全额取回本金且不收取任何费用。此后持仓将被锁定并保留至结算 — 无法卖出。" [pinyin: "Xiazhu hou you yi xiaoduan duixian (cash-out) chuangkou: qian 5 fenzhong nei nin ke quan'e quhui benjin qie bu shouqu renhe feiyong. Cihou chicang jiang bei suoding bing baoliu zhi jiesuan — wufa mai chu." / literal: "After betting there is a short cash-out window: within the FIRST 5 MINUTES you may retrieve your principal IN FULL and no fee is charged. After that the position will be locked and held to settlement — it cannot be sold."] None of the three states the RUNWAY condition. None states the NOT-BONUS-FUNDED condition. The word "Up & Down" does not appear anywhere in the file (grep returns zero hits), so no product carve-out narrows the promise.
findings.whyItIsWrong: market-service.ts:2704 requires THREE conditions — `const sellable = hadRunway && withinWindow && !bonusFunded;` — and line 2688 defines `const hadRunway = graceMs > 0 && closesAt - placedAt >= graceMs;`. On Up & Down, `selectionClosedAt` is set to open + durationMinutes (updown-service.ts:769 -> updown-durations.ts:251, whose own comment says "The lock is the close minus the RESULT PHASE, which lands it exactly `durationMinutes` after the open — the whole advertised duration is bettable"), so a 3-minute round's entire betting window is 180s and a 5-minute round's is 300s, both against a 300,000 ms grace. `ALLOWED_DURATIONS = [3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60]` (updown-durations.ts:85) confirms 3- and 5-minute chains exist. RULES §2.6 records the production measurement: best-ever open-price confirmation was boundary + 72.4s over 9,320 readings, so max runway is 107.6s (3 min) and 227.6s (5 min) — both below 300s, and "CASHED_OUT positions — long-form 5, Up & Down 0 of 688, ever." RULES §2.6 names this failure class explicitly: "The defect was that this document, which calls itself the only statement of the money rules, promised a right on a product where it cannot be exercised. Overstating what a player gets is the same failure class as overstating a control to the Gaming Board" and "Anyone quoting the 5-minute cancellation to a player, an auditor or the Board must say which product and which round length." The terms are the BINDING text (the page itself says so: "The English version of this document is the legally binding text") and they do exactly what §2.6 forbids. The platform demonstrably knows the caveat: the FAQ carries it in all three locales (i18n-dict.ts:1951 EN "(a bet placed close to when betting shuts can't be sold at all)", :4074 SW "(dau lililowekwa karibu na kufungwa kwa uwekaji haliwezi kuuzwa)", :6120 ZH "（在投注即将关闭时下的注则无法卖出）"), and the bet-confirm modal swaps to `noExitWindowBody` when `hasExitRunway` is false. Only the contract omits it.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.6 (Free cancellation — the RUNWAY and NOT-BONUS-FUNDED conditions) and §1's rule table row: "unreachable on Up & Down 3- and 5-minute rounds"
findings.concreteScenario: A player reads /legal/terms in Kiswahili, then stakes TZS 1,000,000 (the §2.3 maximum, one bet) on a 5-minute Up & Down BTC round 40 seconds after the round appears on the board. Round opened at boundary + 80s (typical; median confirmation is 91.3s), so closesAt - placedAt = 300s - 80s - 40s = 180,000 ms < graceMs 300,000 ms. `hadRunway` is false, `sellable` is false, `reason` is "TOO_SHORT" (market-service.ts:2716). Ten seconds later the price moves against them and they hit Sell. There is no Sell control and the server would refuse. The round closes down; they lose the whole TZS 1,000,000. The contract they accepted at registration told them, in the language they read it in, that they could have had every shilling of it back at no charge for another 4 minutes 10 seconds.
findings.moneyImpact: Every Up & Down bet on a 3- or 5-minute chain is exposed: up to TZS 1,000,000 per bet, unlimited bets per round (§1 accepted consequence: the per-bet cap does not bound total exposure). Production has already run 688 Up & Down rounds with 0 cash-outs ever. The loss is not caused by the code — the code is correct per §2.6 — it is a mis-selling exposure: any player who relied on the clause has a claim for the full stake, and the same overstatement sits in the document a Gaming Board reviewer would read.
findings.evidence:
src/app/legal/terms/page.tsx:120-121  `Cash-out is available for a short window after placing a bet: within the first 5 minutes you may sell for` / `a full refund at no charge. After that the position is locked and rides to settlement — it cannot be sold.`

src/lib/server/market-service.ts:2688  `const hadRunway = graceMs > 0 && closesAt - placedAt >= graceMs;`
