findings.title: The withdrawal debit and its Transaction row are in SEPARATE commits — a failure between them strands the player's money in `hold` with no record, invisible to reconcile AND to the trial balance
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Phase A runs inside `withLock('wallet:<userId>')`. Under Postgres `withLock` opens a Prisma `$transaction` and publishes its `tx` on AsyncLocalStorage (locks.ts:126-140). But withdraw's lock callback is declared `async () => {` — it never takes the `tx` — and neither `db.wallet.adjust(...)` (line 1630) nor `db.txn.create({...})` (line 1638) is passed one. In prisma-dal both methods resolve their client as `const db: Db = tx ?? pc();` (prisma-dal.ts:1281 and 1307) and `pc()` returns the plain singleton PrismaClient (prisma-dal.ts:69-73). There is no `$extends`/`$use` middleware anywhere in src. So the balance→hold move autocommits on one pooled connection and the Transaction INSERT autocommits on a later one, outside the advisory-lock transaction entirely. Every other money path in the repo does the opposite: settleWithdrawalConfirmed wraps its three writes in `withMoneyTx` and threads `tx` into each (wallet-service.ts:615-621), and buyPosition does the same (market-service.ts:1312-1317).
findings.whyItIsWrong: `withLock`'s own contract says "Everything inside ONE withLock now shares ONE transaction, so a throw rolls back every write made under the lock" (locks.ts:158-160). That is false for these two writes. If `db.txn.create` fails after `db.wallet.adjust` has committed, the money is gone from the player's spendable balance, sitting in `Wallet.hold`, with no Transaction row that any recovery path can find. `reconcileStalePayments` starts from `db.txn.listByStatus("PROCESSING")` (wallet-service.ts:1228), so it cannot see it. `/admin/payments` derives its stuck count from the same table. And `trialBalance` compares `Wallet.balance + Wallet.hold` against the ledger (ledger.ts:693-697, 766) — moving money from balance into hold changes neither side, and no ledger group is posted at request time, so the books balance to the shilling while the player's money is unreachable. This is exactly the class `docs/MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION.md` §3.2 raises as a blocker ("debit and Transaction row in separate commits") — raised there for the FAILED path, and true here on the REQUEST path.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.8 (a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and NOTHING ELSE) — a permanently stranded hold is an uncompensated deduction; docs/MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION.md §3.2 blocker
findings.concreteScenario: Player holds TZS 300,000 and requests a TZS 200,000 withdrawal to their registered M-Pesa number. Line 1630 commits: balance 300,000 → 100,000, hold 0 → 200,000. Line 1638 then needs a second pooled connection while the enclosing `$transaction` already pins one; the pool is configured `connection_limit=40, pool_timeout=10` (prisma.ts:68-80) and this file records a real production event where "a Railway internal-network blip made all pooled connections hang, cascading into P2024s". The INSERT throws P2024/P2028 (or the container takes SIGTERM mid-rolling-deploy). The throw escapes withLock, rolls back the advisory transaction — which contains nothing but `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock` — and the request 500s. Final state: TZS 200,000 in `Wallet.hold`, zero Transaction rows, `reconcileStalePayments` blind, `trialBalance` drift = 0.00, `/admin/payments` stuck-payout count = 0. The player is permanently short TZS 200,000 and nothing in the platform records that a withdrawal was ever attempted.
findings.moneyImpact: The player loses the full requested amount — up to TZS 1,000,000 inside the stated bounds, up to TZS 5,000,000 by WithdrawSchema — permanently and silently. Nobody can find it: every existing instrument (reconcile sweep, stuck-payout count, trial balance, house-money census §3) reports clean. Recovery requires hand SQL against `Wallet.hold` with no transaction to join to.

findings.title: creditInternal fabricates the new balance when the wallet UPDATE fails and returns a non-null number, so every caller records money as PAID that never moved
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Inside the wallet lock it reads the wallet, issues an unguarded, non-transactional increment, and then computes the new balance with a `??` fallback that CANNOT be null. `db.wallet.adjust` returns `null` on a failed write (prisma-dal.ts:1300 `try { return await run(); } catch { return null; }`, and prisma-dal.ts:1294 `if (res.count === 0) return null;`). On that null, creditInternal does not abort: it invents `wallet.balance + amount`, writes a CONFIRMED Transaction whose `balanceAfter` is that invented figure (line 1904), posts a balanced ledger group crediting PLAYER:<user> the full amount (line 1924), audits `wallet.credit_internal` with `balanceAfter` = the invented figure (line 1931), pushes the invented figure to the player's live balance pill (line 1933) and returns it (line 1934). The documented contract in the function's own doc-block — "Returns the new balance, or null if the wallet is missing/frozen, the player is self-excluded / cooling-off, or the amount is non-positive" — has no clause for a failed write, and the code has no branch for one.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Every caller's success test is `!== null` / truthiness, so a failed money movement is indistinguishable from a successful one. The named caller that writes a PAID record on it is `onRecruitSettlement`: `const credited = await creditWallet(...)` (affiliate-service.ts:1315) → `creditWallet` returns `(await creditInternal(...)) !== null` (affiliate-service.ts:705) → `const status: StoredReferralReward["status"] = credited ? "PAID" : policy.programme === "AGENT" ? "PENDING" : "HELD"` (affiliate-service.ts:1326-1328). recordReward then does `if (input.status === "PAID" ...) await db.affiliate.incrementEarned(input.referrerUserId, input.amountTzs)` (affiliate-service.ts:776), and affiliate-service.ts:1357-1358 emails the agent that the money is in their cash balance. The sibling payer in the same file states the invariant this breaks, verbatim at affiliate-service.ts:991-993: "If the credit can't land (frozen/missing wallet), record the reward as HELD rather than PAID — otherwise the ledger claims money was paid that never moved, and the held queue lets an officer retry it." creditInternal makes that impossible to honour, because it never reports a failed landing. The ledger group it posts sums to zero perfectly while the wallet holds nothing — the books balance and the money is missing.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.10 — the accrual row's Standing/Money terms: an agent's commission is "Real, withdrawable cash — TxnType.AGENT_COMMISSION into the agent's cash balance", and commission not actually paid is "a PENDING payable ... never HELD, never destroyed". A row stamped PAID for money still in the house is neither.
findings.concreteScenario: Agent A (approved, live rate 10%, withholding 5%) recruited player P. P places one bet of TZS 100,000 (inside the §2.3 bounds) on a long-form poll; using RULES §2.10's own guarded fixture the position's attributable `operatorNetFee` is TZS 6,375. onRecruitSettlement computes `grossCut = Math.floor(6375 * 0.10) = 637`; `splitWithholding(637, 5)` gives tax 32, net 605. It calls `creditInternal(A, 605, { type: "AGENT_COMMISSION", taxWithheld: 32 })`. The wallet UPDATE fails (a dropped pooled connection, a statement/lock timeout on the Wallet row, or any error inside `run()`), so `db.wallet.adjust` returns null. A's balance stays at 0. creditInternal returns 0 + 605 = 605. Outcome: a CONFIRMED AGENT_COMMISSION Transaction for 605 with balanceAfter = 605; a balanced ledger group `int_txn_…` reading HOUSE:AGENT_COMMISSION −637 / PLAYER:A +605 / HOUSE:TAX +32; a ReferralReward row `status: "PAID", amountTzs: 605, grossAmountTzs: 637, taxWithheldTzs: 32`; `incrementEarned(A, +605)`; and an email to A headed "Agent commission · TZS 637" saying it "is in your cash balance as withdrawable money". A's wallet holds 0. Nothing retries: PAID is terminal for the accrual and `sourceRef = referral:commission:<marketId>:<positionId>` is now taken, so the replay path RULES §2.10 relies on ("a re-settlement cannot pay twice") now refuses the payment that never happened.
findings.moneyImpact: The agent loses the whole net accrual (TZS 605 in this scenario) while every platform record says it was paid, so no officer queue, no payable and no replay will ever recover it. The house simultaneously books TZS 32 into HOUSE:TAX as withholding it never actually withheld, and debits HOUSE:AGENT_COMMISSION TZS 637 it never actually spent — overstating programme cost and understating cash. Repeats once per failed write; the same fabrication runs for proposal prizes (proposals-service.ts:637-642, where the player is emailed "Proposal approved · TZS <prize> credited") and for player-promo referral bonuses and prizes (affiliate-service.ts:993, 1045). The only control that would ever notice is the nightly `trialBalance` (ledger.ts:806), which reports an unexplained per-user drift a day later with no cause attached.

findings.title: An AML-held withdrawal carries a NEVER-DISPATCHED id in `providerRef`, and approve-dispatch flips the row to PROCESSING without clearing it — the reconcile sweep then re-queries a transid Selcom never saw, reads FAILED, and refunds a payout that is in flight
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: When a withdrawal crosses the AML threshold, `dispatchWithdrawal` returns BEFORE any adapter is touched with `providerRef: correlationId` (payments.ts:209) — our own `wdr_…` id that no gateway has ever received — and `withdraw()` writes it straight into `Transaction.providerRef` at wallet-service.ts:1777 before flipping the row to AML_REVIEW at 1786. `payoutRail` is left NULL (the AML arm returns no `rail`, so the spread at 1779 writes nothing). Hours later the officer approves: `dispatchApprovedWithdrawal` claims the row with `await db.txn.update(txnId, { status: "PROCESSING" })` (736) and does NOT null the stale ref, then makes the gateway call OUTSIDE the lock (742-749). The real ref is written only after the call returns (770-774). `db.txn.update` runs on `pc()` — the plain pooled client, not the lock's transaction (prisma-dal.ts:69-73, 1365-1366) — so the PROCESSING status is committed and visible to every other container the instant line 736 runs.
findings.whyItIsWrong: For the whole duration of the rail call the row is PROCESSING, `createdAt` is hours old, `providerRef` is an id the gateway has never heard of and `payoutRail` is NULL. `reconcileStalePayments` selects on `createdAt` alone (1228), so the row is in its population immediately; it then calls `verifyWithdrawalStatus(ref, t.payoutRail)` (1294) → `railOf(null)` = WALLET_CASHIN → `GET /walletcashin/query?transid=<never-sent id>`. selcomVerifyPayout's own doc comment states the consequence of asking about a transid an endpoint has never heard of: "Any resultcode that is not `000/111/927/999` falls through `envelopeSettlementVerdict` to **FAILED** — and the stale reconcile sweep treats FAILED as 'the payout definitively did not happen' and refunds the player. The money is already gone. That is a double payment, caused by nothing but asking the wrong endpoint." The identical hazard the file was hardened against for the WRONG RAIL is wide open for the WRONG REFERENCE. The same stale ref is what `reverseStuckPayoutAction`'s "machine check" (payment-actions.ts:257) asks about — the last control standing between an officer and a double payment is pointed at a transaction that does not exist. payments.ts:207-208 claims "a real providerRef is only ever minted when the gateway actually accepts the payout"; the column says otherwise from the moment the hold is placed.
findings.rulesReference: §2.8 — a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and NOTHING ELSE; the mirror obligation is that the house pays each payout ONCE. Also §2.7 (the fee is charged once on the amount withdrawn) — a re-credited gross plus a disbursed net is the same withdrawal settled twice.
findings.concreteScenario: Player has 1,200,000 TZS. At 09:00 they withdraw TZS 1,000,000 (exactly the AML threshold, top of the §2.3 band). fee = 1.5% = 15,000, net = 985,000. Row: hold 1,000,000, status AML_REVIEW, providerRef `wdr_a1b2c3d4e5` (never sent anywhere), payoutRail NULL, createdAt 09:00. At 11:20 two officers approve. 11:20:00.1 — line 736 commits status=PROCESSING; 11:20:00.2 — the ladder POSTs /walletcashin/process (PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 45,000 ms, selcom.ts:60). 11:20:03 — the 5-minute lifecycle sweep fires (lifecycle.ts:186 PAYMENT_SWEEP_EVERY_MS). createdAt 09:00 < cutoff 10:50, so the row is stale: it GETs /walletcashin/query?transid=wdr_a1b2c3d4e5, Selcom answers 200 with an unknown-transaction resultcode, `envelopeSettlementVerdict` → FAILED → `settleWithdrawalFailed(t.id, "reconcile-verified-failed")` (1305) → wallet balance +1,000,000, hold −1,000,000, txn FAILED, email "Withdrawal returned · TZS 985,000". 11:20:05 — the ladder returns ACCEPTED and line 770 writes the REAL ref onto the now-FAILED row. Selcom disburses 985,000 to the player's M-Pesa. The player ends with 985,000 in M-Pesa AND 1,000,000 back in a spendable wallet balance.
findings.moneyImpact: The house loses TZS 985,000 in cash plus the TZS 15,000 fee it never earns — TZS 1,000,000 per occurrence, one occurrence per AML-approved payout that overlaps a sweep tick. Window = the rail call's duration (≈1–5 s normally, up to 45 s on a rung timeout) against a 300 s sweep period: roughly 1–15% of every ≥1M payout. It is also permanent, not just racy: any crash, redeploy or pool timeout between line 736 and line 770 leaves the row PROCESSING with the fake ref for good, and every subsequent sweep asks the same unanswerable question. Selcom's later callback carries the REAL transid, so `settlePaymentWebhook` finds the row (ref was overwritten at 770), sees FAILED vs CONFIRMED and takes the `contradicted` arm (925-975) — it alarms, but only after the money is gone, and it deliberately claws nothing back.

findings.title: settleWithdrawalFailed refunds and flips status in TWO separate commits outside the lock transaction — the 5-minute sweep then refunds a second time
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Inside withLock(`wallet:${userId}`) the function credits the wallet (line 806) and marks the transaction FAILED (line 807). NEITHER call passes the lock's transaction client. In prisma-dal, `db.wallet.adjust(id, deltas, opts?, tx?)` and `db.txn.update(id, patch, tx?)` both resolve their client as `tx ?? pc()`, and `pc()` is the plain pooled PrismaClient (prisma-dal.ts:69) — it does NOT consult `currentLockTx()`. So both statements run on a DIFFERENT connection from the advisory-lock $transaction and each auto-commits on its own. Its twin two hundred lines above does the opposite: settleWithdrawalConfirmed wraps the identical pair in `withMoneyTx(async (tx) => …)` and threads `tx` into every call (lines 615-622), which JOINs the lock transaction (ledger.ts:58-59) so the hold release, the status flip and the ledger group commit or roll back together.
findings.whyItIsWrong: There is a durable window between the two auto-commits in which the player has been paid back but the transaction still reads PROCESSING. `reconcileStalePayments` selects on exactly that state — `(await db.txn.listByStatus("PROCESSING")).filter(t => Date.parse(t.createdAt) < cutoff)` (line 1228) — runs every 5 minutes (lifecycle.ts:187 `PAYMENT_SWEEP_EVERY_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`), re-queries the provider, gets FAILED again, and calls `settleWithdrawalFailed(t.id, "reconcile-verified-failed")` (line 1305). The guard at line 803 (`t.status !== "PROCESSING"`) is the ONLY idempotency, and it is precisely the thing the first run failed to write, so it passes and the full gross is credited a second time. The window opens two ways, both routine on Railway: (1) the container is SIGTERMed by a redeploy between the two commits; (2) line 807 hits a transient DB error, which prisma-dal.ts:1383 swallows — `if (tx) return run(); try { return await run(); } catch { return null; }` — and line 807's return value is never checked, so the function proceeds to email the player and return truthy while the row was never updated. The function's own doc-comment (lines 789-797) asserts the property it does not have: "Exactly-once under the wallet lock … the idempotency here is what makes a race with the sweep or a late callback safe." The advisory lock only serializes CONCURRENT callers; it does nothing about a second call minutes later against a status that was never written.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (contradicts the function's own stated exactly-once contract at wallet-service.ts:789-797 and the caller's contract at payment-actions.ts:234-236, and defeats §6a's premise that money-out has been systematically passed)
findings.concreteScenario: Player has TZS 500,000 spendable. They withdraw TZS 200,000 (fee 1.5% = TZS 3,000, net TZS 197,000). withdraw() line 1630 commits balance 300,000 / hold 200,000. Selcom refuses the payout; the webhook posts FAILED; settleWithdrawalFailed line 806 commits balance 500,000 / hold 0. Before line 807 commits, the container restarts on a deploy (or line 807's update errors and is swallowed to null). The Transaction row still reads PROCESSING. 30 minutes later the sweep picks it up, verifyWithdrawalStatus returns FAILED, and settleWithdrawalFailed runs again: line 803 sees PROCESSING, line 806 credits TZS 200,000 a SECOND time. Final wallet: balance 700,000, hold -200,000. The player can immediately bet or withdraw TZS 200,000 of the platform's money. And the nightly detector cannot see it: computeTrialBalance uses `const walletReal = w ? w.balance + w.hold : 0` (ledger.ts:767), so walletReal = 700,000 + (-200,000) = 500,000, ledgerReal = 500,000 (no withdrawal ledger group is ever posted on the FAILED path), realDrift = 0, driftingWallets = 0, ok = true.
findings.moneyImpact: The platform loses the full gross of the withdrawal, once per extra sweep pass. TZS 200,000 in the scenario above. It is unbounded rather than one-shot: the sweep re-runs every 5 minutes for as long as the row stays PROCESSING, and this repo has a measured precedent of a single withdrawal sitting in that sweep for 69 hours (wallet-service.ts:1288 — "THE 1,329-ROW SITE. One withdrawal sat here from 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-10 and this line fired on every sweep"). And it is undetectable: the double error cancels in balance+hold, so the trial balance reports ok.

findings.title: The sweep can auto-reverse an AML-approved payout by querying a providerRef that was never sent to any gateway — the payout is in flight and the player gets the money back
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: A withdrawal with gross >= TZS 1,000,000 never reaches a gateway: `dispatchWithdrawal` returns early with `providerRef: correlationId` (payments.ts:209), and `withdraw()` writes that OUR-ONLY id onto the Transaction row (wallet-service.ts:1777-1781) before setting status AML_REVIEW. `result.rail` is undefined on that branch, so `payoutRail` stays NULL. When an officer approves, `dispatchApprovedWithdrawal` flips the row to PROCESSING FIRST (line 736) and only writes the REAL gateway ref afterwards (line 770), with a network round-trip in between (PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 45,000 per rung, up to two rungs in the ladder). That status write is on the plain Prisma client — `db.txn.update(id, patch)` with no `tx` argument resolves to `pc()` (prisma-dal.ts:1365-1366) — so it COMMITS IMMEDIATELY and is visible to every other connection, notwithstanding the enclosing `withLock`. During that window the row is: status PROCESSING, providerRef = a `wdr_…` id Selcom has never seen, payoutRail NULL, createdAt = the original initiation (hours or days old, because the row sat in AML review). `reconcileStalePayments` selects exactly that shape: `Date.parse(t.createdAt) < cutoff` is true, `ref` is non-null so the safe no-ref arm at line 1290 is skipped, and it calls `verifyWithdrawalStatus(ref, null)` → `railOf(null)` = WALLET_CASHIN → GET /walletcashin/query for a transid that endpoint has never heard of. `envelopeSettlementVerdict` returns FAILED for ANY resultcode outside {000, 111, 927, 999}, so the answer is FAILED → `settleWithdrawalFailed(t.id, "reconcile-verified-failed")` refunds the gross and marks the txn FAILED, while the real payout is being accepted by Selcom.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The repo itself states this exact mechanism as a double-pay (selcom.ts:860-868: "Ask /walletcashin/query about a payout that went out on /selcompesa/cashin and you get an envelope for a transaction it has never heard of… falls through envelopeSettlementVerdict to FAILED — and the stale reconcile sweep treats FAILED as 'the payout definitively did not happen' and refunds the player. The money is already gone."). The fix that was applied threaded `payoutRail` so the RIGHT endpoint is asked — but it never addressed the case where the transid ITSELF is a phantom. wallet-service.ts:1291-1293 claims `t.payoutRail` is what stands between the sweep and a wrong refund; on this path the rail is irrelevant because no endpoint on any rail knows the reference. payments.ts:199-208 explicitly says the AML correlation id "is OUR id and is honest about that" — but `withdraw()` still stores it in the `providerRef` column, the one field every downstream consumer treats as a gateway handle, so downstream is exactly as blind as before. Same class if line 770 simply throws (DB blip, or the enclosing aml-txn $transaction has already blown its 30s Prisma timeout while a 45s Selcom call runs): the row then sits PROCESSING with the phantom ref permanently and EVERY 5-minute sweep re-asks and can reverse.
findings.rulesReference: §2.8 — a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and nothing else; the mirror obligation is that the house pays a payout ONCE. Also RULES.md §2.7 (the withdrawal is one charge on one disbursement). No rule sanctions paying a payout twice.
findings.concreteScenario: Player holds TZS 1,000,000 and withdraws all of it. fee = 1.5% = 15,000; net = 985,000; hold = 1,000,000; the row is created at 09:00 on day 1 and goes to AML_REVIEW with providerRef `wdr_9f2c1ab04e` (never sent anywhere). Two officers approve at 14:02:10 on day 2. `db.txn.update(txnId, { status: "PROCESSING" })` commits at 14:02:10; `dispatchWithdrawal` then spends 40s inside /walletcashin/process. The 5-minute payment sweep fires at 14:02:30. It selects the row (createdAt is 29 hours old), sees a non-null ref, asks /walletcashin/query?transid=wdr_9f2c1ab04e, gets a 200 with a not-found resultcode, resolves FAILED, and calls settleWithdrawalFailed: balance +1,000,000, hold −1,000,000, status FAILED, and the player is emailed "Withdrawal returned · TZS 1,000,000". At 14:02:50 Selcom accepts and disburses 985,000 to the player's M-Pesa. When the real callback lands, settlePaymentWebhook sees FAILED + CONFIRMED, logs `webhook.terminal_contradicted`, and deliberately claws nothing back.
findings.moneyImpact: The house loses the full net payout — 985,000 TZS in the example — and the player can immediately withdraw the restored 1,000,000 again. Every AML-approved payout is >= TZS 1,000,000 by construction, so this is the largest-value path on the platform. It repeats once per approval that overlaps a sweep tick; with a ~40-90s dispatch window against a 300s sweep cadence, the exposure is roughly 1 in 4 to 1 in 8 approvals, and it becomes PERMANENT (every sweep, forever) if line 770 fails to commit.

findings.title: settleWithdrawalFailed — the only refund path — is not atomic and its status write fails SILENTLY, so the 5-minute sweep re-refunds the same payout every cycle
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Inside the wallet lock it credits the wallet and then, as a SEPARATE statement, writes status FAILED. Neither call receives the lock's transaction: `db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt })` is called with two arguments and `db.txn.update(txnId, {...})` with two arguments, so both resolve to `pc()` — a different connection from the `$transaction` that `withAdvisoryLock` opened. Both DAL methods in no-tx mode end with `try { return await run(); } catch { return null; }` (prisma-dal.ts:1300 and 1383), so a database failure on either is swallowed to `null`. Neither return value is checked. The function then returns `t` — truthy — so the caller is told the reversal succeeded.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Every sibling settle function on this file was rebuilt for audit C3 to be atomic: `settleDepositConfirmed` wraps its credit + status + ledger in `withMoneyTx` and passes `tx` to every DAL call (lines 468-474), and `settleWithdrawalConfirmed` does the same (lines 615-622) with the stated reason "a ledger failure now rolls the whole thing back… instead of moving the money with no ledger evidence". The REFUND path — the only one that puts money back into a spendable balance — was left on the old self-committing, error-swallowing shape. The locks.ts header claims "Everything inside ONE withLock now shares ONE transaction, so a throw rolls back every write made under the lock" (locks.ts:158-159); that is false for any DAL call that does not receive `tx`, and this function makes no such call. Because `reconcileStalePayments` re-runs every 5 minutes and re-selects any row still in PROCESSING, a wallet credit that lands with a lost status write is not a one-off inconsistency — it is a refund loop.
findings.rulesReference: §2.8 — a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and nothing else; the converse is that a reversal returns the stake once. Also the money-safety contract stated in reconcileStalePayments' own header (wallet-service.ts:1008-1020) that the sweep must never terminalize a payment more than once.
findings.concreteScenario: A payout of TZS 250,000 (fee 3,750; hold 250,000) sits PROCESSING. At 14:05 the sweep verifies FAILED. `db.wallet.adjust` commits: balance +250,000, hold −250,000. The very next statement, `db.txn.update(txnId, { status: "FAILED", … })`, hits a pool-timeout (P2024) or a dropped connection; the DAL catches it and returns null; `settleWithdrawalFailed` returns `t`, the sweep counts `withdrawalsReversed++`, calls `clearNeedsReview`, and emails the player "Withdrawal returned · TZS 250,000". The row is still PROCESSING. At 14:10 the sweep selects it again, verifies FAILED again, and credits another 250,000. At 14:15, another 250,000. A two-hour period of pool pressure = 24 sweeps = 6,000,000 TZS credited into one wallet against a single 250,000 withdrawal.
findings.moneyImpact: House loses N × the gross withdrawal, where N is the number of sweep cycles until the status write succeeds — unbounded and repeating on a 5-minute clock. The wallet balance is real and immediately withdrawable. The only detection is the nightly wallet↔ledger trial balance (lifecycle.ts:87-120), which runs once every 24 hours and only reports drift; it does not stop the loop.

findings.title: Rejecting an RG-held DEPOSIT in /admin/aml moves no money at all, and three surfaces tell the officer the funds were returned
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: rejectAmlAction guards its ENTIRE money-movement block on `if (txn.type === "WITHDRAWAL")`. For a DEPOSIT held in AML_REVIEW (the RG-suspense path is the only producer of such a row) the action skips the wallet adjust at line 167, posts NO ledger entries anywhere, skips the player email at line 187-197, sets the transaction to FAILED with the officer's reason, writes an `aml.rejected` audit row, and returns `{ ok: true }`. The client then renders an unconditional success card.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The approve arm of the SAME file refuses a deposit with the sentence "it awaits a refund. Use Reject to return the funds to the player." (actions.ts:87) — so the code itself routes the officer to the one control that returns nothing. The queue row helper text says "Reject returns the held funds." (page.tsx:164), the in-flight overlay says "Returning funds to player wallet." (aml-actions-client.tsx:74) and the success card says "Funds returned to wallet." (aml-actions-client.tsx:94) — none of them branches on txn.type. FAILED drops the row out of `db.txn.listByStatus("AML_REVIEW")`, which is the ONLY population /admin/aml, /admin/approvals, /admin/compliance and the /admin KPI read, so the last human-facing record that a player is owed money is deleted by the click that claims to have paid them. The HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE credit is untouched and no PLAYER ledger line was ever posted, so every integrity check stays green: each group still sums to zero, and the per-wallet trial balance is exact precisely because nothing was booked on the player side.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.8 (a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and NOTHING ELSE — keeping a deposit is a third charge) and §2.9 (a refusal/outcome must state the truth at a matching severity; here a success card states a payment that did not happen)
findings.concreteScenario: Player P deposits TZS 400,000 by M-Pesa; the row is created PROCESSING. Three minutes later P self-excludes for 6 months. Selcom's confirmation arrives and `settleDepositConfirmed` finds `isLockedOut = true`, so the txn becomes AML_REVIEW with amlReason `rg_refund_due_self_exclusion` and the ledger books EXTERNAL:MPESA −400,000 / HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE +400,000 (wallet-service.ts:441-452). An officer opens /admin/aml, clicks Approve and is told "…Use Reject to return the funds to the player.", then clicks Reject and types "self-excluded, returning deposit". The server takes the WITHDRAWAL branch nowhere: P's wallet stays at 0, no ledger release leg is written, no email is sent. The txn becomes FAILED and vanishes from the queue. The officer's screen reads `Rejected · Funds returned to wallet.` P is out TZS 400,000 and both the officer and the audit trail believe the case is closed.
findings.moneyImpact: The player loses 100% of the deposited amount — TZS 400,000 in the worked case, up to TZS 1,000,000 for a single deposit at the SOF threshold. Repeatable for every player who self-excludes or cools off between deposit initiation and provider confirmation (a 30-minute window on mobile money, and precisely the moment a harm-aware player acts). The platform keeps the cash; HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE reports it as a liability but nothing and nobody is now tracking the individual debt except a raw LedgerEntry row.

findings.title: HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE has exactly one writer and it is always a CREDIT — no code path in the repo can ever release it, yet the player is emailed that the money "has been reversed and returned to the account it came from"
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `rgSuspenseEntries` is the only function in the repo that names `acct.rgSuspense`, and it emits a single positive line (`amount: opts.amount`) against a negative EXTERNAL line. A repo-wide grep for RG_SUSPENSE finds no debit, no release helper, no officer action and no sweep. At the moment the money is parked, `settleDepositConfirmed` fires `notifyDeposit(..., status: "REVERSED")` and `depositReversedHtml`, both of which assert the money went back to the payer, and the email adds a 5-working-day trace SLA.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The code's own comment at wallet-service.ts:433-435 states the truth — the money "can neither be credited (the account is excluded) nor yet returned (that needs the outbound disbursement rail)" — while the message sent in the same execution path tells the player the return already happened. The rail does not exist, so the promise can never be met by any code in this repo; the debt can only grow. This is also the exact shape recorded in MEMORY as "a suspense account holding money for an object that no longer exists balances perfectly": `reconcileLedger` only asks whether each group sums to zero (ledger.ts:645-670) and `computeTrialBalance` only compares PLAYER:<id> against wallet.balance+hold — neither can ever see a growing RG_SUSPENSE. ⛔ AND THE GUARD ASSERTS THE FALSE SENTENCE: `scripts/deposit-notifications.test.mts:212` is `ok("C9 email says the money went back", /returned to the account it came from/i.test(html))` and :204 asserts the in-app body contains "returned". Both would pass unchanged if the refund feature were entirely absent — which it is.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.8 (nothing may be charged to a player beyond the pool fee and the withdrawal fee) and §2.9 (a player-facing message must state what is true, with the next step)
findings.concreteScenario: Same player P, TZS 400,000. At 14:05 the RG arm runs and P receives an email headed "Deposit reversed" containing "The deposit has been reversed and returned to the account it came from." and "If a refund has not reached you within 5 working days, quote the references above and we'll trace it.", plus an in-app notice "It has been returned to where it came from." No disbursement is dispatched now or ever. On day 6 P calls support quoting txn_… and dep_… ; the officer opens /admin/house, sees one aggregate line "Held for a self-excluded player  −400,000" (page.tsx:487) with no per-player breakdown and no control, and /admin/aml either still shows the row or (after MO-5.a) shows nothing at all.
findings.moneyImpact: Every shilling that enters HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE is permanently retained by the platform while the player holds a written promise of a refund with a stated deadline. TZS 400,000 per occurrence in the worked case; unbounded in aggregate because the account is append-only. It is a regulatory exposure as well as a money one — an LCCP/GBT self-exclusion refund that was promised in writing and never made.

findings.title: A payout callback settles the transaction it CORRELATED on using the status of a DIFFERENT transid the caller chose — on an unauthenticated route
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The handler derives TWO independent ids from the request body: `ref = orderId || transid` is used to LOAD our transaction row (line 243 `db.txn.findByProviderRef(ref)`), while the withdrawal branch asks Selcom about `transid || ref` (line 265). When the body carries BOTH `order_id` and `transid`, and they differ, we look up transaction A and settle it with Selcom's verdict about transaction B. The Digest signature IS computed (line 216 `sigOk`) but is never used to gate anything — line 258's own comment says "(sigOk above is captured for audit only.)" — and there is no timestamp-freshness/replay window and no rate limit. The route is not in the proxy's protected set, so any anonymous POST bearing `Authorization: SELCOM x` reaches this function. A FAILED verdict flows to `settlePaymentWebhook` → `settleWithdrawalFailed` (wallet-service.ts:806 `db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt })`), which returns the full gross to spendable balance. The DEPOSIT branch does NOT have this split: `selcomVerifyOrder(env, orderId || ref)` at line 252 always asks about the same string it correlated on.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The whole safety argument of this handler — stated in its own header, "we do not trust the callback body/signature for a payout confirmation either" — is that settlement comes from an authoritative signed re-query rather than the body. But the body still chooses WHICH QUESTION IS ASKED. That is the session-1 body-credit class in a new costume: the attacker no longer supplies the verdict, they supply the id whose verdict is applied. `selcomVerifyPayout`/`envelopeSettlementVerdict` (selcom.ts:877-892, 383-389) never check that the envelope Selcom returns is about the transid we asked for, and never check it is about the transaction we are settling, so nothing downstream catches the substitution. The repo already knows this exact failure shape: line 259-263's comment explains that a query about a foreign transid "returns a stranger's envelope, which resolves to FAILED and refunds a player whose money already left" — and then hands the caller the power to pick that foreign transid. This also bypasses the deliberate reversal discipline: `settleConfirmedWithdrawals` is documented CONFIRM-ONLY and reversals are reserved for the patient 30-minute `reconcileStalePayments`, yet this route will reverse a payout seconds after dispatch on an anonymous request.
findings.rulesReference: docs/RULES.md §2.8 — a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and NOTHING ELSE; this pays a player TWICE at the house's expense, which is the mirror defect. Also the money-safety doctrine stated verbatim at src/lib/server/selcom.ts:857-869 ("the stale reconcile sweep treats FAILED as 'the payout definitively did not happen' and refunds the player. The money is already gone. That is a double payment").
findings.concreteScenario: Player withdraws TZS 1,000,000. §2.7 fee = 15,000, so Selcom is asked to disburse net TZS 985,000. Wallet: balance −1,000,000, hold +1,000,000; txn PROCESSING with providerRef `wdr_9f2c81ab3d`, which the player can read verbatim off their own wallet (`src/app/wallet/wallet-client.tsx:530-535` renders `tx.providerRef` in full under "Gateway reference", and the withdrawal email carries it too). Selcom accepts with `111 INPROGRESS`; the 985,000 lands on the handset minutes later, but the fast payout lane can only CONFIRM and the reconcile sweep does not look for 30 minutes, so the row is still PROCESSING. The player now sends one anonymous request:  POST /api/webhooks/payments, `Authorization: SELCOM x`, body `{"order_id":"wdr_9f2c81ab3d","transid":"wdr_0011deadbe","payment_status":"FAILED"}` — where `wdr_0011deadbe` is the gateway reference of one of their OWN earlier withdrawals that Selcom accepted and then hard-failed (that ref is likewise printed in their wallet history and in the "Withdrawal returned" email, so no guessing is needed). ref = `wdr_9f2c81ab3d` finds the live withdrawal; `selcomVerifyPayout(WALLET_CASHIN, "wdr_0011deadbe")` returns Selcom's genuine hard-fail code for the OLD payout → FAILED → `settleWithdrawalFailed` credits 1,000,000 back to spendable balance and mails "Withdrawal returned · TZS 1,000,000". Net: the player holds 985,000 in M-Pesa AND 1,000,000 on 50pick. Repeat every withdrawal cycle.
findings.moneyImpact: The house loses the full net payout on every cycle — TZS 985,000 per 1,000,000 withdrawal — with no cap and no rate limit. One HTTP request per cycle, self-serve, no credential required. Ten cycles by one player = TZS 9,850,000 gone with the ledger showing ten cleanly 'failed' withdrawals.

findings.title: The tamper-evident audit chain records a levy figure the ledger never booked — two authoritative records of the same statutory liability, disagreeing by construction
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The settlement audit entry writes `levies: settleLevies` — the single levySplit over the whole fee (computed at :3278). The LedgerEntry rows written moments earlier in the same settlement carry the per-winner sum from settlementPayoutEntries. Nothing reconciles the two, and no code path ever compares them.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The audit chain is the HMAC-anchored record an inspector or a disputing player reads, and the docstring immediately above the payload (market-service.ts:3714-3715) says exactly that: "An inspector (or a player who disputes a payout) can recompute the fee from these numbers." The ledger is what the money actually did and what /admin/house, house-ledger.ts and any remittance run off. RULES §2.2 admits one levy figure per fee, not two. Whichever number a remittance is filed from, the other record contradicts it — and the contradiction is silent because both are internally consistent and every aggregate balances.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.2 — one levy base, one figure, enforced in levySplit. Also §6a's own warning that an aggregate which balances is not evidence its components do.
findings.concreteScenario: Same settlement as LEAD-A.1: 60 winning positions of TZS 1,000 vs a TZS 4,000 losing side, fee 520. The `market.resolved` audit row records `levies: { fee: 520, traLevy: 52, gbtLevy: 26, operatorNet: 442 }`. The LedgerEntry rows for the same market total SETTLEMENT_TRA_LEVY 60 and SETTLEMENT_GBT_LEVY 0. An officer opening /admin/house/[marketId] is told the market's leviesBooked is 60 and its netRetained is 460; the chain entry for the identical market says 78 and 442. Both are stamped, both are signed, and neither knows about the other.
findings.moneyImpact: No shilling moves on this line by itself — but it is the reason the LEAD-A.1 shortfall cannot be caught by inspection. A TRA/GBT remittance filed from the ledger under-pays GBT by up to ~450 TZS per settlement and over-pays TRA; a remittance filed from the audit chain matches the rule but will not reconcile against the ledger the auditor is handed. On the worked example the two records differ by 18 TZS on a single 64,000 TZS book, and the difference is per-settlement and cumulative.

findings.title: The config audit's `changes` field is the entire posted form, not a diff — every one of the 19 fields is recorded as "changed" on every save
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: CLAIM 1 IS REAL IN SOURCE at 2499f324, and I counted the fields. `GlobalConfigForm` renders every input with a populated `defaultValue`, so every key posts a NON-EMPTY string. `parseRate`/`parseInteger`/`parseRatio` return `undefined` only for `null` or `""` (actions.ts:22-39), so on a real browser save EVERY parse succeeds and EVERY `if (x !== undefined) updates.x = x` on lines 83-101 fires. Under the live `loser-share` model the form posts exactly 19 keys: commissionRate, feeCeilingRate, cashOutFeeRate, freeExitGraceMinutes, paidExitWindowMinutes, withdrawalFeeRate, withdrawalGatewayShareRate, minStake, maxStake, thinProfitRatio, starterBalanceTzs, objectionWindowHours, traTaxOnCommissionRate, gbtLevyOnCommissionRate, feeModel, platformFeeRate, operatorFeeRate, estimatedWinningsRate, showEstimatedWinnings (the last one force-set by `fd.set("showEstimatedWinnings", …)` in config-form.tsx:65). `updates` is then handed straight to `setGlobalConfig`, which audits it VERBATIM as `changes` (market-config.ts:813). Nothing anywhere diffs `updates` against `store.global` before the audit is written.
findings.whyItIsWrong: `changes` is the name of a diff, and this is a snapshot of the form. A save that moved ONLY the GBT levy and a save that moved NOTHING AT ALL produce byte-identical `changes` objects containing all 19 numbers. The audit's own vocabulary therefore asserts something false 18 times out of 19 on every rate change. The information is not destroyed — `before` and `after` are in the same payload (market-config.ts:813) — but no surface diffs them (see LEAD-B.1b), so the recoverable answer requires a DBA with raw jsonb access. `setGlobalConfig` also does not refuse a no-op: an officer who opens the form and presses Save writes a full audited `config.global.updated` entry naming 19 fields, indistinguishable from a real rate change.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §5 step 6 ("Verify on production by reading the database") and §2.1 — the fee record must answer *which rate applied, and from when*. Also internal inconsistency: `buildIsoAudit`'s regulator hand-off note (src/lib/server/reports/catalogue.ts:568) states "Full payloads are available on /admin/audit", which LEAD-B.1b shows is not true as rendered.
findings.concreteScenario: Live config: platformFeeRate 0.03, operatorFeeRate 0.10 (RULES §1, 13% of the losing side). An officer with `accounting` ACT opens /admin/config, changes ONLY "Operator fee (%)" from 10.0 to 4.0, and saves. `updates` = all 19 fields; the audit row's `changes` reads `{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeilingRate":0.3333…,"cashOutFeeRate":0.1,"freeExitGraceMinutes":5,"paidExitWindowMinutes":0,"withdrawalFeeRate":0.015,…,"platformFeeRate":0.03,"operatorFeeRate":0.04,"estimatedWinningsRate":0.5,"showEstimatedWinnings":true}`. Every new poll created from that moment freezes a 7% loser-share fee into its immutable feeSnapshot instead of 13%. On a poll with YES 1,000,000 / NO 1,000,000 where NO loses, the house takes 70,000 instead of 130,000 — and an auditor asked six weeks later "when did the operator fee move, and who moved it?" has no entry that says operatorFeeRate moved; it says all 19 fields moved, on that save and on every other save in the log.
findings.moneyImpact: The operator/regulator loses the ability to attribute a fee change to a person and a moment. Direct shillings on the worked example: 60,000 TZS of fee per 2,000,000 TZS pool, unattributable. It is not a leak by itself — it is the loss of the control that would DETECT one, on the single screen that can reprice every future poll on the platform. GBT inspection (audit.ts header: "GBT inspection, FIU AML reporting, ISO 27001 A.12.4") is the consumer of this record.

findings.title: Both surfaces that display a config change render the payload `before`-first in a one-line truncated cell, so `after` and `changes` are never on screen at all
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: /admin/audit renders `JSON.stringify(e.payload)` inside `<td className="font-mono text-text-subtle max-w-[360px] truncate">`. `truncate` is single-line ellipsis; there is no expander, no modal, no row-detail route (I grepped the whole page — `payload` appears exactly once). JSON.stringify emits keys in insertion order, and the payload is built `{ before, after, changes, warn }` (market-config.ts:813), so the first thing rendered is the 20-field `before` object. At 360px in a mono face roughly the first 45-55 characters survive — i.e. `{"before":{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeilingRate…`. `after`, `changes` and `warn` are never reached. The /admin/config "Recent changes" tab (page.tsx:370-372) has the mirror-image problem: it renders ONLY `payload.changes` — the 19-field blob from LEAD-B.1a — in the same `max-w-[360px] truncate` cell, and never renders `before`/`after`, so the one place that COULD show a diff shows the field that is not one.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Between the two screens the platform holds all the information needed to say which rate moved and never displays it. This is the fourth row of MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION §3.1 ("The config audit entry is unreadable on /admin/audit") and it is real. It also makes a regulator-facing document untrue: `buildIsoAudit` ships the ISO 27001 hand-off with the note "Full payloads are available on /admin/audit" (catalogue.ts:568), and the report itself carries only id/time/category/action/actor/target/hashes — so the index points at a screen that cannot deliver what the index promises.
findings.rulesReference: none — internal consistency with src/lib/server/reports/catalogue.ts:568 and with audit.ts's stated purpose ("GBT inspection … ISO 27001 A.12.4"). RULES.md §5 step 6 assumes a change can be verified after the fact.
findings.concreteScenario: Same save as LEAD-B.1a (operatorFeeRate 10% → 4%). An inspector opens /admin/audit, filters category=ADMIN, and finds the row: Time 2026-09-09 08:24, Action `config.global.updated`, Actor `usr_a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8`, Target `MarketConfig#global`, Payload `{"before":{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCei…`. That is the complete determinable content. They cannot tell that the operator fee moved, cannot tell it moved to 4%, and cannot tell this row differs in any way from the adjacent row where an officer opened the form and pressed Save without editing anything. Switching to /admin/config → Recent changes shows the same row's Changes column as `{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeilingRate":0.33333…` — again truncated, and again containing all 19 fields whether or not they moved.
findings.moneyImpact: Same 60,000 TZS per 2,000,000 TZS pool as LEAD-B.1a, and the same class of loss: an unauthorised or mistaken rate change on the platform's most consequential screen leaves a record that is present in the database and invisible to every human who would look for it. Combined with LEAD-B.1a the two defects reinforce each other — the field named `changes` is not a diff AND the fields that would let you compute one are off-screen.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/audit/page.tsx:197 — {e.payload ? JSON.stringify(e.payload) : "—"} src/app/admin/config/page.tsx:370-372 — {(e.payload as { changes?: unknown })?.changes ? JSON.stringify((e.payload as { changes: unknown }).changes) : "—"}

findings.title: The config page renders an editable, unlabelled rate form from code defaults on a failed read — and saving it writes the whole snapshot back, silently deleting every per-market stake override with no audit of the deletion
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: CLAIM 2 IS REAL IN SOURCE, but its stated mechanism is the minor half and I want that on the record so nobody 'fixes' only the `.catch`. Line 28 is `const config = await getGlobalConfig().catch(() => DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG);` and line 29 is `const overrides = await listMarketOverrides().catch(() => []);`. That `.catch` is close to unreachable for the case it looks like it handles: `getGlobalConfig` rejects only if something throws OUTSIDE `loadConfig`'s try (a `new PrismaClient()` failure at prisma.ts:88, or `new Map(stored.perMarket ?? [])` on a non-iterable at market-config.ts:518). A transient DB error does NOT reject — LEAD-B.2a shows it RESOLVES with defaults. So the officer reaches the same wrong screen by the non-throwing path, and the `.catch` merely guarantees the throwing path lands there too. Either way: `config` is `DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG`, `overrides` is `[]`, and the page renders the full editable `GlobalConfigForm` with every input pre-filled from those defaults, every hint reading "Current X%", the KPI band reading them as live, and the Overrides tab printing the positive assertion "No active overrides — every market uses the global config." (page.tsx:281-283). There is no hydration-state banner, no provenance on the returned RateConfig, and no visual difference from a healthy render.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The officer is shown numbers that are not live, told they are current, and given a Save button — and Save is not a partial update. `setGlobalConfig` does `store.global = { ...store.global, ...updates }` then `persist()`, which writes `{ global, perMarket: Array.from(store.perMarket.entries()), v: 3 }`. On a de-hydrated process `store.perMarket` is the empty Map from module init, so the write is not merely a re-freeze of code defaults over the officer's global row (RULES §2.3's recorded trap, running once already) — it is a silent DELETE of the entire per-market override table. `clearMarketOverride` is the audited path for removing one override (market-config.ts:833-847, `config.market.cleared`); this path removes all of them and audits nothing but the 19 global fields. Per-market minStake/maxStake are the two overrides actions.ts:136-139 explicitly documents as LIVE and enforced ("read live via getEffectiveConfig(m.id) on the market page and enforced server-side in buyPosition"), and market-service.ts:1123-1130 confirms it.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.3 — the stake window is a rule an operator may NARROW inside 1,000…1,000,000 but never widen; the trap box in that section records this exact `persist()`-writes-the-whole-snapshot mechanism firing once already (a TZS 500 floor re-frozen by an unrelated save on 2026-08-10). Also RULES.md §5 step 6.
findings.concreteScenario: Market mkt_7f3a is a high-volatility poll the operator narrowed with a per-market override {minStake: 10,000, maxStake: 100,000} — legal under §2.3, and the reason actions.ts:136-139 says the override form still exists. A container boots during a DB blip; hydration swallows the error (LEAD-B.2a); `store.perMarket` = empty Map. An officer opens /admin/config, sees the Overrides tab count read 0 and the sentence "No active overrides — every market uses the global config.", shrugs, switches to Rates and saves an unrelated GBT change. `persist()` writes `perMarket: []` to SystemConfig. mkt_7f3a's override is gone from the database permanently, with no `config.market.cleared` audit entry naming it. The very next bet on mkt_7f3a goes through market-service.ts:1123-1130, which now resolves the GLOBAL bounds: a player stakes TZS 1,000,000 on a market the operator had capped at 100,000 — 900,000 TZS of exposure on a single bet that the operator explicitly refused — and another player stakes TZS 1,000 under the operator's 10,000 floor. Both are accepted, both settle, and the only record of the operator's decision is gone.
findings.moneyImpact: 900,000 TZS of unauthorised exposure per bet on every market that carried a narrowed cap, repeatable for every bet until someone notices the overrides vanished — and there is no alert, because the deletion is not audited and the page renders the empty list as a positive statement of fact. The same save also re-freezes code defaults over the officer's live global row (LEAD-B.2a's second consequence). Magnitude depends on whether any per-market override currently exists in production.

findings.title: defineConfig's synchronous getter has no ready-gate and its failed hydration NEVER retries — and define-config.ts was not one of the four hydrations commit 2499f324 repaired
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: CLAIM 3 IS REAL IN SOURCE, and §1.2's fix did NOT close it. I checked the commit: 2499f324 touched market-config.ts, payment-control.ts, updown-config.ts and payment-ops.ts — `git log -- src/lib/server/define-config.ts` shows its last change is 5e6f1ced, well before the money gate. The factory has TWO separate holes. (1) NO GATE AT ALL: line 57 seeds the registry with `{ ...defaults }` synchronously at module evaluation, line 65 fires `void loadConfig(key).then(…)` with nothing to await, and line 74's `get()` is synchronous — so every caller between module evaluation and the Postgres round-trip resolving receives code defaults, and there is no API by which a caller could wait. market-config.ts's `ensureHydrated` cannot be copied here because `get` is sync by contract. (2) NO RETRY, EVER: `hydrated.add(key)` on line 64 runs BEFORE the load, and the load ends in `.catch(() => {})` on line 71 — so a hydration that fails is swallowed, the key is already marked hydrated, and the process serves code defaults for its whole life with no second attempt. That is strictly worse than the pre-fix market-config shape the money gate called a blocker in four other files.
findings.whyItIsWrong: This factory backs six configs: affiliate-config, agent-config, bonus-config, lipa-config, payout-status and proposals-config. A REAL money caller on the settlement path is `accrualContextFor` (affiliate-service.ts:532), which calls `getAgentConfig()` synchronously and threads four money numbers onto the policy — `maxCommissionPct` (the rate clamp, line 424), `capPerRecruitTzs` (line 431), `commissionWindowMonths` (line 432) and `agentWithholdingTaxPct` (line 437). A second real caller is `/admin/agents` page.tsx:97, whose Settings form pre-fills from the same sync getter (agents-client.tsx:165-169) — the identical trap as LEAD-B.2b, on a second screen, and here `set` (line 76-99) has no hydration gate whatsoever: `before = get()` and `saveConfig(key, merged)` writes the WHOLE merged object, so a save taken from a defaults-filled form overwrites every persisted field the officer did not touch.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.10 — agent commission is 10% of levySplit(fee).operatorNet, ceiling 40%, less 5% withholding to HOUSE:TAX; `capPerRecruitTzs` and `commissionWindowMonths` are the operator's tuning inside that rule (§4). Also RULES.md §2.3's standing rule that a code default is not a live setting — restated verbatim in agent-config.ts:139-149 ("THESE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT PRODUCTION RUNS ON UNTIL A ROW EXISTS … Check the live state, not the file").
findings.concreteScenario: An officer has set a per-recruit budget of TZS 200,000 at /admin/agents → Settings, persisted to `SystemConfig["agent.config"].capPerRecruitTzs`. A cold Railway container's first request into the agent module is that officer's GET /admin/agents; page.tsx:97 calls `getAgentConfig()` in the same tick the module kicked off `loadConfig`, so the Settings form pre-fills `capPerRecruitTzs = 0` with the hint "0 = uncapped". The officer, who only came to change withholding from 5% to 4%, saves — and agents-client.tsx posts every field, so `set` merges `capPerRecruitTzs: 0` and `saveConfig` writes it. The budget is now gone from the database. That agent's recruit then holds a TZS 1,000,000 position on a poll with YES 1,000,000 / NO 1,000,000 where NO loses: fee = 13% × 1,000,000 = 130,000; levySplit gives TRA 13,000 + GBT 6,500, operatorNet 110,500; attributableNetFee = (1,000,000 / 2,000,000) × 110,500 = 55,250; gross commission = Math.floor(55,250 × 0.10) = 5,525, net after 5% withholding = 5,249. Uncapped, that repeats with no ceiling — past roughly 37 such settlements the agent has accrued the full 200,000 the operator budgeted, and every shilling after that is money the operator's own setting refused to spend.
findings.moneyImpact: 5,525 TZS of gross commission per 1,000,000 TZS losing position, accruing without limit once the cap is erased, against a budget the operator set and can no longer see. The same mechanism can move `agentWithholdingTaxPct` (money remitted to HOUSE:TAX that is not owed, or owed and not remitted), `maxCommissionPct` (the RULES §2.10 40% ceiling, reverted to the code value) and `commissionWindowMonths` (a bounded window reverted to lifetime). And it can fire in the other direction on the settlement path itself: an accrual that lands inside the hydration window prices at code defaults rather than the officer's row.

findings.title: A config-change audit row is rendered as one JSON.stringify blob truncated to ~41 characters, so the two rates that actually price every poll are unreadable on every console surface
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: setGlobalConfig writes an ADMIN audit entry whose payload is the FULL before-config, the FULL after-config and the FULL changes object (market-config.ts:813 — `payload: { before, after: store.global, changes: updates, warn: v.warn ?? null }`). /admin/audit renders that entire object with a single `JSON.stringify` into a `<td>` carrying `max-w-[360px] truncate` — one unwrapped line, overflow hidden, ellipsis. There is no `title` attribute, no expand control, no row detail route, and `getAuditById` (audit.ts:487) has ZERO callers anywhere in src. The only other renderer, /admin/config -> History, shows only `changes` and truncates it the same way at 11px (config/page.tsx:370-371). The third surface, /admin/house/[marketId], deliberately refuses to render the payload at all and prints only yes/no from a regex.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Measured on the real payload shape (23 RateConfig fields x before + after + changes): JSON.stringify is 1,630 characters. `platformFeeRate` first occurs at index 474, its post-change value at index 1,035, and inside `changes` at 1,516. `operatorFeeRate` at 497 / 1,058 / 1,539. The cell shows the first ~41 characters at 13px mono in a 324px content box: `{"before":{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeili`. On /admin/config -> History the string is `changes` alone, 470 characters with `platformFeeRate` at index 369 and ~47 characters visible: `{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeilingRate":0.333,"c`. The only two fields an officer can see are `commissionRate` and `feeCeilingRate` — the RETIRED capped-commission knobs that DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG itself labels 'LEGACY FIELDS ... legacy arm only'. The two numbers the live loser-share model charges are structurally out of reach. RULES §5 makes a rate change a seven-step traceable act; step 6 is 'verify by looking at the screen', and the screen cannot show it. Worse, the ISO 27001 regulator hand-off explicitly points its reader here: catalogue.ts:570 prints the note 'Full payloads are available on /admin/audit' while that report's own columns carry no payload at all.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §5 (how to change a rule — the seven-step traceable process) and §2.1 ('Configured in SystemConfig["market.config"].global — feeModel, platformFeeRate, operatorFeeRate, editable at /admin/config'), whose whole point is that a rate change is attributable
findings.concreteScenario: An accounting officer opens /admin/config and raises platformFeeRate 3.0 -> 5.0 and operatorFeeRate 10.0 -> 20.0. validate() permits it (MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE = 1.0 at payout.ts:183, and the winner-floor sweep can never object under loser-share because netPool = winningPool + losingPool*(1-rate) >= winningPool). Every poll created afterwards freezes 25%. On the very next poll — Player A stakes TZS 100,000 on YES, Player B stakes TZS 50,000 on NO, YES wins — the fee is 0.25 x 50,000 = TZS 12,500 instead of 0.13 x 50,000 = TZS 6,500, and A is paid TZS 137,500 instead of TZS 143,500. An officer then investigating 'who changed the fee rate and to what' opens /admin/audit, finds the `config.global.updated` row, and reads exactly: time, `config.global.updated`, the first 16 characters of the actor id, `MarketConfig#global`, and the payload cell `{"before":{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeili`. On /admin/config -> History the Changes cell reads `{"commissionRate":0.1,"feeCeilingRate":0.333,"c`. Neither 0.03->0.05 nor 0.10->0.20 appears on any screen in the console, and the ISO export that promises 'full payloads' carries none.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings move as a direct result — the loss is attribution. In the scenario above TZS 6,000 per settlement of that shape is transferred from players to the house on a rate nobody can be shown to have set. The data IS persisted (AuditLog.payload, audit.ts:201 canonicalize + 271/526/591 select payload), so the record exists; it is the only reading surface that fails, which is the worse failure mode because 'the chain is intact' is simultaneously asserted on the same page.

findings.title: /admin/audit — the only surface that renders any payload, and the one the regulator export names — reads the in-process ring, which starts EMPTY on every process start, while its own 'Chain integrity: Valid' tile is green over zero entries
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The page's single source is `getAuditPage({ limit: 100_000 })`, which reads `ring` — `const ring: AuditEntry[] = globalThis.__50PICK_AUDIT_RING ?? (globalThis.__50PICK_AUDIT_RING = []);` (audit.ts:85). Nothing rehydrates it from AuditLog at boot. audit.ts states the consequence itself, twice, in its own words. /admin/config -> History reads the same ring (config/page.tsx:48). The durable readers that DO exist — `getAuditPageDurable` (audit.ts:507) and `getAuditForTargetDurable` (audit.ts:568) — are not used by either page. The page's 'Chain integrity' KPI calls the synchronous `verifyChain()` (audit.ts:689), whose loop is `for (let i = 0; i < ring.length; i++)`: on an empty ring it never executes and returns `{ valid: true }`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: A rate change is only investigable while the container that served the save is still running and has not evicted the row. After any deploy, restart, or scale event the page shows 'Total entries: 0' and 'No audit entries match this filter' — and beside it 'Chain integrity: Valid · HMAC-chained', because verifying an empty array succeeds. That is the exact failure audit.ts:552 warns against in prose ('an officer reading a blank history concludes nothing happened') while the audit page continues to do it. Applying the standard test — would this KPI still pass if the feature were absent? — yes: it passes with zero entries and would pass if audit writing were removed entirely. Compounding LEAD-C.1: on a multi-container deployment the officer must also be routed to the same instance that wrote the row.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §5 step 6 ('Verify on production by reading the database and by looking at the screen') and §2.1's 'Every set/clear is HMAC-audited so the GBT inspector trail is intact' (market-config.ts:22)
findings.concreteScenario: An officer saves platformFeeRate 3% -> 5% / operatorFeeRate 10% -> 20% on Monday; the same TZS 100,000-vs-TZS 50,000 poll then settles at a 25% fee, moving TZS 6,000 off the winner. A deploy ships Tuesday. On Wednesday a compliance officer opens /admin/audit to answer 'who moved the fee rate' and sees: Total entries 0, Last 24h 0 'no activity', Chain integrity **Valid**, and the empty state 'No audit entries match this filter — Try clearing the actor or category filter to see the full chain.' The row is sitting in AuditLog on the database, unreadable from any screen. The ISO 27001 export he generates instead prints eight columns with no payload and the note 'Full payloads are available on /admin/audit'.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings move. The loss is that a rate change worth TZS 6,000 per settlement of the shape above becomes unattributable through the console the moment the container recycles, while the page simultaneously certifies the chain as intact — a green instrument over an empty population.

findings.title: settleMarket's final totals are read on the global Prisma client while every payout is still uncommitted inside the lock's transaction — the append-only chain and the officer's screen both record '0 positions settled, TZS 0 paid'
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `withLock('market:<id>')` opens ONE `db.$transaction` and publishes its `tx` (locks.ts:126-141), and `withMoneyTx` JOINS it rather than opening its own (ledger.ts:57-59: `const joined = currentLockTx(); if (joined) return fn(joined);`). So every winner credit, every `positionStore.set(p, tx)`, every BET_PAYOUT row and every ledger group written in the settlement loop stays UNCOMMITTED until the whole withLock callback returns. The loss path likewise uses `positionStore.set(p, lockTx ?? undefined)`. Then, still inside that callback, the L2 totals block calls `listPositionsForMarket(m.id)` -> `positionStore.listForMarket(marketId)`, whose Prisma implementation is `const rows = await pc().position.findMany({ where: { marketId } });` (market-dal.ts:1194-1196) — `pc()` is the top-level PrismaClient (market-dal.ts:814-818), a different pooled connection with no access to the open transaction. `listForMarket` does not even accept a `tx` parameter (interface, market-dal.ts:432).
findings.whyItIsWrong: PostgreSQL has no READ UNCOMMITTED; a query on another connection cannot see the in-flight transaction's writes. Every position the loop just marked WIN/LOSS still reads `status: 'OPEN'` with the pre-settlement `finalPayout`, so `totalWinnersPaid` sums nothing and `totalPositionsSettled` counts nothing. The comment directly above claims the opposite — 'Σ(finalPayout WHERE WIN) and the non-OPEN count are correct whether this is the first run or a re-entry. This is the number a regulator reconciles' — and that sentence is false on the production DAL. It is invisible to the suites because they run on the in-memory store (`process.env.USE_PRISMA_DAL = "false"` / no DATABASE_URL), where `memoryPositions.set(p, _tx)` IGNORES the tx and stores the SAME object by reference (market-dal.ts:644), so `listForMarket` returns the already-mutated objects. two-admin-policy.test.mts:92 asserts `winnersPaid === 2700` and concurrency.test.mts:160 asserts `delta === winnersPaid` — both would still pass with this defect fully present, because they can never reach the code path that has it. Note the read 400 lines earlier (`const allMarketPositions = await listPositionsForMarket(m.id);`, line 3289) is correct precisely because it runs BEFORE any write in this scope.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (the function's own L2 comment and the officer-facing confirmation string); it also undermines RULES.md §2.1's 'Guarded by' + §6a's insistence that a settlement's record be reconcilable
findings.concreteScenario: Long-form poll frozen at loser-share 13%. Player A stakes TZS 10,000 on YES; Player B stakes TZS 3,000 on NO. YES wins. losingPool = 3,000, fee = 0.13 x 3,000 = TZS 390, netPool = 13,000 - 390 = TZS 12,610. A is credited TZS 12,610 and B loses TZS 3,000 — the money genuinely moves. Both positions are marked inside the lock's transaction. The totals block then queries on the global client and sees two OPEN rows with finalPayout null, so totalWinnersPaid = 0 and totalPositionsSettled = 0. The permanent HMAC-chained record therefore reads `market.resolved { fee: 390, netPool: 12610, winningPool: 10000, winnersPaid: 0 }` and `market.settled { winnersPaid: 0, positionsSettled: 0, grossPool: 13000 }` — a settlement that states it paid TZS 0 out of a TZS 12,610 net pool. If the officer used the Settle-now button, settleMarketAction returns and displays `0 positions settled · TZS 0 paid to winners` to the person who just released TZS 12,610. AuditLog is append-only and hash-chained, so the false zeros can never be corrected, only out-lived.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings are misdirected — no consumer treats these totals as money. `market-scheduler.ts:265` uses only `r.ok`; `updown-service.ts:966` uses only `s.ok`. The damage is that every settlement writes a false money statement into the 7-year AML record and hands the settling officer a false confirmation: on the shape above, TZS 12,610 paid is recorded as TZS 0. On a resumed settlement it is worse than zero — it silently reports only the PREVIOUS committed run's figures, which reads as a complete total.
