findings.title: The loser-share fee has no rule-level ceiling: /admin/config saves any platformFeeRate + operatorFeeRate up to and including 100% of the losing pool, with no refusal and no warning
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: validate() bounds each loser-share slice, and their sum, by MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE. That constant is 1.0 (payout.ts:183), so the door's only ceiling on the house's share of the losing pool is 100%. platformFeeRate=0.5 with operatorFeeRate=0.5 clears every branch: each field passes `> MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE` (0.5 <= 1.0), the sum check passes (1.0 > 1.0 is false), the winner-floor guardrail returns exactly 1.000 so `worst.ratio < 1` is false, and the only `warn` branch reads `feeCeilingRate` (still 1/3) so no warning is emitted. setGlobalConfig returns `{ ok: true }` with `warn` undefined and config-form.tsx shows a green success toast. The form itself offers `max="100"` on both inputs (config-form.tsx:281,284), so 50/50 is typeable with no client objection either.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES.md §1 makes the fee a RULE — 13% of the losing side, Platform 3% + Operator 10% — and §5 says only Ali changes a rule, in writing, recorded in COMPLIANCE-DECISIONS.md. §4 lists what an operator may tune and the fee rate is NOT on that list. The repo already applies exactly this standard one screen over: minStake/maxStake are refused outside 1,000…1,000,000 with the reason "the platform minimum is a rule, not a setting" (market-config.ts:659-668), and payout.ts:146-165 records that production had in fact been configured out of its own published TZS 1,000 floor for two and a half weeks. The fee rule has no equivalent door. The `MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE` name reads like the protection MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION.md §2 cited it as ("not reachable: validate refuses a save where the two slices sum above MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE") — that statement is factually true and completely unprotective, because the bound is the whole losing pool.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §1 (fee = 13% of the LOSING side, Platform 3% + Operator 10%, both games) · §4 (the fee rate is not among the settings an operator may tune) · §5 (only Ali changes a rule) · §2.8 (a player is charged the pool fee and the withdrawal fee and NOTHING ELSE)
findings.concreteScenario: An officer holding `accounting` ACT opens /admin/config with feeModel = loser-share and types Platform fee 50.0, Operator fee 50.0. The save is accepted with a green toast and no warn. A new poll is created and freezes that snapshot. Aisha stakes TZS 100,000 on YES; Baraka stakes TZS 100,000 on NO. YES wins. poolFee(100000, 100000, snapshot, "YES") → loserRate = clamp(0.5+0.5, 0, 1.0) = 1.0, losingPool = 100,000, fee = 100,000, netPool = 100,000. settledPayoutFor pays Aisha round((100,000/100,000) × 100,000) = TZS 100,000 — her stake back, profit TZS 0. assertWinnerFloor(100000, 100000) passes because payout is not < stake. Under RULES §1 the fee is 13,000, netPool 187,000, and Aisha is paid TZS 187,000. (I verified the arithmetic numerically over the whole savable rate space: the guardrail minimum is exactly 1.000, never below.)
findings.moneyImpact: The winners lose, not the losers. The loser forfeits 100,000 either way — that is the game. The extra fee comes straight out of the prize the winners are paid from, so Aisha is short TZS 87,000 on a correct call and the house books TZS 100,000 where the rule permits TZS 13,000 — TZS 87,000 over the rule on this single 200,000 pool. It repeats on every market created while that config stands, on both products (updown-config.ts:1047 and :1100 validate chain rateProfiles through the same validateRateConfig), and each market's feeSnapshot freezes it for ever (RULES §2.1: a snapshot is never rewritten).

findings.title: The one warning that encodes "the house takes more than all the winners put together" is computed on feeCeilingRate — a knob loser-share never reads — so under the live model it is silent when true and fires when false
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The only `warn` validate() can ever return is gated on `k`, which is `updates.feeCeilingRate ?? store.global.feeCeilingRate`. Under feeModel = "loser-share", poolFee's loser-share arm (payout.ts:476-489) never reads feeCeilingRate at all — it reads only platformFeeRate + operatorFeeRate. So the warning's trigger and the live model's actual house share are wired to two different numbers.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The warning's own text states the exact semantic that matters under loser-share: above one half, "the house takes more than all the winners put together". Under loser-share that condition is precisely `platformFeeRate + operatorFeeRate > 0.5` — the house takes rate × losingPool while all winners' combined profit is (1 − rate) × losingPool. Nothing computes it. This is the same class RULES §2.1 records twice already: the thin-poll alert firing on `closeFee.capped` (a capped-commission concept that loser-share returns `false` for, always), and the simulator's "never exceeds 33.3%" hint quoting feeCeilingRate. A third instance of the same knob is still live in validate(), on the save path itself.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.1 ("THAT ALERT WAS SILENT FOR THREE WEEKS AND NOBODY COULD TELL… `capped` is a capped-commission concept" and the /admin/config simulator entry: "quoting `feeCeilingRate`, which `loser-share` never reads")
findings.concreteScenario: SILENT WHEN TRUE: the officer types Platform 30.0, Operator 30.0. Sum 0.60 <= 1.0, saves clean. On a poll where Aisha stakes TZS 100,000 on YES and Baraka TZS 100,000 on NO, YES wins: fee = 0.60 × 100,000 = TZS 60,000, Aisha is paid TZS 140,000 (profit 40,000). The house has taken 60,000 while every winner's profit combined is 40,000 — the warning's exact condition — and `k` is still 1/3, so `0.3333 > 0.50` is false and no warning is emitted. FIRES WHEN FALSE: the same officer, still on loser-share, types Fee ceiling 80.0. `0.8 > 0.5` is true, so the toast reads "Fee ceiling is 80% of the smaller side… the house takes more than all the winners put together" — about a field poolFee's loser-share arm never reads, on a platform still charging 13%. The audit row records `warn` accordingly (market-config.ts:813), so the trail says an officer was warned when nothing was wrong and says nothing when 60% was saved.
findings.moneyImpact: At 60% on that 200,000 pool the winner is short TZS 47,000 against the rule's 187,000, and the officer who made the change receives no signal at all — the toast is a plain green success. The inverse case trains officers to discount the warning, because the one time it does fire it is about an inert number.

findings.title: The solvency line omits HOUSE:TAX, so unremitted VAT and withholding tax are presented to the owner as his own free cash
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `housePosition` builds the liabilities it subtracts from custodial cash as `owedToOthers = leviesPayable + aggregator + rgSuspense`. `leviesPayable` is only `HOUSE:TRA_LEVY + HOUSE:GBT_LEVY`. `HOUSE:TAX` — which is credited live by two writers (18% VAT on every reconciled agent registration fee, and 5% withholding on every agent commission accrual) — appears in `accounts.all` and is rendered in the accounts table, but is never subtracted from `freeHouseCash` or `freeHouseCashExAdjustments`. The registration-fee group debits `EXTERNAL:SELCOM` by the FULL gross, so `readCustodialCash().railBacked` rises by the whole 118,000 including the VAT leg; the withholding group leaves cash untouched but raises player liability by only the NET, so the withheld tax stays inside the free-cash figure.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.10 makes the 5% withholding and the registration VAT money owed to the state — the same category as the TRA and GBT levies, which ARE subtracted, and which this file's own header calls 'balances we HOLD AND OWE … They reduce free cash'. The function's docstring states its whole purpose: 'A platform holding 100M of which 92M is player balances and 3M is unremitted levies has 5M, and an owner shown "100M" makes decisions that insolvency is built from. Every claim on the cash is subtracted here, explicitly.' HOUSE:TAX is a claim on the cash and it is not subtracted. No guard catches it: the only guard that names the account, `scripts/house-book.test.mts` §3c.4, asserts `Object.keys(housePosition({… all: { "HOUSE:COMMISSION": 1, "HOUSE:TAX": 42 }}) && { ok: 1 }).length === 1` — a tautology over the literal `{ ok: 1 }` that passes whether HOUSE:TAX is present, absent or renamed, and says nothing about the solvency arithmetic.
findings.rulesReference: RULES §2.10 (Withholding: 5% of gross commission 'remitted to HOUSE:TAX'; Registration fee: 'posts to HOUSE:AGENT_FEE (net) + HOUSE:TAX (VAT)') and §2.2 (levies are the platform's liability to the state, never the player's)
findings.concreteScenario: Live config (DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG): rate 10%, withholding 5%, fee 100,000 EXCLUSIVE + 18% VAT = 118,000. (a) Ten applicants are reconciled by an officer: `reconcileFee` posts EXTERNAL:SELCOM −118,000 / HOUSE:AGENT_FEE +100,000 / HOUSE:TAX +18,000 each. Custodial cash rises 1,180,000; HOUSE:TAX holds 180,000; nothing is subtracted. (b) One hundred commission accruals on markets with YES 1,000,000 / NO 1,000,000 (every bet inside the 1,000…1,000,000 bound), NO losing: fee = 13% × 1,000,000 = 130,000; levySplit → TRA 13,000, GBT 6,500, operatorNet 110,500; the agent's grossCut = floor(110,500 × 0.10) = 11,050; withholding = round(11,050 × 0.05) = 553; net credited 10,497. Player liability rises 1,049,700 and is subtracted; HOUSE:TAX gains 55,300 and is not. The 'Strict free cash' and 'Funded free cash' tiles, and the 'Free house cash — strict' line in the derivation table, therefore read 235,300 shillings HIGHER than the money the owner actually owns.
findings.moneyImpact: The owner's solvency line is overstated by the whole HOUSE:TAX balance — 235,300 TZS on the book above, and it grows without bound and never self-corrects, because nothing in the repo ever debits HOUSE:TAX except a registration-fee refund. The overstatement is exactly the money owed to TRA, on the figure the owner uses to decide what he can take out of the business.

findings.title: HOUSE:TAX is captioned "RETIRED — historical rows only" on both owner money screens while two live paths credit it, and no report in the repo reads the account at all
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Both owner-facing money screens carry a caption map that describes `HOUSE:TAX` as retired. `/admin/house` renders it in the 'What it holds' column of the House accounts table for every non-zero `HOUSE:%` account; `/admin/finance` renders it as the `hint` on the account's Stat tile. Meanwhile `agentCommissionEntries` (ledger.ts:584) and `agentRegistrationFeeEntries` (ledger.ts:624) credit that exact account on every accrual and every reconciled registration fee, called from `affiliate-service.ts:1312 → creditWallet → wallet-service.ts:1922` and `agent-application-service.ts:745`. A repo-wide grep for `HOUSE:TAX` / `acct.tax` finds exactly two writers and ZERO readers — no statutory pack, no report builder, no admin figure consumes the balance.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.10 states the withholding is 'deducted at accrual and remitted to HOUSE:TAX' and that the registration fee 'posts to HOUSE:AGENT_FEE (net) + HOUSE:TAX (VAT)'. A caption that tells the reader the account is historical is a false statement about live money on the two screens where the owner and the compliance officer read the books, and it is the only place either screen says anything about that balance. Compounded: because nothing reads HOUSE:TAX, the caption is the only signal that exists, and it points the wrong way. `agent-application-service.ts:139` even calls it 'the one account the statutory pack is read from' — the statutory pack does not read it.

findings.title: The statutory TRA/GBT figure is levied on window GGR instead of on the booked fee, so it charges the whole pool as tax in the window the bets are placed and zero in the window they settle
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `/admin/finance` computes `taxAccrued = Math.round(Math.max(0, ggr) * (traTaxOnCommissionRate + gbtLevyOnCommissionRate))` and renders it as the KPI 'Statutory levies' with the delta caption 'TRA + GBT on commission'. `buildDailyOps` does the same thing for the Daily Operations Report: `traTax = Math.round(Math.max(0, ggr) * TRA_RATE)`, `gbtLevy = Math.round(Math.max(0, ggr) * GBT_RATE)`, then publishes `netAfterTax = ggr - traTax - gbtLevy` as 'Net after tax'. `ggr` comes from `report-money.ts:155` — `stakes - payouts - refunds` over transactions whose `createdAt` falls in the window. The ledger, by contrast, books the levies in `settlementPayoutEntries`/`cashoutEntries` as `Math.round(commAmt * rate)` on the COMMISSION, i.e. `levySplit(fee)`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §1 and §2.2: 'TRA 10% + GBT 5% of the fee we earned'. GGR only equals the fee when the stake and the settlement fall inside the same window; for any long-form poll they do not. The clamp `Math.max(0, ggr)` makes the error one-directional — the stake window is charged tax on the whole handle and the settlement window (whose GGR is negative) is charged nothing — so the two windows never net out. The code comment beside it asserts the opposite: 'GGR = stakes − payouts − refunds = the operator's commission (what we KEEP) … This is the same commission base the ledger levies TRA/GBT on (levySplit) — report and ledger now agree.' They do not agree across a window boundary.
findings.rulesReference: RULES §1 (Tax on our fee: TRA 10% + GBT 5% of the fee we earned) and §2.2 (levies on OUR fee only)
findings.concreteScenario: A long-form poll takes 20 bets of TZS 100,000 in week 1 — YES 1,000,000 / NO 1,000,000, every bet inside the 1,000…1,000,000 bound — and settles in week 3 with NO losing. Week 1, default 7d window: GGR = 2,000,000 − 0 − 0 = 2,000,000, so the 'Statutory levies' tile reads round(2,000,000 × 0.15) = TZS 300,000 while HOUSE:TRA_LEVY and HOUSE:GBT_LEVY moved by 0. Same day on the Daily Operations Report: TRA 200,000, GBT 100,000, 'Net after tax' 1,700,000. Week 3: fee = 13% × 1,000,000 = 130,000, ledger books TRA 13,000 + GBT 6,500 = 19,500 — but that window's GGR = 0 − 1,870,000 = −1,870,000, clamped to 0, so the tile and the report read TZS 0 of statutory levy in the very window the liability was actually incurred.
findings.moneyImpact: On this single poll the two surfaces state a TRA+GBT liability of 300,000 TZS against a real, booked liability of 19,500 TZS — a 280,500 TZS overstatement that never reverses. If the Daily Operations figures are what is remitted, the owner overpays the state by ~15% of turnover instead of ~1.95% of it; if they are used to reconcile against the ledger, the two can never be made to agree and the disagreement is invisible because both numbers look plausible.

findings.title: Two of the three terms in `trialBalance().ok` cannot fail by construction, so the ONLY live money invariant is the per-wallet PLAYER check — escrow (`POOL:*`) and every `HOUSE:*` account are unchecked by anything scheduled
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `ok = drift.length === 0 && globalBalanced && input.imbalancedGroups.length === 0`. `imbalancedGroups` comes from `reconcileLedger()` (:654-659), a `GROUP BY "groupId" HAVING ABS(SUM(amount)) > 0.005`. `globalSum` is `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM "LedgerEntry"` (:839). `drift` is the per-user comparison of `walletReal = w.balance + w.hold` against `Σ PLAYER:{userId}`, plus bonus and grant (:764-780).
findings.whyItIsWrong: The discriminating question, applied: would this still pass if a whole category of entries were wrong or missing? YES, for anything that does not touch a PLAYER account. `postLedgerEntries` REFUSES to insert an imbalanced group — ledger.ts:100-108, throwing inside a money tx and auditing `ledger.imbalanced_rejected` otherwise — so every group in the table sums to zero by construction, and therefore the global sum is zero by construction too. `globalBalanced` and `imbalancedGroups.length === 0` are entailed by the writer for everything the application path produces. `ok` reduces to the per-wallet PLAYER check alone. What that leaves with NO scheduled check anywhere: (a) `POOL:{marketId}` escrow — a settled market's pool must close at exactly zero, and the platform has already shipped a defect where it did not; (b) every `HOUSE:*` account — COMMISSION, TRA_LEVY, GBT_LEVY, AGGREGATOR, AGENT_COMMISSION, TAX, RG_SUSPENSE — a wrong levy split, a wrong agent commission, or a wrong withholding balances perfectly and passes; (c) `HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE`, which ledger.ts:182-188 itself says "must not sit invisible — a non-zero balance here is money we owe a player", surfaced only on /admin/house:487 and watched by nothing. `test:pool-residual` is the one suite that asserts the COMPONENT rather than the aggregate — and it sets `DATABASE_URL = ""` (pool-residual.test.mts:29-30), so it is a pure-function proof of `allocateFeeShares` that can never observe the real books; it is also absent from `predeploy` (grep count 0 on package.json:218).
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency. Directly relevant to RULES §1 (fee = 13% of the losing side, Platform 3% + Operator 10%) and §2.2 (TRA 10% + GBT 5% on OUR fee only): an error in either split is invisible to every scheduled check, because it lives entirely between HOUSE accounts.
findings.concreteScenario: A market settles with two winners staking TZS 3,000 and TZS 5,000 into an 8,000 winning pool against a fee of TZS 260 — all inside the §2.3 bounds. Each winner's settlement is its own balanced group (`settlementPayoutEntries`, ledger.ts:374-394): POOL −(payout+commission), PLAYER +payout, HOUSE:COMMISSION +commission less TRA/GBT. If the per-winner commission shares are derived independently they come to 98 + 163 = 261 against a fee of 260. Every group still sums to zero. Every wallet still matches the ledger exactly (payouts are largest-remainder and exact). `globalSum` is still 0. `imbalancedGroups` is still empty. `trialBalance().ok === true`, and lifecycle.ts:94 prints "books balanced". The escrow account closes at TZS −1 — the platform has paid out one shilling nobody staked — and no production job can see it. This is not hypothetical: scripts/pool-residual.test.mts:9-20 records `POOL:mkt_85f1bae30206db0995a5` closing at −1 on production 2026-08-11, with 9 settled pools non-zero and 7 negative, and states plainly that test:trial-balance (18), test:money-invariants (84), test:ledger (89) and test:payout-alloc (12) were ALL GREEN on both sides of the defect. The same blindness ate TZS 2,000 of escrow for a market that no longer existed on 2026-08-28, plus three pre-existing orphaned POOL:* accounts nobody had noticed (chain-purge.ts:19-25), while "house-money.cjs STILL PRINTED 'the books balance'".
findings.moneyImpact: Per-settlement leakage of the rounding residual (−1 TZS observed, net −6 TZS across 7 pools) plus arbitrarily large orphaned escrow (TZS 2,000 observed for one deleted market). More important than the observed amounts: the CLASS of error — anything wrong between POOL and HOUSE, or between HOUSE accounts, including a wrong TRA/GBT split under RULES §2.2 or a wrong agent withholding under §2.10 — is structurally undetectable by any scheduled job. Both of the amounts above were found by hand, after the fact, by someone who went looking.

findings.title: The live in-app assistant's system prompt states a DIFFERENT and wrong narrowing rule for cash-out — "Selling also closes the moment betting closes" instead of the runway rule — so it will tell a late bettor they still have a free cancellation
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The system prompt that the production chatbot answers every player from teaches: "- Early cash-out (sell position): FREE for 5 minutes after placing the bet (full refund). After that the position LOCKS and rides to settlement — there is no paid exit window and no fee, because there is nothing to sell. Selling also closes the moment betting closes." It states the WINDOW condition and then a closing rule that is NOT the runway rule: it says the sell right shrinks to whatever betting time is left, rather than vanishing entirely when the bet had under 5 minutes of betting time ahead of it.
findings.whyItIsWrong: `hadRunway` is a binary gate evaluated at bet time (market-service.ts:2688), not a truncation of the window. The prompt's rule and the server's rule diverge for exactly the population the runway rule exists to protect: last-moment bets. Under the prompt, a bet placed 2 minutes before close gets 2 minutes of free cancellation; under the server it gets none at all (`reason: "TOO_SHORT"`). market-service.ts's own docstring at line 2655 states the opposite of the prompt: "Bet 2 minutes before a poll closes (or on a 3-minute poll) and you get NO cash-out at all: you took a last-moment position, you ride it." The prompt also omits the NOT-BONUS-FUNDED condition. RULES §2.6 requires anyone quoting the 5-minute cancellation to say which product and which round length; the prompt names neither, and it is the one surface that answers on demand, in whichever of the three languages the player asks in.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.6 (all three conditions; "Anyone quoting the 5-minute cancellation to a player, an auditor or the Board must say which product and which round length") and §2.9 (a player-facing statement must be true at a matching severity)
findings.concreteScenario: A player stakes TZS 300,000 YES on a long-form poll that closes in 3 minutes. He opens the chat widget and asks "can I cancel this bet?". The assistant, following line 129, answers "Yes — free for 5 minutes after placing, and selling closes when betting closes, so you have about 3 minutes." He waits 90 seconds, changes his mind, and hits Sell. `hadRunway = graceMs(300,000) > 0 && closesAt - placedAt (180,000) >= 300,000` is FALSE, `sellable` is false, `reason` = "TOO_SHORT", no Sell control ever renders. He rides to settlement and loses TZS 300,000 that the platform's own assistant told him, 90 seconds earlier, he could take back in full.
findings.moneyImpact: Per incident, up to TZS 1,000,000 (the per-bet maximum) that the player was told, on demand and in writing, was recoverable. Repeatable for every player who asks the assistant about cash-out on a short or ending-soon market — which is precisely the population that asks. The prompt is also the surface RULES/rate-copy already record as "the worst miss of the whole sweep" for exactly this class of error (rate-copy.test.mts:233-237).

findings.title: scripts/rate-copy.test.mts PINS 13% and 1.5% as required literals in the terms and the chat prompt — so RULES §7's "the table is EMPTY, and that is the goal state" is false: there are at least eight live duplicates the guard actively protects, and §4 of the guard cannot see it
findings.functionName: §3 · the two surfaces that state the rule in prose
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: §3 reads the two files and asserts the rate literals must be PRESENT, not absent. 3.2 requires "13%" to appear at least three times in the terms page; 3.3 requires "1.5%" at least three times; 3.6 requires the exact strings "13% OF THE LOSING SIDE" and "1.5% fee" in the chat prompt. Only 3.1 (the retired ceiling) and 3.4/3.5 are refusals. The pinned literals really are inline duplicates: src/app/legal/terms/page.tsx states 13% at lines 98, 223, 342 and 1.5% at lines 134, 260, 370; chat.ts states them at lines 121 and 128. The same file also hardcodes "5 minutes" ×3 (lines 120, 246, 359) and chat.ts hardcodes the stake bounds ("TZS 1,000 and the maximum is TZS 1,000,000", line 120), the deposit bounds ("Min TZS 500, max TZS 2,000,000", line 125) and the AML threshold (line 128). §4 of the guard only asserts that §7 exists and no longer says the guard is unwritten — it never compares the table against reality: `ok("4.2 · ★ …and it no longer says the guard is unwritten", !/is \*\*workstream F5 and is not yet written\*\*/.test(rules), "");`. That check passes identically whether the table lists every duplicate or none.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES.md's own header says "⛔ Do not restate a rate anywhere else. A number written twice is a number that will disagree with itself. Copy that must show a rate reads it from config; copy that cannot is listed in §7 as a known duplicate, with its file and line." §7 defines its own scope as "Every entry here is a number this file also states" — 13%, 1.5% and 5 minutes are all numbers RULES.md states. So by §7's own definition those literals belong in the table, and RULES.md:567 ("The table is EMPTY, and that is the goal state — not an oversight") and RULES.md:600 ("_(none — every rate found by the sweep was made data-driven instead)_") are both false statements in the file that calls itself the single authoritative law. The "could not be made data-driven" justification also fails on the terms page specifically: that page ALREADY calls `getGlobalConfig()` and interpolates `{objectionHours}` in all three locales, for exactly the stated reason ("this page cannot be statically baked — it would freeze a legal promise at whatever the window was on the day of the last build"). The same mechanism is available for the fee and the withdrawal fee and is not used. Every one of the pinned numbers is editable at /admin/config: `platformFeeRate` (3%) + `operatorFeeRate` (10%) = the 13%, `withdrawalFeeRate` (1.5%) and `freeExitGraceMinutes` (5) all have Input fields in config-form.tsx and all are hydrated `{ ...defaults, ...restored }` from the SystemConfig row. Aggravating: `test:rate-copy` is not in the `predeploy` chain — that chain has 94 steps and rate-copy is not one of them (verified by parsing package.json scripts), so nothing on the deploy path runs the only guard §7 says enforces the list.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md header ("Do not restate a rate anywhere else… listed in §7 as a known duplicate, with its file and line") and §7 lines 561, 567, 600
findings.concreteScenario: An officer opens /admin/config and lowers the operator share from 10.0% to 8.0% (a legitimate tune — the field exists, `defaultValue={operatorPct}`, and RULES §5 permits a rule change). Markets created from that moment freeze `platformFeeRate 0.03 + operatorFeeRate 0.08 = 11%` of the losing side. A player then bets TZS 500,000 NO on a market whose YES side loses TZS 400,000; the fee taken is 11% × 400,000 = TZS 44,000, not the 13% × 400,000 = TZS 52,000 the binding contract states in all three languages. /legal/terms still reads "Our commission is 13% of the losing side", the assistant still answers "13% OF THE LOSING SIDE", and `npm run test:rate-copy` — the only guard §7 names — goes GREEN, because 3.2 and 3.6 are satisfied by the stale literals still being there. It would go RED only if someone corrected them.
findings.moneyImpact: The direction of the error is not bounded: the same mechanism lets the binding contract understate or overstate the fee on every settled pool after any /admin/config change. On the worked example above the contract misstates the fee by TZS 8,000 on a single TZS 400,000 losing side, in the document that governs every player's claim. The withdrawal-fee literal has the same shape (`withdrawalFeeRate` step 0.01, min 0, max 5 at /admin/config) and lands directly on each player's cash: a move to 2.0% would take TZS 20,000 off a TZS 1,000,000 withdrawal while the contract still promises 1.5% = TZS 15,000, a TZS 5,000 per-withdrawal gap the guard would never fire on.
