findings.title: The selection-close disclosure quotes Math.round(share x netPool) while settlement pays the largest-remainder floor, so a winner whose exact share ends in .5 is TOLD one shilling more than the wallet receives — under copy that promises the figure is exact "to the shilling"
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Two different rounding regimes price the same position. DISCLOSURE: `notifySelectionClosedForMarket` (market-service.ts:1821-1829) loops every OPEN position and calls `settledPayoutFor`, whose last money line is `const payout = Math.max(0, Math.round(share * fee.netPool));` (payout.ts:595). It writes that figure to `p.potentialPayout`, persists it, sends it in the bell notification and the email, and it is what `/positions` and `/admin/markets/[id]` then render. SETTLEMENT: `settleMarket` never calls `settledPayoutFor` for the money — it calls `allocateWinnerPayouts` (market-service.ts:3518), which floors each winner (`Math.floor(raw)`, payout.ts:695-698) and distributes `Math.floor(netPool) - allocated` top-up shillings to the largest fractional parts, tie-broken by ascending position id (payout.ts:700-703). `Math.round` breaks a .5 tie UPWARD unconditionally; largest-remainder gives the top-up only while `remainder > 0`, so a tied winner who sorts late by id gets nothing.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES' preamble makes a player surface that disagrees with the money the defect, and RULES §2.6 states the doctrine directly: "Overstating what a player gets is the same failure class as overstating a control to the Gaming Board." The surfaces do not hedge — they assert exactness. `i18n-dict.ts:1026` renders the hint "Exact — betting is closed and the pools are final." beside the figure (and the same claim in SW at 3312 and ZH at 5363); `email.ts:1078` says "The pools are frozen, so this is the exact amount — not an estimate. It is what we will pay you, to the shilling, if your side wins." The arithmetic cannot deliver that, because the disclosing function and the paying function are different functions with different tie behaviour. The ledger is NOT wrong — settlement sums exactly to floor(netPool) and RULES §1's own production figures reconcile — so this is a DISCLOSURE / no-fabrication defect (A-5, RULES §2.9 severity-and-truth family), not a mint-or-leak defect. But the direction is the one that matters: on a .5 share the quote is always the HIGHER number.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md preamble ("if ... a player surface disagrees with this file, that other thing is a defect") + §2.6's overstatement doctrine + §2.9 (a player-facing statement must be true); RULES §1 supplies the reproducing production book. No RULES section prescribes a rounding rule, so the rounding itself is internal-consistency.
findings.concreteScenario: RULES §1's own live poll `mkt_3254d2723f3443358300`, replayed through the real code: winning pool 8,000 (three winners staking 5,000 / 2,000 / 1,000 — all inside the 1,000-1,000,000 bounds), losing pool 13,000, fee 0.13 x 13,000 = 1,690, netPool 19,310. Exact shares 12,068.75 / 4,827.50 / 2,413.75 (RULES quotes these verbatim). Executed the two code paths on those numbers: disclosure `[12069, 4828, 2414]` (sum 19,311); settlement `[12069, 4827, 2414]` (sum 19,310 = floor(netPool)). The 2,000-stake winner's bell message, email, /positions card and the admin Payout column all read TZS 4,828; the wallet is credited TZS 4,827. A two-bet market reproduces it with no ties at all: YES 1,000 (one winner) / NO 1,010 (one loser) → fee 131.30, netPool 1,878.70 → disclosed 1,879, paid 1,878.
findings.moneyImpact: The player loses exactly 1 TZS against the figure they were shown, per affected position. No money is minted or leaked — the shilling stays as pool residual/house dust. The cost is the broken promise, not the shilling: the platform states an exact amount in three languages plus email and then pays less, on a licensed money surface, and this is the shape a regulator or a support ticket reads as the operator shaving a payout. Systematic, not random: `Math.round` rounds every .5 up, and equal stakes (the Up & Down preset ladder is literally [1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000], stake-math.ts:12-16) make tied fractions the ordinary case rather than the exotic one.

findings.title: The gap is NOT bounded at one shilling: the selection-close notification SUMS per-position Math.round figures across a player's side, and the Up & Down locked quote prices the whole side as one aggregate — a ten-position holder can be quoted 10 TZS more than settlement pays
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Per POSITION the two regimes can only differ by 1 TZS (round(x) and the allocation are both in {floor(x), floor(x)+1}). But neither disclosure surface quotes per position. `notifySelectionClosedForMarket` builds `ifYes`/`ifNo` by SUMMING each position's independently-rounded figure (market-service.ts:1838-1839) and hands the sum to the bell (`notifySelectionClosed`) and the email subject/body. On Up & Down, `toBoardRound` prices `myPayoutIfUp` / `myPayoutIfDown` / `myExactPayout` from `heldPayout(m, "YES", myUpStake)` (updown-board.ts:532-539), where `myUpStake` is the SUM of the viewer's OPEN positions on that side (updown-board.ts:626 `if (p.side === "YES") e.up += p.stake;`), so one `Math.round` is applied to an aggregate that settlement allocates position by position. RULES §2.4 makes positions per market unlimited, so N is unbounded.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The lead asked whether any surface can overstate by more than a shilling; it can. The error accumulates once per position when fractions tie, because `Math.round` takes every .5 up while largest-remainder tops up only `remainder` of them and tie-breaks by ascending random position id (`pos_${randomId(10)}`) — so roughly half the tied holders are overstated and which half is a coin flip. Nothing in the code bounds the summed divergence, and the surface still carries the exactness copy from LEAD-E.1.
findings.rulesReference: RULES §2.4 (unlimited positions per market, either or both sides) is what removes the bound; RULES §2.6's overstatement doctrine and §2.9 are what make the overstated total a defect. none - the rounding rule itself is internal consistency.
findings.concreteScenario: A long-form poll on the loser-share default. YES pool 20,000 = twenty separate 1,000 bets (all at the platform minimum, inside §2.3 bounds); one of the twenty holders — call her Neema — placed ten of them. NO pool 1,000 (one losing bet). Fee 0.13 x 1,000 = 130, netPool 20,870; every winner's exact share is 1,000/20,000 x 20,870 = 1,043.50 exactly, so all twenty fractions tie at .5. Executed both paths: disclosure rounds each to 1,044, so Neema's bell message and email say "If YES wins you receive TZS 10,440". Settlement floors each to 1,043 (total 20,860), remainder = 20,870 - 20,860 = 10, and the ten top-ups go to the ten LOWEST position ids. If Neema's ten positions are the high-id half she is credited 10 x 1,043 = TZS 10,430. The same shape on Up & Down (ten 1,000 UP taps — the first chip on the preset ladder) makes `heldPayout` quote round(10,000/20,000 x 20,870) = 10,435 on the locked card against 10,430 paid: 5 TZS over.
findings.moneyImpact: Neema is shown TZS 10,440 and paid TZS 10,430 — 10 shillings short of a figure the product called exact, with no explanation on any screen. Nothing is minted or leaked (the ten shillings went to the ten low-id winners; the group still sums to floor(netPool)), so this is disclosure damage that scales with position count, not a ledger hole. Direction is over for a tied book roughly half the time and never predictable to the player.

findings.title: /admin/finance labels a RECOMPUTE as "Total commission this period", and it structurally cannot see fees whose market row no longer exists
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The 'Settlement fees by poll' card footers a bare total: `Total commission this period: {formatTzs(pollFees.totalFee)}.` That total comes from `analytics.ts → settlementFeesByPoll`, which iterates `listMarkets({ status: "RESOLVED" })` and RECOMPUTES each fee with `poolFee(m.yesPool, m.noPool, ratesFor(m), m.resolvedOutcome)` — the current pool columns, priced through `snapshotOrLegacy`, which for a market with no `feeSnapshot` reconstructs the fee at `LEGACY_COMMISSION_RATE = 0.09` under `capped-commission` with today's ceiling. Nothing on this page reads `HOUSE:COMMISSION` entries for the window, and no variance between the recompute and the books is shown.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The repo's own law names this exact function as the hazard it was written against: `src/lib/server/house-ledger.ts:6-12` — 'THE LEDGER IS THE TRUTH; A RECOMPUTE IS A CHECK. `analytics.ts → settlementFeesByPoll()` reports per-poll fees by RECOMPUTING them … the moment one drifts it reports revenue the books never recorded, silently and confidently.' `/admin/house` obeys that and renders a variance; `/admin/finance` prints the recompute under the word 'commission' with nothing beside it. And the population is wrong by construction: the total can only contain markets that still have a `PredictionMarket` row. The legacy arm is also deliberately NOT what was charged — `market-config.ts:308-313` says the 9%-with-new-ceiling fallback 'can only ever REDUCE the fee versus what those players were quoted'.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (RULES §2.1 'Frozen per market' — a market settles by its stamped snapshot forever; a reconstructed rate is not that snapshot)
findings.concreteScenario: On an all-time window, `/admin/house` → Earnings reads booked `HOUSE:COMMISSION` entries and includes the 121 ledger `marketId`s that have no market row — the purge ceremony redacts and a 2026-07/08 teardown deleted some outright — which this repo records as carrying 54,650 TZS of real fees, one of them the second-largest earner in the whole book (src/app/admin/house/page.tsx, comment at the game-row join). `settlementFeesByPoll` starts from `listMarkets(...)`, so those 121 contribute exactly TZS 0. The two owner screens therefore state the same period's commission 54,650 TZS apart, on the same books, with nothing rendered red on either. Separately, for a settled poll with no `feeSnapshot` (44 such markets measured on production 2026-09-05 per market-config.ts; the remediation doc says 58) with pools YES 900,000 / NO 100,000, the row prints fee = min(0.09 × 1,000,000, (1/3) × 100,000) = TZS 33,333 as 'Fee taken' — a number reconstructed today, not the number the ledger booked on the day.
findings.moneyImpact: An accountant reconciling the period against the ledger is handed a commission total that omits every fee whose market row was redacted or deleted (54,650 TZS on the current production book) and that re-prices every snapshot-less market at a rate chosen to differ from what was charged. The error is silent in both directions and there is no variance line to catch it.

findings.title: NGR subtracts the whole player-charged withdrawal fee as a processing cost, so house revenue is booked as an expense on the regulator hand-off pack
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `summarise` builds `fees` as the sum of `t.fee` over CONFIRMED DEPOSIT and WITHDRAWAL transactions and subtracts the whole thing from NGR. On a withdrawal, `t.fee` is the 1.5% charged to the PLAYER (`wallet-service.ts:1572 → computeWithdrawalFee(amount, wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate)`, stamped on the txn at creation). `withdrawalEntries` then splits it: only `gatewayShare` (0.5 percentage points) leaves for `HOUSE:AGGREGATOR`; the remaining `houseShare` is credited to `HOUSE:COMMISSION` as our income. GGR never contained the fee at all (`ggr = stakes - payouts - refunds`), so the subtraction removes money that was never added.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.7: the withdrawal fee is 1.5% of the amount withdrawn and only 0.5 percentage points of it is the gateway's — the other 1.0 point is operator revenue. The pack's own note describes the deduction as 'payment-processing fees', which is the gateway share, not the player-charged fee. Treating the full charge as a cost both loses the revenue and invents an expense.
findings.rulesReference: RULES §2.7 (withdrawal fee 1.5%, 0.5 percentage points of it the gateway's)
findings.concreteScenario: A player withdraws TZS 500,000. `computeWithdrawalFee` → 7,500; `gatewayShare` = round(500,000 × 0.005) = 2,500; `houseShare` = 5,000 credited to HOUSE:COMMISSION. `summarise` puts 7,500 into `fees` and NGR falls by 7,500. The truthful movement is +5,000 of revenue and −2,500 of gateway cost, i.e. +2,500. NGR is therefore 10,000 TZS below the truth for this one withdrawal — 2% of the amount withdrawn — and that NGR is what `buildGbtMonthly` publishes under 'Net gaming revenue' in a document whose own meta says `classification: "Regulator hand-off"`.
findings.moneyImpact: The operator's declared bottom line is understated by 2% of every shilling withdrawn — 10,000 TZS per 500,000 withdrawn — on the monthly pack handed to the Gaming Board and on the `/admin/finance` NGR tile the owner reads beside it.

findings.title: `test:money-invariants` is an in-memory fixture suite that never reads production, so "the money invariants pass" is a statement about synthetic users; the one escrow-component suite is not even in the pre-deploy chain
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The suite's own header declares "in-memory store; no DATABASE_URL". It mints users and wallets directly through `db.user.create` / `db.wallet.create` (lines 59-69) and drives the real services over that in-memory store, asserting NO-NEGATIVE, NO-MINT, CONSERVATION, VOID full-refund, IDEMPOTENCY and AUDITED. It is invoked from `predeploy` (package.json:218) and from CI via `node scripts/test-all.mjs --skip responsive,motion` (ci.yml:74-75), which enumerates every `test:*` script (test-all.mjs:44-46) — in a job whose only DATABASE_URL is the throwaway CI Postgres used later for the s10/s11/s12 cross-instance proofs, never for this suite.
findings.whyItIsWrong: It is a correct and valuable CI suite; the defect is treating it as production coverage. It cannot observe a single real wallet, a single real POOL account or a single real HOUSE balance. Nothing anywhere runs it, or anything like it, against the live database on a schedule. So the platform's answer to "are the books right?" in production rests entirely on the one daily in-app trial balance (LEAD-G.1/G.2) and the nightly backup's source read (LEAD-G.3) — the first of which cannot tell anyone and the second of which is classified as healthy. Separately, `test:pool-residual` — the suite explicitly written because the aggregate checks were green on both sides of a real production defect — is missing from the `predeploy` chain entirely (grep of package.json:218 returns 0), so it runs only under `test:all`.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency; distinguishes REAL-IN-SOURCE (a CI fixture) from REACHABLE-IN-PRODUCTION (nothing)
findings.concreteScenario: Take LEAD-G.4's exact case: two winners on TZS 3,000 and TZS 5,000 of an 8,000 winning pool, fee 260, escrow closing at TZS −1. `npm run test:money-invariants` passes 84/84 against its own in-memory fixtures because the assertions it makes (Σ payouts ≤ gross pool; final + house == in, within a `dust` tolerance of `winnerCount + scenarios.length + 2` shillings at line 220) are aggregate identities that a self-cancelling POOL −1 / COMMISSION +1 pair satisfies. Its own sibling suite states this outright. So the pre-deploy gate reports the money invariants green, the deploy ships, and the production books carry the residual with nothing scheduled that could ever look.
findings.moneyImpact: No direct loss. It removes the last plausible answer to "who would find out?": the suite that carries the word 'invariants' in its name has never read a shilling of real money and never will in its current form.

findings.title: The alarm that says "the money invariant is not running" is itself channel-less — and `payout-observability.test.mts` certifies it as observability by regex-matching the audit call in the source text
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: When five consecutive ticks are swallowed by an overrunning pass, `runLifecyclePass` raises `void audit({ category: "COMPLIANCE", action: "lifecycle.ticker_overrun", ... }).catch(() => {})` with a payload naming `stalled: ["payment reconcile", "wallet↔ledger trial balance", "bonus expiry", "schedule reconcile"]`. Nothing consumes that action — grep for `ticker_overrun` returns lifecycle.ts:286/365 and one regex assertion in payout-observability.test.mts:267.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The code's own comment at lines 360-362 states the intent: "COMPLIANCE, not SYSTEM — the same category the trial-balance drift alert uses, because this is the alert that says the trial balance ISN'T RUNNING. An officer watching one must see the other." Neither is watched by anything, so the sentence describes a pair of alarms that are both mute. The guard that covers this is the sharper problem: scripts/payout-observability.test.mts:250-289 asserts by REGEX OVER lifecycle.ts's SOURCE TEXT that the audit call is present, that it is COMPLIANCE, that it fires once per episode, and that `lifecycleTickerHealth` is exported and referenced by the health route — then names the section "PAYOUT OBSERVABILITY". Would it still pass if the feature (an alarm that reaches a human) were absent? It passes today and that feature IS absent. It is asserting the shape of the write, not the existence of a reader. The one genuine escape hatch is `/api/health` line 95 exposing `ticker.skippedConsecutive` / `skippedTotal` — which requires an external poller that parses that specific field, and the health route's own comment (lines 36-40) records that Railway queries `healthcheckPath` ONLY during a deploy and "explicitly does NOT monitor it afterwards".
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency
findings.concreteScenario: `healUpDownRounds()` runs on every 60-second tick and is documented at lifecycle.ts:285-291 as "THE SLOWEST CHORE IN THE PASS, and the most likely trigger of a `lifecycle.ticker_overrun` alert" — with the AI price reader taking tens of seconds per boundary observation, a batch can exceed the 60s tick. Say it does, for six hours overnight. The overlap guard skips every tick, so `maybePaymentSweeps` (which recovers deposits a player has already been debited for) and `maybeReconcileLedger` never run. On the fifth skipped tick ONE COMPLIANCE audit row is written and then the alert re-arms only after a completed pass. A player who deposited TZS 250,000 through Selcom whose webhook was lost sits on a PROCESSING screen for six hours with the reconcile that would have credited them not running, and the alarm that says so is a row in a table nobody queries.
findings.moneyImpact: Indirect but real: the overrun stalls `reconcileStalePayments` and `notifyStillPendingDeposits`, which are the recovery path for money a player HAS ALREADY PAID (lifecycle.ts:177-182 records that exact incident: "That is money taken and not delivered, and it was live"). A stall of that path is money owed and undelivered for the length of the stall, with the only notification being an audit row.

findings.title: docs/rates-for-admins.html (and the PDF rendered from it) states free cancellation flat, and states the bonus-wagering rule in the present tense as a live player-facing behaviour three days after the bonus wallet was withdrawn
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The rates table in the administrators' guide carries two rows that misdescribe the platform. Line 66: `Free cancellation5 minutes after placing the bet, full refund. After that the bet is locked.` — under a column header that reads "Normal polls and Up & Down — identical" (line 59). Line 65: `Bonus betting requirementOnly one side of a market counts toward clearing a bonus. The player is warned before confirming, and the bet still goes ahead.` — present tense, describing a warning the player product no longer shows because no grant can exist. Nothing anywhere in the 316-line file mentions runway, bonus-funded ineligibility, or that free cancellation cannot be exercised on 3- and 5-minute rounds; grep for "cancel" returns only line 66, and §4 "Game two — Up & Down" and §5 "The two games, side by side" add no caveat.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Two RULES violations in one table. (a) The free-cancellation row states only the WINDOW condition and explicitly extends it to Up & Down via the "identical" column header — RULES §2.6 says the right is "UNREACHABLE at 3 and 5 minutes — always, by construction" and that anyone quoting it "must say which product and which round length". (b) The bonus row states as live a rule the roll-out table marks 💤 DORMANT: "The **bonus wallet is withdrawn from the player product** (Ali, 2026-09-06) — no new grant is issued, so no new stake can be bonus-funded." The chat prompt already carries the withdrawal ("THERE IS NO PLAYER REFERRAL OR INVITE PROGRAMME, AND NO BONUS WALLET", chat.ts:132); the hand-out does not. And this file is unreachable by every guard in the repo: `test:rate-copy` scans `dict` plus two named .tsx/.ts files, never docs/*.html, and it is not in the predeploy chain either. scripts/generate-rates-pdf.mjs:28-29 renders `in: "docs/rates-for-admins.html"` to `out: "docs/50pick-rates-for-admins.pdf"`, and both files carry the same mtime (Sep 9 09:11), so the PDF hand-out carries both errors verbatim.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.6 (runway / not-bonus-funded, and the duty to name product and round length) and the ROLL-OUT STATUS table's bonus row (💤 DORMANT, bonus wallet withdrawn 2026-09-06)
findings.concreteScenario: A support officer takes a call from a player who staked TZS 250,000 on a 3-minute BTC Up & Down round and could not find the Sell button. The officer reads line 66 of the hand-out — "5 minutes after placing the bet, full refund", column header "Normal polls and Up & Down — identical" — and tells the player the platform owes them a refund, or escalates it as a platform bug. The refund is not owed and the code is correct; the officer either credits TZS 250,000 that should not be credited, or burns an escalation on a non-defect, and in either case has restated to a customer the same overstatement RULES §2.6 calls a Gaming-Board-class failure. Separately, an officer reading line 65 tells a player their bonus turnover only counts one side — a rule the player cannot have any subject for, since no grant can be issued.
findings.moneyImpact: Per incident, an unwarranted goodwill credit of up to TZS 1,000,000 (the per-bet maximum) issued because the internal reference contradicts the settlement code; and the officer-facing surface repeats the §2.6 overstatement to customers by voice, where nothing records it. The bonus row is not a direct cash loss but sets up a promise ("you have a bonus requirement, one side counts") for a product feature that has been withdrawn.

findings.title: The binding terms hardcode the 5-minute free-exit window as a literal in all three languages while the same page proves the interpolation mechanism exists — an officer moving freeExitGraceMinutes leaves the contract stating a window the server does not honour
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The terms interpolate exactly one live setting — `const { objectionWindowHours } = await getGlobalConfig();` passed as `{objectionHours}` into §6 in all three locales — and hardcode the free-exit window as "5 minutes" / "dakika 5" / "前 5 分钟" at lines 120, 246 and 359. `freeExitGraceMinutes` is a first-class /admin/config field with `type="number" step="1" min="0" max="60"` (config-form.tsx:128), is validated and persisted (market-config.ts:594-595, admin/config/actions.ts:63,86), and is hydrated over the code default from the SystemConfig row (market-config.ts:217 `freeExitGraceMinutes: DEFAULT_FREE_EXIT_GRACE_MINUTES, // 5`).
findings.whyItIsWrong: The page's own doc-comment states the rule it then breaks: "The void ground in §6 tracks a LIVE setting, so this page cannot be statically baked — it would freeze a legal promise at whatever the window was on the day of the last build." The free-exit window is equally a live setting and equally a legal promise, and it is frozen in the text. RULES.md's header forbids restating a number that this file also states; §2.6 states the 5 minutes and names `market.config` (`freeExitGraceMinutes`) as its configuration. So this is a §7-class duplicate in the binding legal text, sitting in the one file that already demonstrates the correct pattern three lines of code away. It is also invisible to the only guard: rate-copy's RATE_PATTERNS match a percentage `/(?<!\{)\b\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?\s*%/` or a multiple `/(?<!\{)\b\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?\s*[×x](?![\w])/i` — "5 minutes" is neither, so §1 could not see it even if the terms were in the dictionary, and §3 does not check for it.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md header ("Do not restate a rate anywhere else… Copy that must show a rate reads it from config") and §2.6 ("Configured in `market.config` (`freeExitGraceMinutes`)")
findings.concreteScenario: An officer, acting on the 0-of-688 cash-out statistic, sets Free-exit window to 10 minutes at /admin/config so that 10- and 15-minute Up & Down rounds get a usable exit. New markets freeze `freeExitGraceMinutes: 10`. A player stakes TZS 800,000 on a 30-minute round, reads the Chinese terms ("前 5 分钟内您可全额取回本金"), and at minute 7 believes the window shut — so he does not sell, when the server would have refunded the full TZS 800,000. The reverse move (an officer setting 3 to reduce exit abuse) is worse: the contract still promises 5 minutes, and a player selling at minute 4 is refused a refund the binding text says he is owed on TZS 800,000.
findings.moneyImpact: Up to TZS 1,000,000 per bet, either forfeited by a player who trusted a stale contract and did not exercise a right he had, or claimed against the platform by a player refused a right the contract still promises. Unbounded in repetition — every open position after the config change is affected until the legal text is edited and redeployed by hand, with no guard that fires.

src/app/legal/terms/page.tsx (TermsPage)  `  const { objectionWindowHours } = await getGlobalConfig();` — the mechanism exists and is used for exactly one number

src/app/admin/config/config-form.tsx:128  `          <Input name="freeExitGraceMinutes" type="number" step="1" min="0" max="60" defaultValue={config.freeExitGraceMinutes} mono />`

findings.title: The bet dialog's payout hint still teaches the RETIRED capped-commission fee rule to players in all three languages — and it is invisible to test:rate-copy because the retired numbers are interpolated
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The InfoHint beside the payout figure on the conviction dial reads, when the estimate is not shown: "Winners share the pool in proportion to their stake, after our commission. The commission is {pct}% of the pool but never more than {ceiling} of the smaller side — so a winning bet is never paid less than it staked." SW: "Kamisheni ni {pct}% ya bwawa lakini kamwe si zaidi ya {ceiling} ya upande mdogo". ZH: "佣金为奖池的 {pct}%，但绝不超过较小一方的 {ceiling}". conviction-dial.tsx:1602 fills it with `pct: pctNum(rates?.commissionRate ?? DEFAULT_COMMISSION_RATE)` (0.10) and `ceiling: fmtRate(rates?.feeCeilingRate ?? DEFAULT_FEE_CEILING_RATE)`. The branch is chosen at line 1590: `const showEstimate = rates?.feeModel === "loser-share" && rates?.showEstimatedWinnings !== false;` — the retired text renders whenever `showEstimatedWinnings` is false, on a loser-share poll included.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §1 states one fee rule for both games — "13% of the LOSING side — Platform 3% + Operator 10%" — and §3 records capped-commission as legacy, "retained only because markets created before the cutover froze it". §7's Was/Now table records that this exact retired rule was hunted out of `card3Body`, `howStep3B` and /legal/terms; `payoutHowItWorks` states the same retired model and survived, in three locales. The guard cannot see it: RATE_PATTERNS explicitly exempt a placeholder before the unit ("`{pct}%` and `{mult}×` are INTERPOLATED and are exactly what the method asks for, so a placeholder immediately before the unit is never a hit"), §2's positive control only pins the WORDS "third of the smaller side" / "theluthi moja ya upande mdogo", and this string says "{ceiling} of the smaller side" — the model is stated, the retired number is interpolated, and every check passes. That is the guard-that-matches-a-vocabulary failure: the sweep banned a phrase, not a model. This is also the copy the binding terms contradict head-on — /legal/terms:98 says "Our commission is 13% of the losing side… our commission comes only out of the money staked on the outcome that did not happen", while this hint tells the same player the commission is a share of the whole pool.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §1 (the fee is 13% of the LOSING side, both games) and §3 (capped-commission is legacy, frozen per market, never the live model) — and §7, which claims this class of copy was swept
findings.concreteScenario: An officer switches "Show estimated winnings" off at /admin/config (the toggle exists: config-form.tsx:35/65, actions.ts:82/101) — a plausible compliance move, since D3 hid the payout figure pre-bet. A player opens a live loser-share market that froze `showEstimatedWinnings: false`, taps the payout info hint, and is told the commission is 10% of the pool capped at a third of the smaller side. He stakes TZS 200,000 YES on a market that settles YES with a YES pool of 200,000 and a NO pool of 600,000. Under the copy he expects a fee of min(10% × 800,000, 33.3% × 200,000) = TZS 66,600; the market actually charges 13% × 600,000 = TZS 78,000. Same-direction error, but the copy also tells him the fee comes out of the whole pool including his own winning stake — which RULES §1 and the terms both say it never does.
findings.moneyImpact: Per bet, a stated fee that differs from the charged fee by TZS 11,400 on the worked TZS 800,000 pool, and a materially wrong description of whose money is taken. Not a settlement error — the maths is correct — but it is the player-facing fee statement disagreeing with the binding contract on the same screen the money is committed on. Reachability depends on a single config toggle, so the size of the affected population cannot be read from the repo.
