findings.title: Every withdrawal refusal is painted as a hard error; the registry's severity never crosses the redirect
findings.whatTheCodeDoes:
`errorCopy()` routes a reasoned refusal through `renderFailure()` and returns only `.body` (error-copy.ts:43-50) — `renderFailure`'s `severity` is discarded on the floor. The action then puts that bare sentence on the query string (actions.ts:116) and the page renders it, unconditionally, inside the `border-no-700 / bg-no-500` box under the fixed headline "Withdrawal didn't go through" (page.tsx:152-159). There is one visual state for every refusal.

The registry disagrees with all of it: `withdraw_below_min`, `withdraw_balance_insufficient` and `withdraw_bonus_locked` are all `severity: "warning"` (failure-reasons.ts:308-319), because — in the file's own words at line 295 — "a fixable problem is a WARNING and only a genuine block is an ERROR". `failure-banner.ts:77` shows what the converted surfaces do with that severity: `tone: r.severity === "error" ? "danger" : r.severity === "warning" ? "warning" : "info"`. The withdraw page has no such mapping because the severity is never sent.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.9 requires the refusal at "a severity that matches what happened", and lists "below minimum, above maximum, insufficient balance" explicitly as info/warning. This is the same failure the RULES record for the Up & Down acknowledge modal — the file's own line: "Severity answers *how loud*; it cannot also answer *whose decision this was*." Here the channel throws the severity away entirely and defaults everything to the loudest.
findings.rulesReference: §2.9 ("at a severity that matches what happened" — info/warning for insufficient balance and below-minimum; error only for a genuine fault or hard block)
findings.concreteScenario: A player with a TZS 900,000 balance types 1,000,000 (the top of the §2.3 band) and confirms. `withdraw()` reaches wallet-service.ts:1625, `w.balance < amount`, and returns `shortOfFunds` with reason `withdraw_balance_insufficient` — declared `severity: "warning"` at failure-reasons.ts:312. The player sees the losing-bet-red panel headed "Withdrawal didn't go through", identical in weight to what a suspended account or a hard rail failure would produce, for a mistake they fix by typing 900000 instead. Identical treatment for the MO-9.a below-minimum refusal, which is likewise a declared warning.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings move. The harm is that the money-out screen cannot distinguish "retype the amount" from "your account is blocked", so a player who mistyped an amount is told, in the platform's most alarming register, that their withdrawal failed. On a licensed operator that is the difference between a corrected keystroke and a support ticket / an abandoned balance.

findings.title: A payout-rail failure tells the player "check the details and try again" and never says their money came back
findings.whatTheCodeDoes:
When the gateway refuses, `withdraw()` reverses the hold and returns one of two sentences with `code: "INVALID"` and NO `reason` (wallet-service.ts:1759-1761). `errorCopy()` therefore skips the registry (`hasReason` is false), falls into `case "INVALID"`, finds no "·" separator, and returns `t.error.errInvalid` — "That didn't go through. Check the details and try again." (i18n-dict.ts:2098). The service's own carefully-written next step — "Your balance is unchanged — please try again later" / "Funds returned to your balance" — is thrown away before the player sees it.

The same hole swallows the provider kill-switch refusal: wallet-service.ts:1449 returns SUSPENDED with "Try another method or check back shortly", and errorCopy's SUSPENDED arm (error-copy.ts:101-102) fails the /frozen/i test and returns `t.error.errSuspended` — "This service is temporarily paused. Try again shortly." The actionable half ("try another method") is dropped.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.9: "Every player-facing refusal states the reason and the next step" and "⛔ No screen … says only 'failed'." "That didn't go through. Check the details and try again" attributes the fault to the player's input, names no reason, and prescribes a next step that is actively wrong — there are no details to check, and retrying immediately re-hits a rail that is down. This is the exact shape the repo already fixed once (the E-223 note at wallet-service.ts:1613-1622: "It returned INVALID with no reason, so errorCopy fell through to the generic errInvalid … on the most common refusal of the money-out screen"), left unfixed on the rail-failure branches.
findings.rulesReference: §2.9 (reason + next step, matching severity; no screen says only "failed")
findings.concreteScenario: A player requests TZS 250,000 while Selcom's cashin rail is refusing (the state production sat in from 2026-07-29 — see the sealed bypass note at actions.ts:62-68). `withdraw()` places the hold, `dispatchWithdrawal` returns PROVIDER_DOWN, `settleWithdrawalFailed` reverses the hold, and the service composes "Withdrawals are temporarily unavailable. Your balance is unchanged — please try again later." The player never reads that sentence. They read "That didn't go through. Check the details and try again" over the headline "Withdrawal didn't go through", with the amount and provider re-populated in the form. The rational response is to change a digit and press again, which fails again, at whatever rate `wallet.withdraw` allows before RATE_LIMITED. The player's reasonable conclusion is that TZS 250,000 of theirs is stuck.
findings.moneyImpact: The TZS 250,000 is safely returned by settleWithdrawalFailed, so nothing is lost on the ledger — the defect is that the player is not told so on the one screen that could tell them, and is instead pointed at their own input. On a payout rail that has actually been down for weeks, this converts a transient outage into a plausible "the operator has taken my money" for every player who tries.

findings.title: /legal/terms hardcodes the 1.5% withdrawal fee in three languages while the withdraw screen interpolates it — and test:rate-copy REQUIRES the hardcode
findings.whatTheCodeDoes:
The withdraw screen is clean: page.tsx:248 renders `fill(t.wallet.taxBody, { pct: pctNum(wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate) })`, and no dictionary string anywhere states 1.5% (grepped all three locales). The contractual document is not. `/legal/terms` §5 writes the literal "1.5%" three times — EN line 134, SW line 260, ZH line 370 — as prose inside the page component, which `test:rate-copy` cannot reach because that scanner is anchored on the dictionary ("IT SCANS COPY, NOT CODE … The dictionary is the boundary", rate-copy.test.mts:24-26).

Worse, `test:rate-copy` §3.3 asserts the hardcode is PRESENT: it requires at least three literal "1.5%" occurrences in that file. And the page proves the fix is available — it is already `async`, already calls `getGlobalConfig()` (line 419) and already interpolates `{objectionHours}` from live config in all three locales.

RULES §7's known-duplicates table is declared EMPTY ("every rate the sweep found was made data-driven instead"). It is not empty: `/legal/terms` carries 1.5% ×3 and 13% ×3 as literals, guarded into place.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.7 says the withdrawal fee is "Stated to players on /wallet/withdraw, where it is interpolated from live config" — and §7's table, which is the register of every rate written inline, says there are none. There are six. `withdrawalFeeRate` is admin-tunable up to 0.05 (market-config.ts:606-607), so the Terms — the document the player accepted — can be made to state a fee lower than the one being charged, in three languages, with every guard green.
findings.rulesReference: §7 (the known-duplicates table is declared EMPTY — this contradicts it); §2.7 (the fee is interpolated from live config); §2.8 (what a player is charged, in full)
findings.concreteScenario: An operator raises `withdrawalFeeRate` to 0.03 at /admin/config (permitted: the validator at market-config.ts:607 rejects only >0.05). A player withdraws TZS 1,000,000. /wallet/withdraw correctly reads "A 3% fee applies to withdrawals, and nothing else" and the confirm dialog correctly shows "Withdrawal fee −TZS 30,000 · You receive TZS 970,000". /legal/terms §5 still reads, in bold, "A withdrawal is charged a 1.5% fee, and nothing else" — TZS 15,000. The player is charged TZS 15,000 more than the contract they accepted states, per withdrawal. `npm run test:rate-copy` passes; §3.3 would in fact FAIL if anyone made the terms data-driven and the literal "1.5%" disappeared.
findings.moneyImpact: TZS 15,000 per TZS 1,000,000 withdrawal charged above the rate the accepted Terms state, in all three languages, for every player, from the moment an operator retunes the rate. Compliance exposure rather than a ledger error: the operator's own contract denies the fee it is taking. Today, at the documented live 1.5%, the numbers agree and the harm is latent.

findings.title: The one place the derived 1,016 minimum reaches the client is an inert HTML attribute on a text input, and the form disables native validation anyway
findings.whatTheCodeDoes:
page.tsx:209 passes the derived minimum into `AmountField`, which passes it to `Input` as `min` (amount-field.tsx:61). `Input` destructures out `type`, `inputMode`, `step` and `onChange` and spreads the remainder — `min` included — onto the element (input.tsx:85, :133-136), but sets `effectiveType = isNumeric ? "text" : type` (input.tsx:106). Because the withdraw field declares `inputMode="numeric"` and no `type`, `isNumeric` is true and the rendered element is `<input type="text" min="1016" max="…" inputmode="numeric">`. HTML constraint validation applies `min`/`max` only to number, range and the date/time family; on `type="text"` both attributes are ignored outright — no validity state, no stepping, no exposure to assistive technology.

And even on a `type="number"` field it would still do nothing at commit, because `WithdrawConfirm.submitForm` sets `form.noValidate = true` immediately before `form.requestSubmit()` (withdraw-confirm.tsx:148-149). The only client-side amount check that actually runs is `validate()`, which uses WITHDRAW_MIN_TZS = 1,000 (withdraw-confirm.tsx:85).
findings.whyItIsWrong: The page comment at lines 206-208 presents this attribute as the protection against offering an amount "we cannot actually send". It is not a protection — it is a dead attribute that no user, no keyboard, no screen reader and no submit path ever consults. This is the mechanism by which MO-9.a's disagreement stays invisible: the correct number IS computed and IS handed to the client, and then evaporates.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (the page's own stated contract at page.tsx:206-208); it is the delivery mechanism for the §2.9 breach in MO-9.a
findings.concreteScenario: A player with a TZS 200,000 balance types 1014 into the amount box — a value the page's own rendered attribute `min="1016"` would reject if it were live. Nothing stops them: the field is `type="text"`, so the browser raises no constraint; `guardOpen` -> `validate()` compares against 1,000 and passes; the two-step money-commit dialog opens and states "Amount TZS 1,014 · Withdrawal fee −TZS 15 · You receive TZS 999"; `submitForm` sets `noValidate = true` and submits. `withdrawAction` passes. `withdraw()` computes net = 999 < 1,000 and refuses. Zero shillings move; the player has been walked all the way through a confirmation dialog for a transaction the platform will not perform, and told a net (TZS 999) it will not pay.
findings.moneyImpact: No direct loss on this path — the money never moves. The impact is that the ONE correct statement of the minimum on the entire client never reaches the player, which is what makes MO-9.a's stranded-balance case (a 1,010 balance that cannot be withdrawn) possible without anyone noticing. Every withdrawal attempt in the 1,000…1,014 band is a wasted commit.

findings.title: The settlement audit payload writes capped-commission fields on loser-share markets — `feeCeiling` is actually the LOSING POOL and `commissionUncapped` is 13% of the whole pool, neither of which is a ceiling or an uncapped commission
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The payload branches `rates` correctly on feeModel (:3719-3721) but then writes `commissionUncapped`, `feeCeiling` and `feeWasCapped` unconditionally from poolFee's return. poolFee's loser-share arm (payout.ts:483-487) fills those three slots with values that mean something else entirely: `commission` is a notional 13%-of-the-whole-pool figure its own inline comment calls "informational only", `ceiling` is the LOSING POOL, and `capped` is hardcoded false because the model has no ceiling concept.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The comment two lines above the fields invites an inspector to recompute the fee from the payload. On a loser-share market the three capped-model fields are not merely inert — `feeCeiling` aliases the losing pool under a name that says ceiling, and applying the capped recipe the same comment prints (`fee = min(commissionRate·pool, feeCeilingRate·smaller)`) to the payload's own numbers reproduces neither the fee nor anything meaningful. §3.3 of MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION claims exactly this, and it is confirmed.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (the record does not misstate a rule; it misnames the numbers a §2.2/§1 recomputation would use)
findings.concreteScenario: A loser-share poll settles YES on YES 15,000 (fifteen TZS 1,000 positions) / NO 1,000. Fee = 0.13 × 1,000 = 130. The chain records `commissionUncapped: 2080` (= round(0.13 × 16,000)), `feeCeiling: 1000` (= the losing pool), `feeWasCapped: false`, `fee: 130`. A regulator or a player computing min(commissionUncapped, feeCeiling) gets 1,000 — nearly eight times the fee actually charged — and the field literally labelled the ceiling is the base the fee was 13% OF, not a cap on it.
findings.moneyImpact: No money moves. Record integrity only: the settlement record for every loser-share market — the default model for all new polls (payout.ts:176 DEFAULT_FEE_MODEL) and therefore for every Up & Down round created since 2026-08-14 — carries three fields whose names assert a fee model that market did not use. The cost lands when a fee is disputed or a return is audited and the payload is read at face value.

findings.title: The permanent market.resolved audit payload writes capped-commission-named fields on loser-share settlements, where feeCeiling actually holds the LOSING POOL and commissionUncapped a figure never charged
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The `market.resolved` payload correctly branches its `rates:` object on `settleCfg.feeModel`, but writes `commissionUncapped`, `feeCeiling` and `feeWasCapped` unconditionally from `settleFee`. Under the loser-share arm poolFee sets `commission: loserRate * pool, // notional whole-pool figure — informational only`, `ceiling: losingPool, // the losing pool the fee is a share of` and `capped: false, // no ceiling concept in this model` (payout.ts:481-486).
findings.whyItIsWrong: The chain therefore permanently records, under a capped-commission vocabulary, two numbers that describe a retired law: `commissionUncapped` = 13% of the WHOLE pool (a fee that was never charged and cannot be under this model), and `feeCeiling` = the losing pool, which is not a ceiling at all. This is the same class RULES.md §2.1 records three times over ('A NUMBER CAN BE RIGHT UNDER A LAW THAT IS WRONG' — the /admin/updown caption, the /admin/config simulator), and here it is written into an append-only, HMAC-chained, 7-year record that cannot be corrected. The docblock two lines above promises 'An inspector (or a player who disputes a payout) can recompute the fee from these numbers'.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.1 ('⛔ The two maths NEVER mix'; §3 'Do not harmonise history') and §2.2 — the payload is the inspector-facing arithmetic record
findings.concreteScenario: The same loser-share poll: YES 100,000 (winner), NO 50,000 (loser), 13% frozen. The real fee is TZS 6,500 on the losing side. The `market.resolved` row records `fee: 6500` and `netPool: 143500` correctly, alongside `commissionUncapped: 19500` (0.13 x 150,000 — a figure nobody was ever charged), `feeCeiling: 50000` (the losing pool, labelled a ceiling) and `feeWasCapped: false`. A GBT inspector or a player disputing the payout reads a record stating an uncapped commission of TZS 19,500 against a ceiling of TZS 50,000 on a settlement that took TZS 6,500 — three numbers under a model with no commission-on-pool and no ceiling.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings move; the fee actually charged (TZS 6,500) and the payout (TZS 143,500) are both recorded correctly. The cost is that the permanent inspector-facing arithmetic record carries TZS 19,500 and TZS 50,000 as though they were the fee's mechanism, on a record that cannot be amended.

findings.title: Both money surfaces document an identity that does not exist — "come out of the same line of code, so they cannot disagree" and "the same arithmetic. To the shilling" — while settlement runs a different function with different tie behaviour
findings.functionName: notifySelectionClosedForMarket doc block / selectionClosedHtml doc block
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The disclosure block asserts that the quoted figure and the paid figure share a code path. They do not: disclosure is `settledPayoutFor` (payout.ts:595, `Math.round`) and settlement is `allocateWinnerPayouts` (payout.ts:695-703, floor + largest remainder). `settledPayoutFor` moves no money anywhere in the product — the only money callers of the payout module in `settleMarket` are `allocateWinnerPayouts` and `allocateFeeShares`, and `market-config.ts:875 settledPayoutWhole` has zero callers.
findings.whyItIsWrong: This is the exact failure class `payout.ts` already documents against itself at its `poolFee` doc block: "THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE FEE WAS PREVIEWED AGAINST THE SMALLER POOL, AND IT NEVER WAS ... a false sentence with no failing test behind it is invisible." RULES' preamble names a disagreeing code comment as a defect in its own right. Here the false sentence is load-bearing: it is the stated justification for printing "Exact" and "to the shilling" in front of a player, so the untrue comment is what authorises the untrue copy in LEAD-E.1.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md preamble — "If another document, a code comment, an admin screen or a player surface disagrees with this file, that other thing is a defect". Otherwise: none - internal consistency.
findings.concreteScenario: On the RULES §1 production book (winning pool 8,000; stakes 5,000/2,000/1,000; losing pool 13,000; fee 1,690; netPool 19,310) the comment claims the two figures cannot disagree, and they disagree for the 2,000-stake holder: disclosed 4,828, paid 4,827. An engineer reading market-service.ts:1807-1811 before touching the close sweep is told the invariant already holds and has no reason to test it; the one guard that asserts it strictly (money-e2e.test.mts:232 `what we PROMISED at close is what we PAID`, a `===`) runs on a fixture whose pools divide exactly — YES 100,000 / NO 80,000 under capped-commission, fee 18,000, netPool 162,000, shares 97,200 and 64,800, both whole — so it would still pass with `allocateWinnerPayouts` replaced by `Math.round`. The one guard that does drive real settlement against a quote, updown-hedge-quote.test.mts:288-292, uses `Math.abs(...) <= 1` and its own comment concedes "the dust can land a shilling either way".
findings.moneyImpact: No direct shillings. It is the mechanism by which LEAD-E.1 survives: a false invariant stated in the money file, with no discriminating guard behind it, in front of copy that repeats the invariant to the player in three languages.

findings.title: "Net retained" excludes HOUSE:AGENT_FEE, so the tile that claims to be what the owner keeps omits every shilling of registration-fee revenue
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `netRetained: commission + agentCommission` sums only `HOUSE:COMMISSION` and the (negative) `HOUSE:AGENT_COMMISSION`. `HOUSE:AGENT_FEE` — the net 100,000 of every reconciled registration fee, which `ledger.ts:200-207` describes as 'money taken from a member of the public [that] must be visible to the house book, the trial balance and every tax figure' — is not in the sum. It reaches `freeHouseCash` (via custodial cash) but not the earnings figure, and neither `ACCOUNT_NOTE` nor `HOUSE_ACCOUNT_NOTE` describes it, so it renders with an em-dash on /admin/house and with no hint on /admin/finance.
findings.whyItIsWrong: `HousePosition.netRetained` is documented as '⭐ What the owner actually keeps' and is rendered as the gold 'Net retained' KPI. It keeps the registration fee. The omission is in the conservative direction, so it does not build insolvency, but the two owner figures then disagree about the same money: free cash includes it, net retained does not, and no caption explains the gap.
findings.rulesReference: RULES §2.10 (Registration fee: 'it posts to HOUSE:AGENT_FEE (net) + HOUSE:TAX (VAT)')
findings.concreteScenario: Ten applicants are approved and their fees reconciled at TZS 118,000 each. HOUSE:AGENT_FEE holds 1,000,000. `/admin/house`'s 'Net retained' tile is unmoved by all ten, while 'Strict free cash' rises by 1,180,000. The owner reading 'what did we make' is short 1,000,000 TZS of real, earned, non-gaming revenue that is sitting one table down the same page under a caption that reads '—'.
findings.moneyImpact: The owner's earnings figure understates by TZS 100,000 per approved agent — 1,000,000 on a ten-agent book — and the same page's solvency line counts it, so the two cannot be reconciled from what is shown.

findings.title: `trialBalance()` returns `ok: true` when it cannot read the database, and the lifecycle then logs "books balanced" after checking nothing
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: If `prisma()` returns null, `trialBalance()` returns a fully clean report — `ok: true, checkedWallets: 0, globalBalanced: true, drift: []` — rather than an unknown/unavailable state. `maybeReconcileLedger` then takes the `tb.ok` branch and prints `[lifecycle] ledger trial balance OK — 0 wallets reconcile, books balanced` (lifecycle.ts:93-95).
findings.whyItIsWrong: A check that returns PASS on a read it could not perform is a vacuous green — the same class the platform has already fixed elsewhere (the `/api/health` `users: -1` in a 200 body, health/route.ts:29-34; the hardcoded backup tick, backup/state.ts:5-16). `prisma()` returns null iff `DATABASE_URL` is unset (prisma.ts:17-19, 86-87). The compounding part is that `/api/health` treats an unset DATABASE_URL as READY: `const dbReady = !dbPing.envSet || (dbPing.reachable && dbPing.tableExists);` (route.ts:46). So a container that ships without the variable answers HTTP 200 `ok:true` AND logs "books balanced", with `checkedWallets: 0` as the only tell — printed into a log nobody reads, per LEAD-G.1. The honest shape is a third state (unknown), not `ok: true`.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency
findings.concreteScenario: A Railway deploy ships with DATABASE_URL missing from the service (a variable-group rename, a new environment). The container boots, `/api/health` returns 200 with `database.configured: false` and `ok: true`, so the deploy gate passes and traffic is routed to it. Five minutes later the lifecycle pass prints `[lifecycle] ledger trial balance OK — 0 wallets reconcile, books balanced`. Every scheduled money check on the platform has now reported a clean pass while reading zero wallets and zero ledger entries. In practice the app is broken enough elsewhere to be noticed quickly, which is why this is `low` — but it means the ONE function this entire lane depends on cannot distinguish "I checked and it is fine" from "I checked nothing".
findings.moneyImpact: No direct shilling loss on its own. It removes the last safety property from the detector: after LEAD-G.2 a throw is silent, and after this a null client is a PASS — so `tb.ok === true` is not evidence that anything was examined.

findings.title: The /admin/config hint for freeExitGraceMinutes states only the window condition, so the officer who sets the number is never told about the runway rule — and the neighbouring hint contradicts itself by hardcoding "5-min" beside the interpolated value
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: The only guidance an officer gets when setting the free-exit window is: `hint={\`Current ${config.freeExitGraceMinutes} min. Sell within this long of placing a bet and it's a full refund at zero fee. 0 = no free window.\`}`. It states the WINDOW condition only — no runway, no bonus-funded exclusion, and no warning that at 5 minutes the setting is inert on 3- and 5-minute Up & Down chains. The adjacent paid-exit hint (line 132) interpolates `${config.freeExitGraceMinutes}-min` and then hardcodes the figure again in the same sentence: `(current policy — "5-min free exit, then nothing")`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.6 says free cancellation needs all three of `hadRunway && withinWindow && !bonusFunded`, and that the runway rule is what makes the setting unreachable on short rounds. The officer screen — the surface where the number is actually chosen — states one of the three. That is the same omission §2.6 was corrected to fix in RULES itself. The paid-exit hint's parenthetical is a straightforward self-contradiction: set the free window to 3 and the sentence reads "…the sell window LOCKS the moment the 3-min free window ends (current policy — \"5-min free exit, then nothing\")". Neither is player-facing, so this is not a mis-selling exposure — it is the setting's own documentation being wrong at the point of change, which is how a wrong value gets chosen.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.6 (the two conditions the section "used to omit"; free cancellation is configured in market.config and enforced in cashOutPosition)
findings.concreteScenario: An officer sees 0 cash-outs across 688 Up & Down rounds and concludes the 5-minute window is too tight. Reading only this hint — "Sell within this long of placing a bet and it's a full refund at zero fee" — he lowers it to 2 minutes to "tighten abuse", or raises it to 10 to "give players time". Lowering it to 2 does not help 3-minute rounds at all in the way he expects and silently shortens the promise the binding terms still state as 5 (see LEAD-H.5): a player selling at minute 3 on a TZS 600,000 stake is refused a refund the contract promises. Raising it to 10 makes the runway bar 600s, which no round shorter than 10 minutes can clear, so it removes the exit from 10-minute rounds that previously had one — the opposite of his intent — and again the contract still says 5.
findings.moneyImpact: Indirect but real: the officer's choice moves a refund right worth up to TZS 1,000,000 per bet, and the screen he chooses it on states one of the three conditions that govern it. On the 10-minute example the change silently withdraws the exit from a chain that had it, with no player notice and no guard.

findings.title: `minWithdrawalForRate` is one shilling too high at 1.5%, and the guard that exists to catch exactly that accepts the failing case by using `<=`
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `return Math.ceil(PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS / (1 - r));` → ceil(1000 / 0.985) = 1016. But the enforced test is `net < PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS` where net = amount − Math.round(amount × rate). At amount = 1015: fee = round(15.225) = 15, net = 1000, which is NOT less than 1000 — so 1,015 is accepted. The derived "minimum" overstates the true boundary by one shilling because it solves the continuous equation while the enforcement rounds the fee down.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The number is quoted to the player as the next step in the refusal (`detail.min`) and as the form's `min` attribute. More importantly, the guard written to pin this boundary asserts the defect: its label says "one shilling below the derived minimum does NOT clear it", but its comparison is `belowNet <= PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS`, which is TRUE precisely when belowNet == 1000 — i.e. when the shilling below DOES clear it. Would this assertion still pass if `minWithdrawalForRate` were correct? Yes. Would it pass if it were wrong? Also yes. It cannot distinguish the two.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (RULES.md §2.9 accuracy of the stated next step)
findings.concreteScenario: Live rate 1.5%. A player asks for TZS 1,014: fee 15, net 999 → refused, told "Withdraw at least TZS 1,016". A player who instead types 1,015 succeeds: fee 15, net 1,000, accepted and dispatched. So the platform refuses a figure while naming a minimum one shilling above the one it will actually take, and the withdraw form's `min="1016"` blocks the native spinner from ever reaching the true floor.
findings.moneyImpact: One shilling of stated minimum per player, and no shillings lost. The material harm is the guard: `scripts/withdrawal-fee.test.mts` is the only thing standing between this boundary and a rate change, and it is structurally unable to fail on it.

findings.title: The race-loss refusal reports the STALE balance, so it can tell a player "insufficient funds" while naming a balance larger than the amount refused — and can blame the bonus for it
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: When the atomic `WHERE balance >= amount` guard rejects the debit, the code calls `shortOfFunds(w, amount)` with `w` — the wallet object read at line 1614, BEFORE the concurrent debit that caused the rejection. `shortOfFunds` then returns `detail: { balance: w.balance, needed: amount }` and picks its reason from `bonusExplainsIt = bonus > 0 && amount <= w.balance + bonus`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Reaching line 1636 means the live balance is now below `amount`; but `w.balance` is by construction >= `amount` (line 1625 already passed on it). So the refusal ships a `balance` figure greater than or equal to the `needed` figure in the same payload, and if the player holds any bonus at all it selects `withdraw_bonus_locked` — telling them a wagering requirement is the obstacle when it is not. The code comment beside it insists both refusals "must say the SAME thing"; they say the same words over contradictory numbers. The fix is one line: re-read the wallet, or pass the live balance.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.9 (the refusal must state the reason and the next step; a figure that contradicts the refusal is neither)
findings.concreteScenario: Player holds TZS 60,000 cash plus a TZS 10,000 unfulfilled bonus grant. Two debits land in the same instant on the same wallet (a withdrawal of 50,000 and a bet of 20,000 whose debit commits first). The withdrawal's line 1625 check passed on the pre-bet read of 60,000; the conditional update at line 1630 then finds 40,000 and returns null. `shortOfFunds(w, 50000)` runs on the stale w: bonusExplainsIt = 10,000 > 0 && 50,000 <= 70,000 → true. The player is shown the bonus-locked wagering message with `detail = { balance: 60000, needed: 50000 }` — "you cannot withdraw 50,000; your balance is 60,000; it is your bonus". All three statements are wrong.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings move. A player is given a false balance figure and a false cause on the money-out screen, and is pointed at a wagering requirement instead of at the real reason, so their next action is wrong.

findings.title: creditInternal's default transaction type is BONUS_CREDIT while it always credits the CASH balance, so cash paid to players is reported to the owner as bonus-wallet cost
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `const txnType = opts.type ?? "BONUS_CREDIT";` (line 1889-1897 region) while the wallet mutation is unconditionally `{ balance: amount }` — the cash column — and the ledger leg is `internalCreditEntries`, which credits `PLAYER:<userId>` (cash), not `PLAYER_BONUS:` (ledger.ts:535-538). Two live callers omit the type: `creditWallet`'s fall-through after a failed bonus credit (affiliate-service.ts:716) and the proposal prize fall-through (proposals-service.ts:637).
findings.whyItIsWrong: `report-money.ts:147` computes `const bonusCost = conf.filter((t) => t.type === "BONUS_CREDIT").reduce((s, t) => s + Math.abs(t.amount), 0)` and subtracts it in NGR, so real withdrawable cash appears on the owner's and the statutory pack's bonus line. RULES §2.10 names this exact misclassification as forbidden — "⛔ Never BONUS_CREDIT: agent commission is contractual income, and reporting it as bonus cost would misstate the bonus programme the Board was told is withdrawn" — and the agent path passes an explicit type for that reason (affiliate-service.ts:700-705). The player-promo and proposal paths do not, and since the bonus wallet was withdrawn from the product (RULES roll-out table, 2026-09-06) these fall-throughs are now the normal route, not the exception. The ledger disagrees with the Transaction table about the same movement: PLAYER: cash on one side, a BONUS_CREDIT-typed row on the other.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.10 (Money row: never BONUS_CREDIT for cash income, because it misstates a withdrawn bonus programme) — the same principle, applied to the two callers that do not pass a type
findings.concreteScenario: A proposal is approved with the configured prize of TZS 5,000. `creditBonus` refuses because the bonus wallet is withdrawn, so `approveProposal` falls through to `creditInternal(p.proposerId, 5000, { description: note })` with no type (proposals-service.ts:637). The player's CASH balance rises by 5,000 and the ledger credits PLAYER:<player> 5,000, but the Transaction row is typed BONUS_CREDIT. The monthly money report adds 5,000 to `bonusCost` and reports it to the owner and in the statutory pack as bonus-wallet spend on a programme the Board was told is withdrawn and which issued no grant.
findings.moneyImpact: No shilling is lost or gained — NGR is arithmetically unaffected because bonusCost is subtracted either way — but every cash prize and cash referral bonus is attributed to the wrong cost line. The bonus programme's reported cost is inflated by the full amount of every such credit, and the withdrawn-programme disclosure the Board relies on is contradicted by the operator's own report.

findings.title: The gateway's share is re-derived from LIVE config at confirm time, two lines under a comment forbidding exactly that — and falls to zero if the config read throws
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Lines 603-610 read the fee off the frozen transaction row (`const fee = t.fee ?? 0;`) under the comment "read it back, never recompute (a rate change mid-flight would reprice a withdrawal in flight)" — and then immediately recompute the gateway's slice from live config: `const wcfg = await getEffectiveConfig().catch(() => null); const gatewayShare = wcfg ? Math.min(fee, Math.max(0, Math.round(amt * Math.max(0, wcfg.withdrawalGatewayShareRate)))) : 0;`. The same expression was already evaluated and audited at initiation (line 1573) against the config live at that moment. Whichever value comes out at confirm time is what `withdrawalEntries` splits between `HOUSE:AGGREGATOR` and `HOUSE:COMMISSION` (ledger.ts:271-278).
findings.whyItIsWrong: Two internal inconsistencies, neither of which reaches the player. (1) If an operator edits `withdrawalGatewayShareRate` at /admin/config while a payout is in flight, the `withdraw.initiated` audit row and the `wdr_` ledger group disagree about the split of a fee that was frozen. (2) The `.catch(() => null)` degrades to `gatewayShare = 0`, which books the ENTIRE withdrawal fee to `HOUSE:COMMISSION` and nothing to `HOUSE:AGGREGATOR` — the operator's books then overstate net fee income and understate the gateway cost of every payout confirmed during a config-read outage. The player is unaffected: the total fee is frozen on the row, `withdrawalEntries` still sums to zero, and `levySplit` is applied to the POOL fee only (market-service.ts:3278, analytics.ts:113) — the withdrawal fee never enters the TRA/GBT base, so no tax figure moves. I am reporting this at low precisely because it is a house-books misattribution, not a player loss.
findings.rulesReference: §2.7 — "0.5 percentage points of it is the payment gateway's share" — the split is a stated rule; booking 100% of it to the operator misstates it
findings.concreteScenario: A player withdraws TZS 800,000. At initiation `fee` freezes at TZS 12,000 (1.5%) and `gatewayShare` audits as TZS 4,000 (0.5%). The payout is asynchronous and settles 20 minutes later. If the SystemConfig hydration read throws at that moment, `wcfg` is null and `gatewayShare` becomes 0: the `wdr_` group posts PLAYER -800,000, EXTERNAL:SELCOM +788,000, HOUSE:COMMISSION +12,000 and NO HOUSE:AGGREGATOR line. The books show TZS 12,000 of operator fee income against a payout that actually cost the platform TZS 4,000 in gateway charges — a TZS 4,000 overstatement of net revenue on this one payout, while the `withdraw.initiated` audit row for the same transaction says gatewayShare 4,000. The player still receives TZS 788,000 either way.
findings.moneyImpact: No player impact and no tax impact. Per-payout misattribution of the gateway's share (TZS 4,000 on a TZS 800,000 withdrawal) between HOUSE:AGGREGATOR and HOUSE:COMMISSION, which distorts the operator's own cost-of-payout reporting. Magnitude in production depends entirely on whether getEffectiveConfig() actually fails and whether the rate has been edited mid-flight — neither is determinable from the repo.

findings.title: settlePaymentWebhook reports 'deposit-confirmed' when the money was diverted to HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE — the sweep and the fast lane both count a player who got nothing as credited
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `settlePaymentWebhook` discards the return value of `settleDepositConfirmed` and returns `{ handled: true, reason: "deposit-confirmed" }` unconditionally. But `settleDepositConfirmed` has a branch (lines 423-461) that credits nothing: when the player is self-excluded or cooling off, it books the deposit to HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE, sets status AML_REVIEW, and returns `{ credited: false }`. Both callers key off the reason string alone: the fast lane does `if (r.handled && r.reason === "deposit-confirmed") confirmed++;` and the sweep does `if (r.handled) { depositsConfirmed++; clearNeedsReview(t.id); }`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The fast lane's own comment, three lines above the bug, states the rule it breaks: "Counting that as a credit inflates the metric and makes a duplicate poll look like a duplicate payment in the audit log, which is exactly the wrong signal on a money surface. Count only a fresh settle." A deposit parked in suspense is not a fresh settle — it is an open liability to a player who has NOT been credited, and it is the one case where the platform is holding cash it owes back. The sweep also calls `clearNeedsReview(t.id)` for it, forgetting the transaction in the announce-once set.
findings.concreteScenario: A player who self-excluded on Monday has a TZS 400,000 mobile-money deposit that was initiated before the exclusion and settles on Tuesday. The fast poll re-queries it, Selcom says COMPLETED, `settleDepositConfirmed` books 400,000 into HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE and sets the row to AML_REVIEW with zero credited. `settlePaymentWebhook` returns reason "deposit-confirmed", so the lane logs "[lifecycle] fast-credited 1 of 3 in-flight deposit(s)" and writes a `payments.fast_credit` WALLET audit row with confirmed: 1.
findings.moneyImpact: No money moves wrongly — the suspense booking is correct and the row does reach an operator queue via AML_REVIEW. The defect is that the audit trail and the operator log both state that 400,000 TZS was credited to a player who received nothing, on the one class of transaction where the platform is holding a player's cash pending return. That is the 'ledger sums to zero is not integrity' shape: the books balance and the record is wrong.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency (the counting rule stated at wallet-service.ts:1067-1070)

findings.title: bulkRetryAction takes an arbitrary 50 rows from an unordered listByStatus while the queue on screen is sorted oldest-first, and the overlay reports "Bulk retry done" when rows 51+ were never attempted
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: `db.txn.listByStatus("FAILED")` is `findMany({ where: { status } })` with no `orderBy` and no `take` (prisma-dal.ts:1385-1388), so Postgres returns rows in arbitrary physical order; the action then `.slice(0, 50)`. The UI beside it presents `retryQueue()`, which sorts `b.ageMs - a.ageMs` (oldest first) and paginates. The client overlay reports `if (r.stillFailed === 0) overlay.succeed("Bulk retry done", `${r.retried} dispatched.`)` (bulk-retry-controls.tsx:123), with no reference to how many rows were left unattempted, and the confirm prompt is the bare "Retry all failed?" with no count and no aggregate amount — even though up to 50 real payouts of up to TZS 999,999 each can leave on one click.
findings.whyItIsWrong: "Retry all" is neither all, nor the 50 the officer is looking at. When the queue exceeds 50 rows the batch is an arbitrary sample, so the oldest and largest obligations — the ones the age-sorted, red-bordered table puts at the top — are not preferentially retried, and a success message can be shown while the bulk of the queue was never touched. The server audit is honest (`attempted: failed.length` = the capped 50), but the officer's result card is not.
findings.rulesReference: none - internal consistency
findings.concreteScenario: The all-time FAILED queue holds 210 rows (there is no time window on `retryQueue()` or `listByStatus`). An officer clicks "Retry all". 50 arbitrary rows are attempted; all 50 succeed. The overlay reads "Bulk retry done · 50 dispatched." 160 rows remain, including a TZS 900,000 payout that has been the oldest row in the table for three days and was not in the arbitrary 50. The audit row says `{ attempted: 50, retried: 50, stillFailed: 0 }`.
findings.moneyImpact: No shillings are misdirected; the harm is that a TZS 900,000 obligation the console flags as the oldest goes unattempted while the officer is told the run is done, and that one confirm click with no figure on it can dispatch up to 50 payouts (anything under the TZS 1,000,000 AML hold, so up to ~TZS 50,000,000) without the officer seeing an aggregate.

findings.title: Stale doc-comments in ledger.ts and the schema state a retired 1% withdrawal fee, a VAT-INCLUSIVE agent fee, and that HOUSE:TAX is "never credited again" — all three are false and one of them is the misbelief behind MO-8.b
findings.whatTheCodeDoes: Four comments in the money files state facts that the code beside them contradicts, and two admin pages render one of them to officers as a label. (1) ledger.ts:22-24 declares HOUSE:TAX and HOUSE:RESERVE retired and "Never credited again" — while ledger.ts:584 and ledger.ts:624 credit HOUSE:TAX on two live paths. (2) ledger.ts:260 documents the withdrawal fee parameter as "1% of gross" — RULES §2.7 is 1.5% and `DEFAULT_WITHDRAWAL_FEE_RATE` has read 0.015 since 2026-08-14. (3) ledger.ts:601 states "The fee is VAT-INCLUSIVE by decision" — RULES §2.10 records management's 2026-09-08 amendment to EXCLUSIVE, and `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG.feeVatTreatment` is "EXCLUSIVE" (agent-config.ts:167). (4) prisma/schema.prisma:2476 documents the WITHDRAWAL_FEE enum arm as "(1%)". Downstream, house-ledger.ts:49-50 and house-book.ts:51-52 repeat the retirement claim, and src/app/admin/house/page.tsx:69 and src/app/admin/finance/page.tsx:46 both render `"HOUSE:TAX": "RETIRED — historical rows only"`.
findings.whyItIsWrong: RULES §2.7 already records that two doc-comments quoting a retired 1% default were corrected on 2026-09-08 and closes with "A number written twice is a number that will disagree with itself" — these were missed by that sweep, and one of them is in the file that owns the ledger arithmetic. The HOUSE:TAX retirement claim is not merely stale prose: it is the belief that produced MO-8.b (the account left out of `owedToOthers`), the two console labels that tell an officer a live tax liability is dead, and a guard at scripts/money-e2e.test.mts:363-364 that now asserts a false invariant — `ok("★ the RETIRED accounts (HOUSE:TAX / HOUSE:RESERVE) were never credited", deadAccounts.length === 0)` — which will go red the first time it is run against data containing a single agent registration fee or commission accrual.
findings.rulesReference: RULES.md §2.7 (withdrawal fee 1.5%; the 2026-09-08 correction of two "1% default" comments) and §2.10 (feeVatTreatment = EXCLUSIVE since 2026-09-08; withholding remitted to HOUSE:TAX).
findings.concreteScenario: An engineer sizing a fee change reads `withdrawalEntries`'s parameter doc at ledger.ts:260 and computes the gateway split against 1% of a TZS 1,000,000 withdrawal — 10,000 rather than the 15,000 the code actually charges, a 5,000 error on the largest permitted withdrawal. A compliance officer opening /admin/house after two agent registrations reads `HOUSE:TAX  36,000  RETIRED — historical rows only` and files no VAT return against it. A developer reading ledger.ts:601 implements a refund path on the INCLUSIVE assumption and back-outs 18,000 from 118,000 as 118,000×18/118 = 18,000 by coincidence of the current rate — the exact bug agent-application-service.ts:135-140 records having already been fixed once.
findings.moneyImpact: No money moves wrongly from the comments alone, but they are the documented cause of MO-8.b (TZS 18,000 of VAT per agent and 5% of every commission reported as free house cash) and they mislabel a live statutory liability as dead on the two surfaces an officer reads to compute what is owed. The 1% figures mis-size any hand calculation of the withdrawal fee by a third.

findings.title: minWithdrawalForRate over-states the enforced minimum by one shilling at 1.5%, and its guard's "one shilling below" assertion is written with <= so it passes on exactly that case
findings.whatTheCodeDoes:
`minWithdrawalForRate` solves `gross × (1 − r) ≥ 1000` in continuous arithmetic, but the fee the platform actually charges is ROUNDED: `computeWithdrawalFee` = `Math.round(amount × rate)` (payout.ts:515). The enforced condition at wallet-service.ts:1580 is `amount − round(amount × r) ≥ 1000`, which is satisfied one shilling earlier.

By hand at 1.5%: ceil(1000 / 0.985) = ceil(1015.2284) = 1016. But gross 1,015 gives fee = round(15.225) = 15 and net = 1,000, which is NOT `< PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS` — so 1,015 is accepted by the server while the refusal text and the page attribute both say 1,016. Same one-shilling overstatement at 0.5%, 1%, 2% and 10%; exact at 3% and 5%.

The guard that claims to pin this boundary asserts the wrong inequality. withdrawal-fee.test.mts:181-182 requires "one shilling below the derived minimum does NOT clear it", then tests `belowNet <= PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS` for every non-zero rate. At 1.5% belowNet is exactly 1000, so `1000 <= 1000` passes — the assertion is satisfied by the very case its own label says must be excluded. Written as `<` (which is what "does NOT clear it" means, since the enforcement is `net < 1000`), it would fail today.
findings.whyItIsWrong: It is a fourth disagreement about the same number: 1,000 in the copy, 1,000 in the schema, 1,016 in the message and the attribute, 1,015 actually enforced. The refusal sentence therefore names a minimum that is not the minimum — the same class of defect §2.9 records for the {min} placeholder that shipped in three languages, differing only in size.
findings.rulesReference: §2.9 (the refusal must name the figure the server actually enforces); §2.7 (the derived floor)
findings.concreteScenario: A player with a TZS 1,015 balance withdraws all of it. Fee = round(1015 × 0.015) = 15, net = 1,000, `net < 1000` is false — the payout is ACCEPTED and dispatched. Meanwhile the same player, had they typed 1,014, would have been told "Withdraw at least TZS 1,016" — a figure that is one shilling above the amount the platform would in fact have sent for them. Nothing breaks; the platform simply advertises a floor it does not hold itself to.
findings.moneyImpact: TZS 1 per affected boundary case — negligible in shillings. Reported because (a) it is a fourth home for a number that already has three, and (b) the guard that exists specifically to pin this boundary is written to pass on the discrepancy, so raising the fee later will not surface it either.

cleared.claim: A dispatch timeout is treated as a failure, reversing a payout that Selcom may still pay
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:770-774 — `catch (err) { ... return { ok: false, reason: "AMBIGUOUS", detail }; } // timeout / network after send — payout may be in flight`; payments.ts:463-467 — on AMBIGUOUS `runPayoutLadder` returns `{ ok: true, status: "PENDING", providerRef: transid, ... }` with the comment `⛔ STOP. Do not try the next rail.`
cleared.whyNotADefect: A timeout is classified AMBIGUOUS, the ladder stops rather than advancing, the withdrawal stays PROCESSING with the hold intact and the transid preserved for re-query. Only 401/403 — refused at the door, before any disbursement logic — is treated as definitively FAILED, and that distinction is correct and explicitly reasoned. I drove the whole ladder body; there is no arm that advances on an ambiguity.

cleared.claim: The payout query treats a 401/403 as a failed payout and refunds
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:890 — `if (!res.ok) return { status: null, detail };`
cleared.whyNotADefect: On the QUERY side any non-2xx (including the 4035 'endpoint not enabled') yields null, which the callers map to PENDING and never act on. The 401/403→FAILED rule exists only on the DISPATCH side, where it is sound.

cleared.claim: Shillings/cents confusion at the adapter boundary — Math.round(o.amount) in the rail bodies could truncate a fractional payout
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1572-1574 — `const fee = computeWithdrawalFee(amount, wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate); ... const net = amount - fee;` with payout.ts:516 `return Math.max(0, Math.round(amount * Math.max(0, rate)));`; docs/SELCOM-API-DIGEST.md:120 — `**Amount = whole TZS integer** (NOT cents). Currency `"TZS"`.`
cleared.whyNotADefect: The fee is already rounded to a whole shilling before net is derived, so `net` is an integer and `Math.round(o.amount)` in every rail body is a no-op. Nothing in the adapter multiplies or divides by 100, and the digest confirms Selcom wants whole TZS. No unit defect.

cleared.claim: selcomAdapter.withdraw can return PROVIDER_DOWN after a request has already reached Selcom, so the automatic refund could double-pay
cleared.evidence: payments.ts:368-372 — the `!env`, `!env.pin` and `!msisdn` refusals all `return` before `runPayoutLadder(env, ...)` is called
cleared.whyNotADefect: All three PROVIDER_DOWN preconditions are evaluated before any HTTP call is made, so `settleWithdrawalFailed` on that arm reverses a hold for a request that provably never left the process. The only other PROVIDER_DOWN is 'every rung refused definitively', which is 401/403-or-hard-reject only.

cleared.claim: railOf() defaulting a null payoutRail to WALLET_CASHIN could query the wrong endpoint and refund a paid payout
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:616-618 — `export function railOf(payoutRail) { return isPayoutRail(payoutRail) ? payoutRail : "WALLET_CASHIN"; }`; the rail is persisted alongside the ref at wallet-service.ts:1770-1774 and 770-774
cleared.whyNotADefect: WALLET_CASHIN was the only rail that ever ran before the column existed, so the default is factually right for every legacy row, and every new dispatch persists `payoutRail` in the same update as `providerRef`. All three consumers (webhook, fast lane, reconcile sweep) thread the rail off the transaction row consistently. The residual risk is the id substitution in MO-6.a, not the rail default.

cleared.claim: The fast payout lane (every 15s) could reverse an in-flight payout
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1155-1157 — `if (v.status !== "CONFIRMED") continue; const r = await settlePaymentWebhook({ providerRef: t.providerRef!, status: "CONFIRMED" });`
cleared.whyNotADefect: The lane is genuinely confirm-only in code, not merely in its comment: the single `continue` guard means FAILED and PENDING both fall through untouched, and the only settle call is hardcoded to CONFIRMED. I checked the whole function; there is no reversal path.

cleared.claim: The reconcile sweep has the same split-id defect as the webhook
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1290-1294 — `const ref = t.providerRef; ... const v = await verifyWithdrawalStatus(ref, t.payoutRail);`
cleared.whyNotADefect: The sweep asks about the ref it read off the row itself; no request body is involved and there is no second id. Its UNSUPPORTED arm also refuses to auto-reverse in ANY mode. The sweep is the well-built version of what the webhook does badly.

cleared.claim: resultcode 999 (AMBIGUOUS) is hard-failed somewhere, reversing a real payout
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:376 — `if (code === "000" || code === "111" || code === "927" || code === "999" || [...].includes(result)) return "ACCEPTED";` and selcom.ts:387 — `if (code === "111" || code === "927" || code === "999" || ...) return null;`
cleared.whyNotADefect: 999 is correctly non-terminal on both the initiate verdict and the settlement verdict, matching docs/SELCOM-API-DIGEST.md §8 ('⚠️ NEVER hard-fail'). The defect in that function is the fall-through for an ABSENT code (MO-6.b), not the handling of the documented ones.

cleared.claim: verifySelcomCallback has no timestamp-freshness window, so a genuine callback can be replayed for ever
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:135-152 — the function checks only presence of signedFields/timestamp/digest and then HMACs; there is no skew comparison, unlike crypto.ts:203-208 which enforces a 300-second window on the generic lane
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not reported separately because the signature is not enforced at all on the Selcom lane — an attacker never needs a captured callback to replay. The missing freshness window is subsumed by MO-6.a; fixing MO-6.a by enforcing `sigOk` would then make this window a live requirement.

cleared.claim: The Selcom callback response bodies leak whether a providerRef exists ('unknown-reference' vs 'non-terminal-status')
cleared.evidence: route.ts:244 — `if (!txn) return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, ignored: true, reason: "unknown-reference" });`
cleared.whyNotADefect: It is an existence oracle over random 12-character ids, not a money movement. Out of scope for a money-correctness lane, and it costs one gateway round-trip per probe rather than any shillings.

cleared.claim: payout-status.ts could suppress a real outage or manufacture a false one and cost money
cleared.evidence: payout-status.ts:136 — `status: worstOf(c.declared, derived)`; payout-status.ts:119-121 — `catch { return { derived: "operational", stuckCount: 0, oldestStuckHours: null }; }`
cleared.whyNotADefect: Read in full. It only decides what the player is TOLD and whether the withdraw form accepts a submission; it moves no money and terminalises nothing. The declared floor can only make the picture worse, and the DB-failure fallback affects the derived half alone, so it cannot suppress a declared outage.

cleared.claim: selcom-statement.ts could misreport money that left the rail
cleared.evidence: selcom-statement.ts:99 — `slot.amount += Math.abs(t.amount);` guarded by `if (t.status !== "CONFIRMED") continue;`, and the `source: "rail" | "ledger"` provenance type
cleared.whyNotADefect: Read in full. It is a pure reporting function over confirmed DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL/BET_PAYOUT tallies with the sign handled correctly (withdrawals are stored negative and absolutised), and it never constructs a rail-sourced figure from ledger data — `railFloat()` is the only constructor. No money decision depends on it.

cleared.claim: On FAILED the player is refunded the withdrawal amount but NOT the 1.5% fee, so a payout that never left still charges them (§2.7/§2.8 violation).
cleared.evidence: withdraw() debits the GROSS, not the net: `const updated = await db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: -amount, hold: amount }, { requireBalanceGte: amount });` (wallet-service.ts:1630), where `amount` is the requested gross and `fee` is stored separately on the row (`amount: -amount, fee, taxWithheld: 0`, lines 1643-1645). The fee is never a separate wallet debit — it is only ever realised at CONFIRM, when the gateway is sent `net` and `withdrawalEntries` books fee to the house accounts. settleWithdrawalFailed returns `const amt = Math.abs(t.amount)` (line 804), i.e. the full gross.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The fee IS returned, because it was never separately taken. A TZS 200,000 withdrawal debits exactly TZS 200,000 and a failure credits exactly TZS 200,000 back. §2.8's "nothing else" holds on this path.

cleared.claim: The gateway's 0.5pp share is stranded in HOUSE:AGGREGATOR when a withdrawal fails, because the refund does not reverse it.
cleared.evidence: A repo-wide grep shows exactly one withdrawal ledger posting: `await postLedgerEntries(`wdr_${t.id}`, withdrawalEntries({ ... }), tx);` at wallet-service.ts:621, inside settleWithdrawalConfirmed. withdraw() Phase A posts no ledger group at all, and settleWithdrawalFailed posts none.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Nothing is booked to HOUSE:AGGREGATOR (or to any account) until the payout is CONFIRMED, so a FAILED withdrawal has nothing to reverse. The absence of ledger entries on the FAILED path is correct by construction, not an omission.

cleared.claim: The ledger entries for a settled withdrawal are posted outside the transaction that moves the money.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:615-622 wraps the hold release, the status flip and the ledger post in one `withMoneyTx(async (tx) => …)` and threads `tx` into all three. ledger.ts:58-59 — `const joined = currentLockTx(); if (joined) return fn(joined);` — makes that the enclosing withLock transaction. ledger.ts:104-107: an imbalanced group inside a tx THROWS rather than being audited-and-skipped, and ledger.ts:132-135 does the createMany on the tx client with no retry/swallow. withdrawalEntries sums to zero by construction: -gross + (gross - fee) + gatewayShare + (fee - gatewayShare) = 0.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The CONFIRM path is genuinely atomic and genuinely balanced. This is the correct pattern — and it is the direct evidence that the FAILED path's omission of it (MO-3.a) is a defect and not a house style.

cleared.claim: Two concurrent settleWithdrawalFailed calls (sweep racing a webhook) double-credit the player.
cleared.evidence: Both enter `withLock(`wallet:${pre.userId}`)` (line 801), which in production is `pg_advisory_xact_lock` held for the life of a $transaction (locks.ts:126-141) and is therefore mutually exclusive. Because the two writes at 806/807 run on the POOLED client, they auto-commit before the lock is released, so the second caller's `db.txn.findById` (also pooled, READ COMMITTED) sees status FAILED and line 803 returns null.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The pure concurrency race is safe — ironically because the writes are NOT in the lock transaction. The defect in MO-3.a is not a race; it is a crash or swallowed-error window between two commits followed by a LATER sweep pass. Stating it as a race would have been demolished on verify.

cleared.claim: settleWithdrawalConfirmed and settleWithdrawalFailed can both settle the same transaction (a late FAILED callback after a CONFIRMED, or vice versa), moving the money twice.
cleared.evidence: Both open with `if (!t || t.status !== "PROCESSING") return null;` (lines 600 and 803) and both hold the same `wallet:${userId}` advisory lock. settlePaymentWebhook additionally short-circuits an already-terminal transaction before dispatching to either (lines 979-984, `return { handled: true, reason: `already-${txn.status.toLowerCase()}` }`), and the officer path re-queries the provider and refuses on a CONFIRMED verdict (payment-actions.ts:259-263).
cleared.whyNotADefect: Under correct operation the status guard plus the lock makes the pair mutually exclusive. It only becomes reachable as a SECOND-ORDER consequence of MO-3.a/b leaving the status un-flipped — I have folded that compound (a late CONFIRMED after a partial FAILED pays the gateway AND leaves the refund in the player's balance) into MO-3.a rather than claiming it as an independent defect.

cleared.claim: The trial balance produces false drift for every in-flight withdrawal, because the wallet is debited at initiation but PLAYER is not debited in the ledger until confirmation.
cleared.evidence: ledger.ts:767 — `const walletReal = w ? w.balance + w.hold : 0;`. withdraw() moves balance -amount / hold +amount, so balance+hold is unchanged while PROCESSING, and PLAYER has no entry yet. On CONFIRM, hold -= amount and PLAYER is debited -gross together.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The balance+hold construction is correct and deliberate — an in-flight payout produces zero drift, as it should. But this is the same construction that nets a duplicated credit/hold-release to zero, which is why I raised MO-3.d separately: the detector is right about the normal case and structurally blind to exactly the abnormal case these paths produce.

cleared.claim: gatewayShare is computed wrongly — 0.5% of the amount rather than a share of the fee, so the gateway takes a third of the fee instead of 0.5 percentage points.
cleared.evidence: §2.7: "Charged on the amount withdrawn; 0.5 percentage points of it is the payment gateway's share." payout.ts:120-122: DEFAULT_WITHDRAWAL_FEE_RATE = 0.015, DEFAULT_WITHDRAWAL_GATEWAY_SHARE_RATE = 0.005. Both initiation (line 1573) and confirm (line 609) compute `Math.round(amount * withdrawalGatewayShareRate)`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: 0.5 percentage points of a 1.5% fee IS 0.5% of the amount — one third of the fee, by design. The arithmetic matches §2.7. The clamp `Math.min(fee, …)` also keeps the ledger group balanced if the two rates are ever configured inconsistently. (What the LIVE rates are cannot be read from the repo — these are code defaults over a SystemConfig row.)

cleared.claim: The 15-second fast payout lane can reverse a payout that is actually in flight.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1157 — `if (v.status !== "CONFIRMED") continue;` and 1158 — `const r = await settlePaymentWebhook({ providerRef: t.providerRef!, status: "CONFIRMED" });`. The lane never constructs a FAILED status and never calls settleWithdrawalFailed. scripts/fast-payout.test.mts:96-101 asserts this against the function's SOURCE TEXT, which for once is the right instrument — it would fail if the call were added.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Confirm-only, and it settles through the same exactly-once webhook path. Reversals are confined to the 30-minute sweep, whose UNSUPPORTED arm refuses to reverse on "we could not ask" (lines 1306-1319). This half of the design is sound.

cleared.claim: The AML approve-dispatch path releases the hold on the strength of its own call, so an approved large payout can be paid without ever reaching the gateway.
cleared.evidence: dispatchApprovedWithdrawal moves AML_REVIEW → PROCESSING under the wallet lock (line 735) and dispatches; on a provider refusal it reverts to AML_REVIEW with the hold intact (line 757 — `if (t && t.status === "PROCESSING") await db.txn.update(txnId, { status: "AML_REVIEW" });`), and on PENDING it leaves the row PROCESSING for the webhook/re-query. The hold is released only by settleWithdrawalConfirmed.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The hold survives the whole dispatch and money only leaves on the authoritative settle. AMBIGUOUS is never blind-reversed. This is correct.

cleared.claim: A duplicate refund would be caught by the money-invariants suite's negative-balance net.
cleared.evidence: scripts/money-invariants.test.mts:101-107 does check `w.hold < 0`. But that suite runs against the in-memory store (store.ts:1934 selects `memoryDb` when hasDatabase() is false), where withLock is a Promise-chain mutex (locks.ts:66-93) and every write self-applies in-process — the two-commit window that MO-3.a needs cannot be constructed there, and the suite never crashes a process mid-settle.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Cleared as an EXONERATION, not as a defect: the suite is real and its assertion is the right one, but it can never exercise the defect. Would it still pass if the atomicity were absent? Yes — which is why I did not treat its green as evidence.

cleared.claim: §3.2 lead, second half: "the HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE debt is CLOSED with no release leg"
cleared.evidence: rejectAmlAction posts no ledger entries at all for a DEPOSIT — the only ledger call in the whole action is absent; `postLedgerEntries` is not even imported into src/app/admin/aml/actions.ts. house-book.ts:151 `const owedToOthers = leviesPayable + aggregator + rgSuspense;` keeps counting it as a liability, and /admin/house:487 renders it as "Held for a self-excluded player".
cleared.whyNotADefect: The lead's wording is wrong in the player's favour on this one point: the debt is NOT closed in the books, it is left standing for ever. The real defect (MO-5.a) is that the CASE is closed — the row leaves AML_REVIEW, the officer is told the money went back, and no per-player record survives anywhere a human looks. Correcting the lead matters, because a fix aimed at "re-open the ledger leg" would be aimed at a leg that was never written.

cleared.claim: A read-only AUDITOR can approve or reject AML holds and move money here
cleared.evidence: `requireAdmin()` in aml/actions.ts:20-24 is `requireStaff("compliance")`; roles.ts:193-197 gives AUDITOR `compliance: { canView: true, canAct: false }`; rbac.ts:97-100 `canAct` resolves override-or-default and returns the grant's canAct; rbac.ts:57-61 on a grant-load failure logs and leaves the map EMPTY so every role falls back to DEFAULT_GRANTS.
cleared.whyNotADefect: By code default an AUDITOR is refused, the refusal is audited as `privilege_escalation_blocked`, and the loader fails CLOSED. The client `useMayAct` gate renders <ActReadOnly/> rather than a button (aml-actions-client.tsx:54). ⚠️ Grants are DB data (RoleDomainGrant, Owner-editable at /admin/roles), so the LIVE matrix cannot be settled from the repo — see productionQuestions.

cleared.claim: The two-person threshold can drift from the AML hold threshold, letting a single officer release a held payout
cleared.evidence: src/app/admin/aml/constants.ts:52 `export const TWO_PERSON_THRESHOLD_TZS = 1_000_000;` and src/lib/server/payments.ts:138 `export const AML_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_TZS = 1_000_000;`
cleared.whyNotADefect: Both are plain module constants, not `defineConfig` fields, so neither is hydrated from a SystemConfig row and the `{ ...defaults, ...restored }` override hazard does not apply. They are equal, so every AML-held withdrawal is ≥ the two-person bar and `if (gross >= TWO_PERSON_THRESHOLD_TZS)` (actions.ts:93) can never be skipped for a genuinely held payout.

cleared.claim: AML reject of a WITHDRAWAL over- or under-refunds, or leaks the hold
cleared.evidence: withdraw() phase A: `await db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: -amount, hold: amount }, { requireBalanceGte: amount })` (wallet-service.ts:1629) against reject's `await db.wallet.adjust(wallet.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt })` with `amt = Math.abs(txn.amount)` and the txn stored as `amount: -amount` (wallet-service.ts:1645).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The two are exact inverses on the gross, so balance and hold both return to their pre-withdrawal values. No ledger reversal is owed either: `withdrawalEntries` is posted only inside `settleWithdrawalConfirmed`, never at initiation, so a withdrawal that never confirmed has no ledger group to unwind.

cleared.claim: Two officers double-clicking Reject refund the same withdrawal twice, or a Reject races an Approve mid-dispatch
cleared.evidence: Both actions open with `withLock(`aml-txn:${txnId}`, …)` (actions.ts:70, 145) and both re-read `db.txn.listByStatus("AML_REVIEW")` INSIDE the lock; locks.ts:126-144 shows the production path is `pg_advisory_xact_lock` held for the transaction, safe across Railway instances.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The second caller finds the txn is no longer AML_REVIEW and returns "Transaction not in AML_REVIEW." `dispatchApprovedWithdrawal` additionally re-claims AML_REVIEW → PROCESSING under `wallet:<userId>` and returns "Withdrawal already actioned." if it lost.

cleared.claim: Approving a DEPOSIT held in AML marks it settled with nothing delivered
cleared.evidence: actions.ts:85-88 refuses `txn.type !== "WITHDRAWAL"` with a COMPLIANCE audit row `aml.approve.deposit_refused` before any state change.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The refusal is real and precedes the two-person gate and the dispatch. This is the half of the old defect that WAS fixed; the reject half (MO-5.a) is what was not.

cleared.claim: Approving a held payout marks money sent without contacting the gateway (the pre-ab72f77 defect)
cleared.evidence: dispatchApprovedWithdrawal (wallet-service.ts:718-790) claims AML_REVIEW → PROCESSING under the wallet lock, calls `dispatchWithdrawal({ … reviewed: true })`, writes the REAL `result.providerRef` plus `payoutRail`/`providerStatus`, and only settles on `result.status === "CONFIRMED"` via the shared `settleWithdrawalConfirmed`. A `!result.ok` reverts to AML_REVIEW with the hold intact.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Approval leaves the txn PROCESSING with a real gateway reference and the hold still on the wallet; nothing is marked sent on the strength of the officer's click. (Whether a STALE providerRef can be re-dispatched is MO-2's question, not settled here.)

cleared.claim: An officer can re-charge a self-excluded player by clicking "Retry now" on the FAILED RG deposit
cleared.evidence: retryDepositAction calls `deposit(t.userId, …)`, and deposit()'s FIRST door is `const lockout = await isLockedOut(userId); if (lockout.locked) { … return { ok: false, … code: "SUSPENDED", reason: "self_excluded" } }` (wallet-service.ts:138-153), ahead of identity, email, caps and SOF.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The retry is refused before any money can move, and retryDepositAction records the refusal in the row's description rather than cancelling it.

cleared.claim: An RG-held deposit inflates the player's own RG deposit cap while it sits in the queue
cleared.evidence: The RG arm sets `status: "AML_REVIEW"` (wallet-service.ts:443); `sumDepositsSince` aggregates only `["CONFIRMED", "PROCESSING"]` (prisma-dal.ts:1522).
cleared.whyNotADefect: AML_REVIEW is excluded from both the cap and the SOF sum, which is correct — the money was never credited. The cap problem is the separate phantom-PROCESSING case (MO-5.d).

cleared.claim: CLAUDE.md's "⛔ AML approval is BLOCKED for both types" describes current behaviour
cleared.evidence: CLAUDE.md:62-64 versus actions.ts:107-127, which dispatches an approved withdrawal.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Stale documentation, not a code defect — the withdrawal arm was deliberately re-enabled dispatch-first exactly as that note prescribes. Flagged only so a reader does not "restore" a block that is meant to be gone.

cleared.claim: AML reject of a WITHDRAWAL is silent to the player
cleared.evidence: rejectAmlAction sends `amlRejectRefundHtml` (actions.ts:188-196) but, unlike `settleWithdrawalFailed` (wallet-service.ts:800-822), does NOT `emit("wallet:balance", …)` and does not `notifyWithdraw(FAILED)`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: A comms/parity gap, not a money-correctness defect: the balance really is credited and the email really is sent. The live balance simply does not push until the player refreshes. Recorded here rather than reported, per the money-only instruction.

cleared.claim: The confirm screen's NET is a second re-implementation of the fee, so it can drift from what the server charges.
cleared.evidence: withdraw-confirm.tsx:17 `import { computeWithdrawalFee } from "@/lib/payout";` then :133-134 `const fee = computeWithdrawalFee(summary.amount, feeRate); const net = Math.max(0, summary.amount - fee);`. wallet-service.ts:1572-1574 `const fee = computeWithdrawalFee(amount, wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate); … const net = amount - fee;`. The rate prop comes from the same `getEffectiveConfig()` read (page.tsx:55 -> :251 `<WithdrawConfirm feeRate={wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate} />`).
cleared.whyNotADefect: It is literally the same exported function on the same rate, isomorphic by design (payout.ts:509-513: "the confirm modal (client) and wallet-service (server) both call this, so what the player is shown before confirming equals what leaves the wallet, to the shilling"). The confirm screen DOES state the net, on the loudest line of the dialog (`t.dialog.youReceive`, ReceiptRow emphasis="total"). The only residual gap is a theoretical one: `feeRate` is captured at page render and shipped as a prop, so an admin retune of `withdrawalFeeRate` between render and submit would let the dialog quote a stale rate. The window is a single page-view and requires a concurrent /admin/config edit — not worth a finding.

cleared.claim: The 1.5% withdrawal fee is hardcoded in the player copy on the withdrawal surface.
cleared.evidence: page.tsx:248 `<NoticeRow … body={fill(t.wallet.taxBody, { pct: pctNum(wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate) })} />`; i18n-dict.ts:1131 `taxBody: "A {pct}% fee applies to withdrawals, and nothing else. …"` (and :3383 SW, :5438 ZH, all with `{pct}`). `pctNum(0.015)` = 1.5 (utils.ts:417-420). A grep for `1.5%` across all three dictionaries returns nothing.
cleared.whyNotADefect: On /wallet/withdraw the rate is genuinely interpolated from live config exactly as RULES §2.7 states. The hardcode exists only on /legal/terms, which is reported separately as MO-9.e.

cleared.claim: The withdraw screen shows a withdrawable figure that includes non-withdrawable bonus money.
cleared.evidence: page.tsx:141-143 renders `formatTzs(wallet?.balance ?? 0)` under the label `t.wallet.available`; `bonusBalance` is a separate column (store.ts:169, adjusted independently at store.ts:1129 and throughout bonus-service.ts, converted to `balance` only when wagering completes at bonus-service.ts:444). The AmountField cap is `Math.min(WITHDRAW_MAX_TZS, wallet?.balance ?? 0)` (page.tsx:210) — balance only, and `hold` is already subtracted from balance by `db.wallet.adjust({ balance: -amount, hold: amount })`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Bonus is never folded into the figure the withdraw page offers, and wallet-service.ts:1622-1625 carries the same discipline explicitly ("THE FIGURE IS `w.balance`, NOT `w.balance + w.bonusBalance` … naming the sum would promise money they cannot have"). Cleanly correct; `withdraw_bonus_locked` even exists to explain the gap when a player asks for cash+bonus.

cleared.claim: A refused withdrawal can leave the player debited (money in `hold` with no payout).
cleared.evidence: Every pre-dispatch refusal in `withdraw()` returns BEFORE `db.wallet.adjust` — rate limit (:1433), schema (:1447), provider pause (:1449), destination (:1481-1503), KYC (:1543-1560), below-min (:1580-1596). The in-lock duplicate re-check at :1613 exists specifically to stop a double debit, and the dispatch-failure path calls `settleWithdrawalFailed(txnId, result.reason)` before returning (:1757).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The ordering is deliberate and correct, and the code says so at :1471-1475 ("IT SITS HERE, BEFORE THE HOLD, AND THE ORDER IS THE POINT"). No stranded-funds shape found on the player withdrawal path.

cleared.claim: The post-withdrawal success modal misstates what the player receives (it shows the GROSS).
cleared.evidence: wallet/page.tsx:265-268 passes `amount={String(Math.abs(resultOwned.amount))}` — the gross debit — and wallet-result-modal.tsx:71 renders it as `{ label: t.common.amountLabel, value: amt }` under the title "Withdrawal on its way".
cleared.whyNotADefect: The label is "Amount", the same label the confirm dialog used for its own gross row (withdraw-confirm.tsx:175) directly above the fee and the "You receive" net — so the two screens agree on what "Amount" means, and the net was disclosed one tap earlier by the same figure the server charged. It reads the STORED txn amount, never the query param (wallet/page.tsx:190-197), so it cannot be faked. Ambiguous phrasing rather than a false statement; not reported as a money defect.

cleared.claim: `payout-honesty.test.mts` §7 proves the withdraw action's bounds are correct.
cleared.evidence: scripts/payout-honesty.test.mts:209-212 — `ok("bounds come from the validators, not re-typed literals", action.includes("WITHDRAW_MIN_TZS") && action.includes("WITHDRAW_MAX_TZS"), …)`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not itself a money defect, but it is not evidence either, and it is worth recording that it pins the WRONG home in place: it asserts the action must reference `WITHDRAW_MIN_TZS` (1,000), which is precisely the constant MO-9.a shows is not the enforced minimum. It is a substring check on source text — it would pass identically if the action's bound were wrong in every other respect.

cleared.claim: `amountHint`'s "Max TZS 5,000,000" disagrees with the enforced maximum.
cleared.evidence: validators.ts:88 `export const WITHDRAW_MAX_TZS = 5_000_000;`, enforced at actions.ts:95, withdraw-confirm.tsx:85 and validators.ts:101.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The maximum agrees across all three homes. Only the minimum disagrees. (Note the §2.3 stake band of 1,000…1,000,000 is per BET and does not govern withdrawals.)

cleared.claim: The `withdraw_below_min` refusal renders a literal `{net}` or `{min}` placeholder, the way the §2.3 bet-minimum sentence once did.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1593-1595 carries the figures as NUMBERS in `detail: { net: PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT_TZS, min: minGross }`; failure-reasons.ts:319 declares `needs: ["net", "min"]`; i18n-dict.ts:2097 `errWithdrawMin: "The smallest amount we can send after the fee is {net}. Withdraw at least {min}."` and the SW/ZH twins at :4188 and :6234 both carry both placeholders.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Both declared figures are supplied and `renderFailure` fills both; the regex-out-of-prose route (`tzsFigures`) was genuinely deleted. The sentence renders correctly in all three languages. The defect is the NUMBER it names (MO-9.a / MO-9.f), not the rendering.

cleared.claim: debitInternal can overdraw a wallet, or guards the overdraw with a prior read rather than a WHERE clause
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1998 `const updated = await db.wallet.adjust(wallet.id, { balance: -take }, { requireBalanceGte: take }, tx);` and prisma-dal.ts:1285 `if (opts?.requireBalanceGte !== undefined) where.balance = { gte: opts.requireBalanceGte };` — the guard is a WHERE clause on a single conditional updateMany, applied inside the money transaction. The prior read at line 1993 (`take = Math.max(0, Math.min(want, wallet.balance))`) only sizes the request; if a concurrent spend has since drained the balance, `res.count === 0`, `adjust` returns null, line 1999 `if (!updated) return false;` and the caller returns `{ debited: 0, shortfall: want, balance: wallet.balance, taxReversed: 0 }` having written nothing.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The overdraw guard is at the database, not in application state, so it is correct under concurrency and across instances. A failed guard reports zero debited and the full shortfall — conservative in the right direction.

cleared.claim: debitInternal's proportional tax reversal produces an unbalanced ledger group
cleared.evidence: taxBack = Math.round((taxTotal * take) / want) (wallet-service.ts:1996 region); the lines built by agentCommissionEntries with amount = -take and taxWithheld = -taxBack are HOUSE:AGENT_COMMISSION −(−take + −taxBack) = +(take+taxBack), PLAYER:<user> −take, HOUSE:TAX −taxBack (ledger.ts:574-585).
