cleared.whyNotADefect: The three legs sum to exactly zero for any take and any taxBack, so postLedgerEntries' balance invariant holds on a full and on a partial recovery alike. The proportional choice is also the only one that can balance, exactly as the doc-block argues.

cleared.claim: adminAdjustBalance can drive a balance negative, or lets an officer move an arbitrary amount with no second signature
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:2076-2080 `amount < 0 ? { requireBalanceGte: -amount } : undefined` — a WHERE-clause overdraw guard inside withMoneyTx; wallet-service.ts:2051 `const ADJUSTMENT_CAP_TZS = 50_000_000;` refused at line 2058; and the only two callers in the repo (grep of the whole tree) are actions.ts:330 and actions.ts:338, both inside `adjustBalanceAction`, which imposes a two-person rule at `Math.abs(signed) >= TWO_PERSON_THRESHOLD_TZS` = TZS 1,000,000 (aml/constants.ts:10).
cleared.whyNotADefect: A debit can never write a negative balance; a single officer is bounded at TZS 999,999 per adjustment, with a mandatory ≥5-character reason, a WATCHED COMPLIANCE audit carrying the officer id, and a hard TZS 50,000,000 ceiling. The remaining weakness is the clearance/locking of the two-person record, reported separately as MO-10.c — not the bounds or the direction guard.

cleared.claim: debitInternal and adminAdjustBalance post their ledger entries outside the transaction that moves the balance
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:2013 `await postLedgerEntries(\`int_${txnId}\`, lines, tx);` and wallet-service.ts:2091 `await postLedgerEntries(\`adj_${txnId}\`, adjustmentEntries({ … }), tx);` — both pass `tx`, and ledger.ts:132-135 takes the atomic branch (`if (tx) { await tx.ledgerEntry.createMany(...); return groupId; }`) where a failure throws and rolls the wallet move back with it.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Both are correctly atomic. Only creditInternal is not (MO-10.b).

cleared.claim: bonusBalance and the cash balance are confused between the three primitives
cleared.evidence: All three mutate only `{ balance: … }` (wallet-service.ts:1888, 1998, 2077); none passes `bonusBalance` or `requireBonusBalanceGte`. Their ledger legs all hit `acct.player(userId)` = PLAYER: (ledger.ts:537, 578, 638), never `acct.playerBonus` = PLAYER_BONUS: (used only by the bonus-service builders at ledger.ts:494-513).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The money column and the ledger account agree in all three. The only bonus/cash mismatch is the TRANSACTION TYPE default, which is a reporting classification issue reported as MO-10.f, not a movement of the wrong column.

cleared.claim: creditInternal deadlocks or blocks against a settlement transaction because it writes on a different connection from the lock it holds
cleared.evidence: market-service.ts:3798-3801: "Referral commission, on the fee we ACTUALLY KEPT. Outside the market lock ... onRecruitSettlement takes the REFERRER's wallet lock, and taking a wallet lock while holding the market lock would invert buyPosition's wallet→market order and could deadlock." The call at market-service.ts:3816 is after the market lock's transaction has ended.
cleared.whyNotADefect: No settlement row lock on the agent's wallet is held while creditInternal's autocommit UPDATE runs, so the obvious lock-wait path is not reachable from the settlement caller. The non-atomicity is still a defect (MO-10.b); the deadlock/lock-wait theory is not supported.

cleared.claim: A failure between the credit and the ReferralReward row lets a resumed settlement pay the same commission twice
cleared.evidence: onRecruitSettlement credits at affiliate-service.ts:1315 and only then writes the sourceRef-bearing row at 1329-1350; but market-service.ts:3688-3689 pushes an accrual only from inside the settle loop over OPEN positions, and market-service.ts:3694-3695 states "A resumed settlement's loop sees only the still-OPEN positions".
cleared.whyNotADefect: A position whose accrual failed after the credit is already settled, so a re-run never re-attempts it — there is no second payment. The real consequence is an unrecorded payment, which is folded into MO-10.b rather than claimed as a double-pay.

cleared.claim: clawbackMarketCommission over-decrements the agent's lifetime earnings when the clawback only partly recovers
cleared.evidence: affiliate-service.ts:1450 `await db.affiliate.incrementEarned(current.referrerUserId, -current.amountTzs);` runs for the full accrual even when `res.debited < current.amountTzs`, guarded by `if (current.status === "PAID")` which mirrors the increment at line 776.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The reward row is marked REVERSED, so the accrual is no longer an earning at all — decrementing the full amount is the consistent statement, and the unrecovered part is separately audited as a debt (`affiliate.clawback.shortfall`, lines 1430-1438) rather than forgiven.

cleared.claim: Agent commission can be routed into the bonus wallet by a bonus-config switch
cleared.evidence: affiliate-service.ts:704-705 `if (policy.destination === "CASH") { return (await creditInternal(userId, amount, { description, type: policy.txnType, taxWithheld })) !== null; }` short-circuits before `referralRewardDestination()` is ever consulted, and the AGENT policy is built with `destination: "CASH"` (affiliate-service.ts:430, 1713).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The agent branch never reaches bonus-config, so no operator switch can move a partner's contracted income into a wagering-gated grant. Explicitly correct.

cleared.claim: A test proves creditInternal reports a failed credit correctly
cleared.evidence: The only suite that touches it is scripts/rg-cash-incentive.test.mts, which asserts the responsible-gambling refusals (lines 72, 85, 99, 110) — every case returns null from the RG gate at wallet-service.ts:1870-1879, i.e. BEFORE the wallet lock is ever taken. No test in the repo drives the `db.wallet.adjust → null` path.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not a defect in itself, but recorded so nobody cites a green `rg-cash-incentive` run as evidence for MO-10.a: that suite would pass identically with the wallet write removed entirely, because it never reaches the write.

cleared.claim: §3.2's named lead as literally worded: "An AML-approved payout may RE-DISPATCH on a stale providerRef → double pay" — i.e. the same transaction being sent to the gateway twice.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:724 `if (pre.status !== "AML_REVIEW") return { ok: false, error: `Withdrawal is ${pre.status}, not under review.` };` and the in-lock re-read at 734-736 `const t = await db.txn.findById(txnId); if (!t || t.status !== "AML_REVIEW") return null;`. `dispatchApprovedWithdrawal` has exactly one caller (admin/aml/actions.ts:113), which itself holds `withLock(`aml-txn:${txnId}`)` across the whole approve, and `withLock` is a Postgres `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (locks.ts:120-140) so it serialises across Railway instances. Once the row is PROCESSING every re-entry is refused, including after a crash mid-dispatch.
cleared.whyNotADefect: A second DISPATCH is genuinely blocked. But the lead points at a real hazard from the wrong end: the stale providerRef does not cause a second payment, it causes a wrong REVERSAL of the first one — which is the other half of the same double-pay. Re-aimed and reported as MO-2.a. The claim as written would have been refuted; the mechanism behind it is a blocker.

cleared.claim: The rail LADDER can advance to rail B after rail A has possibly already paid.
cleared.evidence: payments.ts:460-465 — `if (r.reason === "AMBIGUOUS") { attempts.push({ rail, transid, outcome: "AMBIGUOUS", detail: r.detail }); return { ok: true, status: "PENDING", providerRef: transid, rail, correlationId, detail: r.detail, attempts }; }` — it STOPS and returns PENDING with the hold intact. selcom.ts:790-806 classifies only HTTP 401/403 ("refused at the door") and a 2xx hard-fail resultcode as FAILED; a network throw, a timeout and every other non-2xx return AMBIGUOUS. Each rung also gets its own transid (payments.ts:454), so the ref that is persisted is the rung that can still be in flight.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The one move that turns a fallback into a double payment is correctly refused, and the taxonomy behind it is argued from a real 2026-07-29 incident. Residual uncertainty recorded as a production question: `selcomInitiateVerdict` treats a 200 with any resultcode outside {000,111,927,999} as definitive FAILED and advances — if Selcom ever emits an 'accepted' code outside that set, rung 2 would be a second live payout. No evidence in the repo that such a code exists.

cleared.claim: `notifyWithdrawalSent` tells the player money is sent before it actually is.
cleared.evidence: It has exactly one caller: wallet-service.ts:632, inside `settleWithdrawalConfirmed`'s `if (done)` block, which only runs after the status-gated release of the hold — and that is only reached from `settlePaymentWebhook`'s CONFIRMED arm, the fast lane's CONFIRMED verdict, the reconcile sweep's CONFIRMED verdict, or a synchronous `result.status === "CONFIRMED"` adapter. Its net figure is `gross - (txn.fee ?? 0)` — §2.7's 1.5% and nothing else.
cleared.whyNotADefect: On every real rail the receipt follows the provider's own confirmation. Two notes, neither a money defect: (a) its doc comment claims it is "Shared by the normal settle path AND the AML-approval release path (admin/aml/actions.ts)" — admin/aml/actions.ts never calls it; it reaches it indirectly via dispatchApprovedWithdrawal → settleWithdrawalConfirmed; (b) with the mock adapter chosen on LIVE money it fires on a payout nobody sent, which is the owner's audited 2026-07-24 simulation decision, not a code defect.

cleared.claim: A dispatch failure fails to roll the money back to the player.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1742-1754 — `!result.ok` writes `providerStatus` first, then calls `settleWithdrawalFailed`, which credits balance and releases hold. On the approve path 751-758 deliberately does NOT refund; it reverts PROCESSING → AML_REVIEW with the hold intact, gated `if (t && t.status === "PROCESSING")`. `result.ok === false` is only produced by ladder exhaustion where every rung answered definitively (payments.ts:472-474) or by an unconfigured env — states in which nothing can be in flight.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The rollback exists and is aimed at the right states. Its non-atomicity is the separate defect reported as MO-2.c; the routing decision itself is correct.

cleared.claim: The reconcile sweep can auto-reverse a payout with no provider reference (the crash-window rows).
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1290 — `if (!ref) { leftPending++; auditNeedsReviewOnce(t.id, "stale withdrawal has no providerRef — not auto-reversed", {}); continue; }` and 1306-1318, where UNSUPPORTED is deliberately NOT mode-gated: "a withdrawal that has a providerRef is never auto-reversed in ANY mode. Gating it would leave a branch shaped exactly like the bug, waiting for someone to flip a flag."
cleared.whyNotADefect: No automatic path reverses a ref-less payout. The residual exposure runs through the officer's "Return to player", where the absence of a ref disables the machine check — reported as MO-2.d rather than here.

cleared.claim: The window between `providerRef` being written (wallet-service.ts:1777) and the status flip to AML_REVIEW (1786) is a second stale-ref hazard: the row is briefly PROCESSING with a never-dispatched ref.
cleared.evidence: `isFastPayoutCandidate` requires `at < nowMs - olderThanMs` with olderThanMs = 8,000 ms, and `reconcileStalePayments` requires createdAt older than 30 minutes. The AML arm of `dispatchWithdrawal` returns before any network call (payments.ts:197-209), so only milliseconds elapse between 1777 and 1786.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Both sweeps are age-gated out of that window. If the process dies inside it the row is stranded PROCESSING with a fake ref, but nothing was dispatched, so the eventual sweep-driven refund is the correct outcome for the player — the loss is that a ≥1M payout leaves the AML queue as a refund rather than a review.

cleared.claim: `bulkRetryAction` / `retryWithdrawalAction` re-dispatch a payout an AML officer deliberately rejected.
cleared.evidence: payment-actions.ts:301 selects every FAILED withdrawal, and rejectAmlAction (admin/aml/actions.ts) sets exactly that status. But the retry goes through `withdraw()`, and every AML-rejected withdrawal is ≥ TZS 1,000,000 by construction, so `amlBasis >= AML_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_TZS` (payments.ts:197) puts the replacement straight back into AML_REVIEW rather than onto a rail.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The officer's refusal is re-opened as a review item, not converted into a payment — no money leaves. Worth an operator-facing fix (a rejected payout should not be in the bulk-retry population) but it is not a money-correctness defect.

cleared.claim: The §E-215 payout-destination law is bypassed on the approve-dispatch path.
cleared.evidence: `dispatchApprovedWithdrawal` sends `msisdn: claimed.msisdn ?? undefined` (742-748) — the number stored on the transaction, which `withdraw()` validated against `user.phoneE164` through `payoutDestinationFor` before any money moved (1479-1481).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The dispatched destination is the one the law already approved at creation. The only gap is a player who changes their registered number DURING the review: the payout then goes to the number registered when they asked, which is the safe direction and is what they requested.

cleared.claim: The existing suite covers the approve-dispatch reference handling.
cleared.evidence: scripts/payment-webhook.test.mts:225 asserts `!!await ref(selAmlTxn)` — truthiness only — on a row that already carried a truthy providerRef from wallet-service.ts:1777. Its stubbed gateway answers every `/walletcashin/query` with the same envelope regardless of transid (lines 190-197), so a query about an id Selcom never received is indistinguishable from a query about the real one.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Listed here because it is the reason MO-2.a is UNVERIFIED rather than caught: the assertion passes with the ref-write at line 770 deleted, and the fixture cannot express the failure. Not itself a money movement, so it is not filed as a finding — it is cited as evidence inside MO-2.a.

cleared.claim: `reconcileLedger()` (ledger.ts:~645) is a check that lies — it re-asserts an invariant `postLedgerEntries` already enforces at write time, and would pass with a whole category of entries missing.
cleared.evidence: `reconcileLedger` runs `SELECT "groupId", SUM(amount) … HAVING ABS(SUM(amount)) > 0.005`. `postLedgerEntries` throws on an imbalanced group inside a tx and refuses/audits it outside one, so no imbalanced group can normally be inserted. A group that was NEVER WRITTEN produces nothing to be imbalanced.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The observation is correct but it is not an undisclosed defect: ledger.ts's own comment block above `computeTrialBalance` states it in plain terms — "reconcileLedger() only asks 'does each group sum to zero?' — which postLedgerEntries already guarantees before insert, so it is structurally blind to a group that was NEVER WRITTEN (the fire-and-forget failure mode)" — and `trialBalance()` exists as the real detector, comparing per-wallet money against ledger evidence plus a global sum. The gap that remains (no check that POOL:{marketId} nets to ~0 after a market closes) is reported inside MO-8.a rather than as a separate finding.

cleared.claim: `agentCommissionEntries` is called with a `marketId` on the clawback leg (wallet-service.ts:2015) but with none on the credit leg (wallet-service.ts:1922 / affiliate-service.ts:705), so per-market ledger reads see one side of the pair.
cleared.evidence: Credit: `agentCommissionEntries({ txnId, userId, amount, taxWithheld, description })` — no marketId. Clawback: `agentCommissionEntries({ … marketId: opts.marketId })`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: No money figure moves. Every per-market reader filters by account or entryType in a way that excludes AGENT_COMMISSION: `readGameRows`/`readGameTotals` gate paidout on `entryType IN ('PAYOUT_CREDIT','REFUND','CASHOUT')`, feebooked on `account = 'HOUSE:COMMISSION'`, and leviesbooked on the two levy accounts, so `gameBook.closesTo` is untouched in both directions. The window-based `agentCommissionOut` read does not use marketId at all. It only makes the drill-down evidence panel asymmetric.

cleared.claim: `marketStore.has()` returning false on a transient database failure would make `repairOrphanedPositions` void and refund a LIVE position.
cleared.evidence: `async has(id) { const r = await pc().predictionMarket.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { id: true } }); return !!r; }` — market-dal.ts:965-968.
cleared.whyNotADefect: There is no `.catch()`: a DB error rejects, the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop, and `repairOrphanedPositions().catch(() => {})` at lifecycle.ts:474 swallows the whole run. It cannot return a false negative, so it cannot manufacture an orphan. (Contrast `delete` at market-dal.ts:963, which does `.catch(() => {})`.)

cleared.claim: `LedgerEntry` rows could be cascade-deleted when a market or user row is removed, destroying the evidence for money that moved.
cleared.evidence: `prisma/schema.prisma:2452-2471` — `txnId String?  // soft ref`, `marketId String?  // soft ref`, `userId String?  // soft ref`; no `@relation`, no `onDelete`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: All three references are plain nullable strings with indexes and no foreign key, so no delete anywhere can cascade into LedgerEntry. `chain-purge.ts` independently REDACTS PredictionMarket into a tombstone rather than deleting it and lists LedgerEntry under `NEVER` (chain-purge.ts:11-13), and it only `count()`s ledger rows in the preview.

cleared.claim: `settleWithdrawalFailed` returns TZS to spendable balance with no ledger group — a money movement with no entry.
cleared.evidence: `if (w) await db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt });` — wallet-service.ts:806, no postLedgerEntries in the function.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Correct by construction. The ledger only debits PLAYER on WITHDRAWAL when the payout CONFIRMS (wallet-service.ts:621), so a failed withdrawal has no ledger entry to reverse. `trialBalance` compares `Wallet.balance + Wallet.hold` against Σ PLAYER: precisely so the in-flight hold window nets out (ledger.ts comment block: "hold = money reserved for an in-flight withdrawal … netting hold makes both sides move together"). Moving `amt` from hold back to balance leaves `balance + hold` unchanged, so no drift is created and no entry is owed.

cleared.claim: `HOUSE:AGENT_FEE` (the TZS 100,000 net registration fee) is real revenue but is excluded from `housePosition.netRetained`, understating what the owner keeps.
cleared.evidence: `netRetained: commission + agentCommission` — house-book.ts:162; `agentFee: "HOUSE:AGENT_FEE"` is never read by name in house-book.ts or house-ledger.ts.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Deliberate and documented: ledger.ts:200-206 says the fee "buys vetting, not a bet, so it is deliberately kept out of `HOUSE:COMMISSION`, out of GGR and out of the levy base", matching RULES §2.10. `netRetained` on the Position tab is the GAMING result. The fee is still visible — `readHouseAccounts` sweeps `LIKE 'HOUSE:%'` and the page renders every entry of `all` (page.tsx:413-419) — and its cash correctly reaches `custodialCash` via EXTERNAL:SELCOM, so `freeHouseCash` picks up the 100,000 net. The 18,000 VAT half of the same posting is the real defect and is reported as MO-8.b.

cleared.claim: `refundBonusToActive` moves `Wallet.bonusBalance` with no ledger entry (bonus-service.ts:841), so every void refund of a bonus stake creates bonus drift.
cleared.evidence: `await db.bonusGrant.update(target.id, { remainingTzs: target.remainingTzs + amount }); await db.wallet.adjust(target.walletId, { bonusBalance: amount });` — no postLedgerEntries.
cleared.whyNotADefect: On the ordinary void paths the ledger side is already posted by `refundEntries` inside the money tx (market-service.ts:3342, 3471, 4148), which credits PLAYER_BONUS:{userId} with the bonus part; `refundBonusToActive` is the deliberately-separate wallet leg run outside the market lock. The two agree. (The exception is `repairOrphanedPositions`, which calls `refundBonusToActive` with no `refundEntries` counterpart — that is inside MO-8.a, not a separate finding.)

cleared.claim: `agentRegistrationFeeEntries` is posted fire-and-forget (`await postLedgerEntries(...).catch(() => {})` at agent-application-service.ts:748 and :809) rather than inside a money transaction.
cleared.evidence: `await postLedgerEntries(\`agentfee_${app.id}\`, agentRegistrationFeeEntries({ … })).catch(() => {});`
cleared.whyNotADefect: No wallet or Transaction row moves on this path — RULES §2.10 and ledger.ts:594-597 both state the fee "never enters the player ledger" and is paid out of band. There is no balance change for the ledger write to be atomic WITH, so a failure creates no wallet↔ledger drift; it is awaited, and `postLedgerEntries` still retries three times and raises a watched `ledger.post_failed` COMPLIANCE audit before returning null. Weaker than the money paths, but not a money-out atomicity defect.

cleared.claim: An officer could set `withdrawalGatewayShareRate` above `withdrawalFeeRate` and hand the gateway the entire withdrawal fee.
cleared.evidence: `withdrawalEntries` clamps `const gatewayShare = Math.min(fee, …)` (ledger.ts:267), so HOUSE:COMMISSION would receive 0.
cleared.whyNotADefect: `validateConfig` refuses the save: market-config.ts:619-625 computes `const gs = updates.withdrawalGatewayShareRate ?? store.global.withdrawalGatewayShareRate;` and returns `{ ok: false, reason: "Gateway share cannot exceed the withdrawal fee — it is paid out of it." }` when `gs > wf`, checking the merged value rather than only the field being changed. The mid-flight variant that survives this gate is reported as MO-8.e.

cleared.claim: Two containers running the unleased 15s fast poll simultaneously would double-credit a deposit or double-release a payout hold.
cleared.evidence: locks.ts:99-145 `withAdvisoryLock` uses `pg_advisory_xact_lock` inside a `$transaction` and `withLock` routes to it whenever `hasDatabase()` (line 165-167). `settleDepositConfirmed` (wallet-service.ts:407-414) and `settleWithdrawalConfirmed` (598-600) both re-read the row INSIDE that lock and return early unless `status === "PROCESSING"`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The advisory lock is transaction-scoped in Postgres and therefore serialises across containers, and both settle functions are status-gated inside it. The second container's call resolves to `already-confirmed` and is not counted (`if (r.handled && r.reason === "deposit-confirmed")`). The missing lease is real and is reported as MO-4.d, but the money consequence is duplicated gateway calls and audit rows, NOT a double credit. Saying otherwise would be the confident claim a verifier demolishes.

cleared.claim: `olderThanMs = -1` leaks into production and makes the sweep terminalise brand-new payments.
cleared.evidence: A repo-wide grep shows `reconcileStalePayments` is called with an argument only in scripts/payment-webhook.test.mts (138, 206, 211, 227, 248, 251) and scripts/reconcile-announce-once.test.mts (112, 126). The single production call site, lifecycle.ts:230, is `await reconcileStalePayments();` — the 30-minute default.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not reachable in production source. Worth recording what it WOULD do if it ever leaked: `cutoff = Date.now() + 1` matches every PROCESSING row, including one created milliseconds ago. In LIVE money-mode the damage is bounded — a mid-dispatch withdrawal has providerRef null and takes the safe no-ref arm, and a fresh deposit re-queries as PENDING. The dangerous combination is a negative cutoff plus a non-null-but-phantom providerRef, which is exactly the state MO-4.a already reaches with the DEFAULT 30-minute cutoff. There is no argument validation (`Math.max(0, olderThanMs)` or similar), so the fuse is unblown rather than absent.

cleared.claim: `notifyStillPendingDeposits` can mail the same player twice, or mail a deposit that already settled, when two containers sweep.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1357-1363 — the claim is made under `withLock(`wallet:${t.userId}`)` with a re-read: `const cur = await db.txn.findById(t.id); if (!cur || cur.status !== "PROCESSING" || cur.pendingNotifiedAt) return false; await db.txn.update(t.id, { pendingNotifiedAt: ... });`
cleared.whyNotADefect: The advisory lock serialises the read-modify-write across containers and the re-read covers both the already-notified and the already-settled cases. The header's wording ("claimed with a conditional update") is inaccurate — it is a lock plus a re-read, not a conditional UPDATE — but the property it claims genuinely holds. This function moves no money.

cleared.claim: `settleWithdrawalFailed` refunds only the net, or double-charges the 1.5% fee on a reversal.
cleared.evidence: withdraw() debits the GROSS into hold: `db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: -amount, hold: amount }, { requireBalanceGte: amount })` (line 1630) and stores `amount: -amount` with `fee` in its own column (1644-1645). settleWithdrawalFailed reverses with `amt = Math.abs(t.amount)` — the gross — at line 804-806.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Correct under §2.7/§2.8: a payout that did not happen must cost the player nothing, and the gross is what returns. No ledger entry is needed on the reversal because none is posted at hold time either — the WITHDRAWAL ledger group is posted only in `settleWithdrawalConfirmed` (line 621). The non-atomicity of those two writes is a separate defect and is reported as MO-4.b.

cleared.claim: `auditNeedsReviewOnce`'s in-memory dedupe loses money or hides an open item.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1203-1218 — `const NEEDS_REVIEW_SEEN: Set<string> = ((globalThis as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).__kpNeedsReviewSeen ??= new Set<string>())`, keyed `${txnId}::${reason}`, cleared wholesale at `NEEDS_REVIEW_CAP = 5_000`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: "Once" means once per (transaction, reason) per PROCESS. It is pinned on globalThis, so it is not lost between Next.js module instances inside one container, but it IS lost on restart and is NOT shared across containers — both stated in the header as intended ("A process restart re-announces each open item exactly once, which is intended"). The failure direction is extra audit rows, never a missing one, and /admin/payments derives its stuck count from the Transaction table rather than these rows. No money consequence.

cleared.claim: A PROCESSING transaction that is neither DEPOSIT nor WITHDRAWAL falls through the sweep loop with no counter at all, so `payments.reconcile_sweep` under-reports.
cleared.evidence: The loop is `if (t.type === "DEPOSIT") { … } else if (t.type === "WITHDRAWAL") { … }` (lines 1236, 1287) with no else. TXN_TYPES has twelve members (store.ts:251-255).
cleared.whyNotADefect: A repo-wide grep for `status: "PROCESSING"` shows only two creation sites — wallet-service.ts:286 (DEPOSIT) and 1643 (WITHDRAWAL). No other transaction type is ever written in PROCESSING, so the silent fall-through is unreachable.

cleared.claim: A transient DB error could simultaneously make `verifyDepositStatus` return UNSUPPORTED and make `isLiveMoneyMode()` return false, mass-failing paid deposits.
cleared.evidence: runtime-mode.ts:28-30 — `return process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" && process.env.TEST_FUNDING !== "true";`
cleared.whyNotADefect: `isLiveMoneyMode()` is a pure environment read with no I/O and no dependency on the payment control plane, so a DB blip cannot flip it. The predicate is nonetheless the WRONG one for this guard, for reasons independent of any race — reported as MO-4.c.

cleared.claim: The admin retry paths (`retryWithdrawalAction`, `bulkRetryAction`) re-dispatch a payout on a different rail without updating `payoutRail`, so a later re-query asks the wrong endpoint.
cleared.evidence: payment-actions.ts:181 and 312 both call `withdraw(...)`, which creates a brand-new txn row and writes `providerRef` + `payoutRail` together at wallet-service.ts:1777-1781; the old row is set to CANCELLED (183, 314).
cleared.whyNotADefect: A retry never reuses the old row, so the ref/rail pair is always written fresh and consistently. The one place the pair genuinely diverges is the AML approve-dispatch window, reported as MO-4.a.

cleared.claim: `railOf(null) → WALLET_CASHIN` is an unsafe guess that could send the sweep to the wrong endpoint on a modern row.
cleared.evidence: selcom.ts:610-618 and the guard at scripts/payout-rails.test.mts:104-107; every ladder result carries `rail` (payments.ts:459, 464) and `withdraw()` persists it whenever present.
cleared.whyNotADefect: NULL genuinely does mean wallet-cashin for pre-rail rows, and every post-rail dispatch writes the rail. The defect is not the default — it is that the AML branch produces a row with a non-null providerRef and a null rail because no rail was ever used (MO-4.a).

cleared.claim: The fast-lane counters inflate the confirmed count by including idempotent no-ops.
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1071 `if (r.handled && r.reason === "deposit-confirmed") confirmed++;` and 1162 `if (r.handled && r.reason === "withdrawal-confirmed") confirmed++;`
cleared.whyNotADefect: The already-settled case returns `already-<status>`, which the reason test excludes, so a duplicate poll does not inflate the metric. The one leak is the RG-suspense case, which also returns `deposit-confirmed` — reported separately as MO-4.h.

cleared.claim: reconcileWriteOffAction lets an officer write off an arbitrary amount taken from their own input
cleared.evidence: payment-actions.ts:280-293 reads only `txnId` and `reason` from the FormData. No amount is read, no ledger entry is posted, no wallet is adjusted. The amount in the audit payload is `Math.abs(t.amount)` — read off the stored transaction, never supplied by the officer. It also refuses anything that is not a CONFIRMED DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL and anything already carrying a providerRef.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The write-off moves no money and cannot invent a figure. It is a bookkeeping annotation on an already-settled movement, exactly as the modal says ("No money moves"). The defects in it are the sentinel collision (MO-7.b) and the fact that reconcile() then counts it as matched (MO-7.d), not the amount.

cleared.claim: reconcileMatchAction can match a transaction that is already matched
cleared.evidence: payment-actions.ts:205 — `if (t.providerRef) return { ok: false, error: "Already matched." };` — and the same guard at line 288 for the write-off. Both also require `t.status === "CONFIRMED"` and a DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL type.
cleared.whyNotADefect: An already-matched movement is refused before any write. The real exposure is a ref that collides with ANOTHER row's ref, which the DB either rejects (silently — MO-7.c) or accepts across rails, not a re-match of the same row.

cleared.claim: Some exported server action in payment-actions.ts has no role check
cleared.evidence: All eleven exported actions — toggleKillSwitchAction (40), setPaymentControlsAction (61), setPayoutStatusAction (89), testSelcomConnectionAction (112), retryDepositAction (125), cancelRefundTxnAction (145), retryWithdrawalAction (167), reconcileMatchAction (197), reverseStuckPayoutAction (239), reconcileWriteOffAction (281), bulkRetryAction (299) — open with `const g = await gate("…")` and return on `"error" in g`. `gate()` is `softRequireStaff("accounting", action, "Forbidden: your role cannot manage payments.")`, which redirects with no session, re-reads the role from the live DB (never the session claim), applies `canAct(role, "accounting")` for non-ADMIN, writes a SECURITY `privilege_escalation_blocked` row on refusal, and takes step-up TOTP via `requireAdminTotp` (rbac-guard.ts:118-140).
cleared.whyNotADefect: Every money-moving action on this surface is gated identically, on the live DB role, with 2FA and an audited refusal. No gap found. Caveat worth recording, not a finding: the file header says "All gated to ADMIN/COMPLIANCE + 2FA", but DEFAULT_GRANTS (roles.ts:175-197) gives `accounting: { canView: true, canAct: false }` to COMPLIANCE and `accounting: { canView: true, canAct: true }` to FINANCE — so by default the roles that can bulk-retry payouts are ADMIN and FINANCE, and COMPLIANCE cannot. Grants are DB data (RoleDomainGrant), so the live answer needs a production read.

cleared.claim: Bulk retry can re-dispatch a payout that already succeeded
cleared.evidence: bulkRetryAction selects only `db.txn.listByStatus("FAILED")`; a settled payout is CONFIRMED. The only automatic path that marks a withdrawal FAILED is reconcileStalePayments (wallet-service.ts:1287-1322), which refuses on a missing ref, never reverses on UNSUPPORTED ("we could not ask, NOT nothing happened"), never reverses on PENDING, and calls settleWithdrawalFailed only on a provider-confirmed FAILED. withdraw()'s own failure arm only reaches settleWithdrawalFailed on a definitive refusal — the payout ladder STOPS rather than advances on AMBIGUOUS (payments.ts:404-422).
cleared.whyNotADefect: There is no direct route from a genuinely settled payout into the FAILED bucket the bulk retry reads. The residual route is via a wrongly-reversed payout, which is MO-7.e's territory (a reversal performed with no provider query at all), not the retry selection itself.

cleared.claim: The bulk path skips a money gate that the single-row path enforces
cleared.evidence: Both call the identical `deposit()` / `withdraw()` entry points. That means both take: the per-provider kill-switch (wallet-service.ts:107 and 1450), maintenance mode, the RG lockout, the KYC gate, the E-215 payout-destination law (`payoutDestinationFor`, which the comment says binds the operator retry paths deliberately), the ≥ TZS 1,000,000 AML two-officer hold (payments.ts:197-209, `reviewed` is not set by either retry path), the atomic `WHERE balance >= amount` overdraw guard, and the PROVIDER_MIN_PAYOUT floor.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The gates are identical between the two paths. What both skip is the idempotency key the PLAYER path passes — reported as MO-7.f.

cleared.claim: The kill-switch fails OPEN when it cannot read its map, and §4.1 no longer describes it correctly
cleared.evidence: ensureKill (payment-ops.ts:121-131): `const stored = await loadConfig<KillMap>(KILL_KEY); if (stored) Object.assign(kstore, stored); globalThis.__50PICK_KILLSWITCH_HYDRATED = true;` — the latch is raised only after the read lands, the in-flight promise is shared, and a `loadConfig` failure (which returns null, never throws) leaves the flag DOWN so the next money-path call retries. On an unreadable map `kstore` is empty and `isPaymentPaused` returns false for every rail and both flows, i.e. nothing is paused.
cleared.whyNotADefect: This is the direction MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION §4.1 records as an open policy question for Ali, and the code, its comment and §4.1 all still agree: today it fails OPEN, and the permanence that made it a blocker is gone. Not proposing a change of direction. Reporting only that §4.1 remains an accurate description of the code at 2499f324.

cleared.claim: A kill-switch set on one container never reaches another, so an emergency STOP is per-instance
cleared.evidence: `ensureKill` short-circuits on `if (globalThis.__50PICK_KILLSWITCH_HYDRATED) return;` with no TTL and no invalidation, and `isPaymentPaused` reads only the process-local `kstore`. `setKillSwitch` writes `kstore` plus a fire-and-forget `saveConfig`, and nothing notifies other processes. So a second instance that hydrated before the pause would serve the paused rail for the whole life of its process.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Real in source, but NOT reachable on production today: docs/RAILWAY-LIVE.md:100 records `numReplicas` = **1**, and line 353 records that single-replica is a deliberate standing decision precisely because of per-container latches ("per-container latches incl. SELF-EXCLUSION make >1 replica a regulatory hazard; keep 1"). Recording it as a latent hazard bound to that constraint: the day 50pick scales past one replica, the kill-switch stops being a platform control. The durability half of the same code IS a live defect and is reported as MO-7.i.

cleared.claim: setPayoutStatusAction lets an officer make the player-facing payout picture better than reality
cleared.evidence: getPayoutStatus returns `status: worstOf(c.declared, derived)` (payout-status.ts:136) with `worstOf` ranking operational < delayed < unavailable, and the admin panel renders `derivedOverrodeDeclared` with "reality wins" when the queue is worse than the declaration (payout-status-control.tsx:91-99). The action validates `PAYOUT_STATUSES.includes(declared)` and preserves a null note so the localised default is used rather than a blank string.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The asymmetry holds: an officer can only make the picture worse. Declaring "operational" over a stuck queue changes nothing a player sees. Noted but not raised: `setPayoutStatus` persists through `defineConfig`'s `void saveConfig(...)`, the same un-awaited write as MO-7.i, so a declaration is also reported as applied before it is durable — but this control can only ever tighten what players are told, so a lost write reverts to the derived signal, which is the safe direction.

cleared.claim: reverseStuckPayoutAction can reverse a payout the provider has confirmed
cleared.evidence: When `t.providerRef` is present it calls `verifyWithdrawalStatus(t.providerRef, t.payoutRail)` — routed to the rail that actually carried the payout — and on CONFIRMED writes a `payments.payout_reverse_refused` audit row and returns before touching money. `settleWithdrawalFailed` is additionally status-gated to PROCESSING inside the wallet lock (wallet-service.ts:801-809), so a race with the sweep or a late callback cannot refund twice.
cleared.whyNotADefect: For the population that has a real gateway reference and a live Selcom disburse env, the check works and precedes any money movement. The gap is the population WITHOUT a ref (MO-7.e). A second, narrower risk I could not settle from the repo: reverseStuckPayoutAction proceeds on `UNSUPPORTED` ("we could not ask" — verifyWithdrawalStatus returns it when the active provider is not selcom or the disburse env is unset), which is the exact verdict reconcileStalePayments refuses to act on in ANY mode. The action's own doc-block declares that proceed a deliberate officer decision, so I am not calling it a defect — but it means a dropped PAYMENT_API_* variable turns the machine check into a no-op for every frozen payout at once.

cleared.claim: The 1.5% fee might be applied to the net, the balance, or gross+fee rather than to the amount withdrawn (§2.7)
cleared.evidence: payout.ts:515-517 `export function computeWithdrawalFee(amount: number, rate: number): number { return Math.max(0, Math.round(amount * Math.max(0, rate))); }`; wallet-service.ts:1572-1574 `const fee = computeWithdrawalFee(amount, wcfg.withdrawalFeeRate); ... const net = amount - fee;`; the wallet is debited `amount` (line 1630) and the gateway is sent `net` (line 1734 `dispatchWithdrawal({ ... amount: net, grossAmount: amount ... })`).
cleared.whyNotADefect: Worked by hand at the live 1.5%: 10,000 → fee 150, net 9,850; 50,000 → fee 750, net 49,250; 1,000,000 → fee 15,000, net 985,000. The fee is a straight percentage of the amount withdrawn, the player's balance falls by exactly the gross, and they receive gross − fee. Exactly §2.7.

cleared.claim: The gateway's 0.5pp share might be charged ON TOP of the 1.5%, breaking §2.8
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1573 `const gatewayShare = Math.min(fee, Math.max(0, Math.round(amount * Math.max(0, wcfg.withdrawalGatewayShareRate))));` — used only in the audit payload here; ledger.ts:265-280 `const gatewayShare = Math.min(fee, ...); const houseShare = fee - gatewayShare; const net = opts.grossAmount - fee;`; market-config.ts:619-626 refuses a saved gateway share that exceeds the fee.
cleared.whyNotADefect: On a 100,000 withdrawal the player pays 1,500 and receives 98,500; the 500 gateway slice is carved OUT of that 1,500 (HOUSE:AGGREGATOR 500 + HOUSE:COMMISSION 1,000), never added to it. The player's debit is `amount` and their receipt is `amount − fee` regardless of the split. The ledger group sums to zero: −100,000 + 98,500 + 500 + 1,000 = 0.

cleared.claim: BONUS balance might be withdrawable
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1625 `if (w.balance < amount) return shortOfFunds(w, amount);`; 1630 `db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: -amount, hold: amount }, { requireBalanceGte: amount })` — `bonusBalance` is a separate column and is never in the deltas or the guard; withdraw/page.tsx:210 `max={Math.min(WITHDRAW_MAX_TZS, wallet?.balance ?? 0)}` and :142 shows `wallet?.balance` as "available".
cleared.whyNotADefect: Every gate on the withdrawal path reads `Wallet.balance` alone, and the player-facing maximum is the same figure. Bonus is structurally unreachable by a withdrawal.

cleared.claim: The debit could overdraw, or a TOCTOU window could let two concurrent requests both pass the balance check
cleared.evidence: prisma-dal.ts:1284-1295 — the guard becomes `where.balance = { gte: opts.requireBalanceGte }` on a single `db.wallet.updateMany({ where, data })` with `{ increment: -amount }`, and `res.count === 0` returns null; all wallet debits in the repo take `withLock('wallet:<userId>')` (market-service.ts:1158, bonus-service.ts:174/320/730, wallet-service.ts:234/407/598/801/1602/1885/1982/2064).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The decrement is a single conditional UPDATE, so even with the advisory lock removed entirely two concurrent debits cannot both apply — the second's WHERE fails and `adjust` returns null, which line 1636 turns into a refusal. Overdraw is impossible. (The separate atomicity problem is MO-1.a, which is about the txn ROW, not about the balance going negative.)

cleared.claim: KYC / destination / provider-pause gates might sit after the debit, or be bypassable via the actorId (admin-initiated) path
cleared.evidence: Order in `withdraw`: rate limit (1432) → idempotency (1438) → schema (1447) → `isPaymentPaused` (1451) → `payoutDestinationFor(user.phoneE164, parse.data.msisdn)` (1479) → `assertKycForMoney(userId, "WITHDRAW")` (1542) → net floor (1580) → hold (1602). Both gates key on `userId`, never on `actor`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Every gate is above line 1602 and nothing has moved when any of them returns, exactly as the comments at 1471-1478 and 1544-1546 claim. `actorId` only changes who is NAMED in the audit rows (`actorId: actor`, `onBehalfOf: userId`); it never selects a branch. The two operator paths in admin/payments are bound by the identical checks.

cleared.claim: There might be a withholding tax or some other deduction (§2.8)
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1646 `taxWithheld: 0,   // no withholding tax — deleted 2026-07`; ledger.ts:270-281 books only PLAYER (−gross), EXTERNAL (+net), HOUSE:AGGREGATOR (+gatewayShare), HOUSE:COMMISSION (+houseShare); scripts/withdrawal-fee.test.mts:155-156 asserts nothing reaches HOUSE:TAX.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Exactly one deduction exists on this path and it is the withdrawal fee. §2.8 is satisfied.

cleared.claim: Ledger entries might be unbalanced, or posted outside the transaction that moves the money
cleared.evidence: ledger.ts:256-282 (`withdrawalEntries`) and wallet-service.ts:615-622 — `withMoneyTx` joins the enclosing lock's transaction (ledger.ts:57-63) and `tx` is threaded into the hold release, the status update and `postLedgerEntries`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The CONFIRM half genuinely is atomic and the group sums to zero by construction (−gross + net + gatewayShare + houseShare). No ledger group is posted at REQUEST time, which is deliberate and documented at ledger.ts:693-697 — the trial balance nets `hold` so both sides stay level during the in-flight window. (The consequence of that netting is what makes MO-1.a invisible, but the netting itself is correct.)

cleared.claim: A rate change mid-flight could reprice a withdrawal already in progress
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1440-1442 reads the fee off the stored row on a replay; :604-606 `const fee = t.fee ?? 0;` with the comment "The fee was frozen onto the txn row at initiation — read it back, never recompute".
cleared.whyNotADefect: The fee is frozen on the Transaction row at request time and every later reader takes it from there. Only the gateway SHARE is recomputed at confirm (line 608-610), and that only moves money between two house accounts — the player's charge is unaffected and the group still balances.

cleared.claim: The AML ≥ TZS 1,000,000 hold might be evaluated on the net, letting a withdrawal just over the threshold slip past the second officer
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1734 `dispatchWithdrawal({ provider: ..., amount: net, grossAmount: amount, ... })`; payments.ts:179 `const amlBasis = opts.grossAmount ?? opts.amount;` and :197 `if (!opts.reviewed && amlBasis >= AML_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_TZS) {`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The hold is evaluated on the GROSS. A TZS 1,000,000 withdrawal (net 985,000) is still held for two-officer review. Separately, the AML-reject path refunds the gross (`db.wallet.adjust(wallet.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt })`, admin/aml/actions.ts:167), so no fee is kept on a payout that never happened.

cleared.claim: Rounding could let a player be charged a fraction of a shilling, or the house lose one per withdrawal at scale
cleared.evidence: payout.ts:516 `Math.round(amount * Math.max(0, rate))` — all money is integer TZS (`z.number().int()` at validators.ts:99).
cleared.whyNotADefect: Math.round is half-up, so the largest possible discrepancy is 0.5 TZS and it falls AGAINST the player, not the house (e.g. 1,100 × 1.5% = 16.5 → charged 17). No fractional shilling can be stored or charged, and the direction cannot bleed the house.

cleared.claim: Self-exclusion and responsible-gambling lockout are not checked on the withdraw path
cleared.evidence: `withdraw` contains no `isLockedOut` call (contrast wallet-service.ts:139 in deposit and market-service.ts:949 in buyPosition); responsible-gambling.ts:243-244 `await db.user.update(userId, { status: "SELF_EXCLUDED" }); ... await db.wallet.update(wallet.id, { status: "FROZEN" });`; wallet-service.ts:1616 `if (w.status !== "ACTIVE") return { ... code: "SUSPENDED" }`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not checking RG lockout on a withdrawal is the correct direction — an excluded player must be able to reach their own money, and blocking it would trap funds. The wallet FROZEN check is the operative control, self-exclusion is its only writer, and an officer unfreeze path exists (admin/players/[id]/actions.ts:189-193). Worth an operational read (below), but not a code defect in this function.

cleared.claim: The dispatched msisdn is `parse.data.msisdn` rather than the canonical `destination.msisdn` the destination checker deliberately returns
cleared.evidence: wallet-service.ts:1479 computes `destination` but :1651 stores `msisdn: parse.data.msisdn ?? null` and :1734 dispatches `msisdn: parse.data.msisdn`; payout-destination.ts:105-109 explains it returns the registered digits so "the value written to the ledger and dispatched to the rail is the account's own, in one shape".
cleared.whyNotADefect: `tzPhone` (validators.ts:20-38) already normalises every accepted shape to canonical `+255XXXXXXXXX` before `parse.data.msisdn` exists, so the value stored and dispatched is in one stable shape whatever the player typed. The two differ only in notation (E.164 vs 9 local digits), and the equality check that authorises the payout runs on the normalised digits either way.

cleared.claim: The admin retry re-charges the withdrawal fee on the gross, double-charging the player for one payout
cleared.evidence: payment-actions.ts:181 passes `amount: Math.abs(t.amount)` (the gross); wallet-service.ts:806 `if (w) await db.wallet.adjust(w.id, { balance: amt, hold: -amt });` where `const amt = Math.abs(t.amount);`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: A failed withdrawal returns the FULL gross to spendable balance, fee included — nothing is retained. So retrying at the gross and charging the fee once more is one fee for one successful payout. (The separate concurrency problem on that path is MO-1.g.)

cleared.claim: The cross-user idempotency collision could expose another player's transaction on their wallet screen
cleared.evidence: wallet/page.tsx:193-197 `const resultTxn = ... ; const resultOwned = resultTxn && resultTxn.userId === session.userId ? resultTxn : undefined;` and :266-267 the modal renders `resultOwned.status` and `Math.abs(resultOwned.amount)`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The wallet result modal re-reads the row and refuses to render one that does not belong to the signed-in user, and it takes the status and amount from the ROW, not from the query string. The leak is limited to another account's transaction ID appearing in the redirect URL — recorded under MO-1.b rather than as a display defect.

cleared.claim: allocateFeeShares itself over- or under-collects the commission, the way the pre-2026-08-11 per-winner Math.round did
cleared.evidence: payout.ts:739-755 — `const total = Math.max(0, Math.floor(fee));` then floor each raw share, then `let remainder = total - allocated;` distributed one shilling at a time by descending fractional part with a stable id tiebreak. I ran a verbatim transcription over 15/14/13/20/40/60/100/200/1,000-winner shapes and every one summed to exactly floor(fee).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The COMMISSION half is correct and exact. The defect is one layer down: the levies are taken off each of those exact shares independently instead of off their sum. allocateFeeShares is the fix that was applied to commission and never extended to the levies.

cleared.claim: settledPayoutFor's per-winner Math.round is what settlement pays, so payouts drift too
cleared.evidence: market-service.ts:3518-3522 uses `allocateWinnerPayouts(...)` and :3551 reads `const payout = payoutByPos.get(p.id) ?? 0;`. settledPayoutFor is not called on the settlement money path.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Settlement pays the largest-remainder allocation, which sums to floor(netPool) exactly. settledPayoutFor is the projection/preview function and the assertWinnerFloor tripwire. (§3.3 separately flags a disclosure-vs-payout gap at selection close — a different lane.)

cleared.claim: cashoutEntries has the same split-levy problem
cleared.evidence: ledger.ts:446-448 — `const fee = Math.max(0, Math.round(opts.fee)); const traLevyAmt = Math.round(fee * opts.rates.traTaxOnCommissionRate); const gbtLevyAmt = Math.round(fee * opts.rates.gbtLevyOnCommissionRate);`
cleared.whyNotADefect: A cash-out is ONE position and ONE fee, so the levy is computed once over the whole fee — byte-identical to levySplit's arithmetic for the same input. No fragmentation, no divergence.

cleared.claim: cashOutValue's runway rule is itself the defect

This is what stops a short/no-gap poll being sold at the wire, when the outcome is becoming visible.` RULES §2.6: "⚠️ **This is not a defect in `cashOutValue`** — the RUNWAY rule is deliberate and correct".
cleared.whyNotADefect: The code is right and the law agrees with the code. Every finding in this lane is a document or a string that disagrees with correct code, never the reverse.

cleared.claim: The clamp in poolFee's loser-share arm makes the LEAD-D claim FALSE — the combined rate is capped at settlement time independently of the form (remediation §1.6's "clamped shareOfLosers").
cleared.evidence: src/lib/payout.ts:476 `const loserRate = clamp(r.platformFeeRate + r.operatorFeeRate, 0, MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE);` with src/lib/payout.ts:183 `export const MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE = 1.0;`. The identical clamp is in describeFeeModel at payout.ts:403.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The clamp EXISTS and IS real, but its ceiling is 1.0 — 100% of the losing pool, exactly the figure the claim names. So it does not falsify the claim; it is what fixes the answer to Q4 at 100%. It is a genuine protection against something else, and that part should be recorded as sound: a hand-written SystemConfig row or a hand-written feeSnapshot carrying platformFeeRate 5.0 still settles at 100%, so netPool can never go negative and assertWinnerFloor can never throw. What it is not is a ceiling on the house's share. The "clamped shareOfLosers" §1.6 refers to is a DISPLAY fix — making the simulator quote the clamped rate rather than the raw sum — not a money-path ceiling.

cleared.claim: validate() does not really enforce MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE on BOTH fields and on their SUM (the lane brief asked me to verify the §2 not-a-defect entry).
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-config.ts:714-731 — an individual `> MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE` branch for platformFeeRate, an identical one for operatorFeeRate, and a combined block computing `pf + of` with `store.global` fallbacks and refusing `> MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE`. I confirmed 0.5+0.5 = 1.0 exactly in IEEE754, so the sum branch is not taken.
cleared.whyNotADefect: It does enforce all three. MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION.md §2's entry — "not reachable: market-config.ts validate refuses a save where the two slices sum above MAX_LOSER_SHARE_RATE" — is factually accurate. The trap is that it is accurate and unprotective at once: the previous finder was answered with a constant whose name promises a ceiling and whose value is the whole losing pool. The bug is in the constant, not in the enforcement.

cleared.claim: The winner-floor guardrail is wired to `feeCeilingRate`, a capped-commission concept loser-share never reads (the lane brief's hypothesis 3).
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-config.ts:754-756 passes `feeModel`, `platformFeeRate` and `operatorFeeRate` into worstCaseWinnerRatio alongside commissionRate/feeCeilingRate. src/lib/payout.ts:898-901 passes `side` into poolFee inside the sweep, with the comment "Pass `side` as the winning side so loser-share is swept honestly across BOTH outcomes".
cleared.whyNotADefect: The stated MECHANISM is wrong and should not be repeated. worstCaseWinnerRatio is fully model-aware and sweeps loser-share honestly across both outcomes. It is blind for a different and deeper reason (LEAD-D.c): under loser-share netPool >= winningPool is an algebraic identity for any clamped rate, so its predicate `worst.ratio < 1` is unsatisfiable. A verifier who tests the lead's literal wording will find it false and may discard the whole finding; the correct statement is "model-aware and still structurally unable to object". The guard that IS wired to the retired knob is the WARN at market-config.ts:769 (LEAD-D.b) and the test at scripts/fee-model.test.mts:374 (LEAD-D.d).

cleared.claim: The thin-poll alert is also wired to the retired model's knob and stays silent at a high loser-share rate.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-service.ts:1896-1900: `const ratios = open.map((p) => (p.stake > 0 ? (payoutByPosition.get(p.id) ?? 0) / p.stake : Infinity)); const worstWinnerRatio = ratios.length ? Math.min(...ratios) : 0; … const thinUpside = ratios.length > 0 && leanFor(worstWinnerRatio, rates.thinProfitRatio) === "thin";` — payoutByPosition is built by settledPayoutFor, the settling function.
cleared.whyNotADefect: This one was genuinely fixed (F1, 2026-08-14) and is model-correct. At a 100% rate every position's ratio is exactly 1.000, which is below THIN_PROFIT_RATIO 1.05, so `thinUpside` fires on every market. scripts/thin-market-alert.test.mts:239 even exercises an 80% profile deliberately. Two caveats worth recording rather than reporting: it is a post-close audit row, not a save-time gate, so it cannot stop the config or the money; and its own reason text reads "THIN UPSIDE — … Winners are protected (never below stake) but there is little in it for them", which frames a 100% house take as a thin-market condition rather than a misconfiguration.

cleared.claim: A per-market fee override is a second door that bypasses the loser-share validation.
cleared.evidence: src/app/admin/config/actions.ts, setMarketOverrideAction: `const DEAD_RATE_KEYS = ["commissionRate", "feeCeilingRate", "cashOutFeeRate", "thinProfitRatio"] as const; … if (attempted.length > 0) { return { ok: false, error: … } }`; and src/lib/server/market-config.ts:818-820, setMarketOverride still calls `validate(updates)` before writing.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The override action refuses rate keys outright rather than dropping them (F3), only minStake/maxStake reach setMarketOverride, and setMarketOverride runs the same validate() anyway. There is no second door here. Separately, createMarket freezes rates from getEffectiveConfig at creation, so an override stored under an existing poll's id could not reprice it in any case.

cleared.claim: A hand-written SystemConfig row could push the effective take above 100% of the losing pool, because hydration does not validate.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-config.ts:516-517 `store.global = { ...DEFAULT_GLOBAL_CONFIG, ...stored.global };` — no clamp, no validate on the hydration path. safeRate (line 326-328) is applied only in snapshotOrLegacy, and even there platformFeeRate/operatorFeeRate default to hi = 1.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The store CAN hold 5.0, but poolFee clamps at settlement (payout.ts:476), so the effective share is bounded at 100% regardless. This is exactly what the clamp is for and it works. The answer to Q4 is therefore 100% whichever door the value came through — the form, a migration, a restore, or a hand-written row.

cleared.claim: validateRateConfig lets an Up & Down chain profile inherit the POLLS' global rate through the `?? store.global` fallback in the sum check.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-config.ts:727-728 `const pf = updates.platformFeeRate ?? store.global.platformFeeRate; const of = updates.operatorFeeRate ?? store.global.operatorFeeRate;` reached from updown-config.ts:1047 and :1100 via validateRateConfig, which is synchronous and never awaits ensureHydrated().
cleared.whyNotADefect: Real in the source and worth a second look by whoever owns the config lane, but not a money defect I can evidence here: no admin surface exposes platformFeeRate or operatorFeeRate for a chain (grep of src/app/admin/updown/ returns only comments), DEFAULT_UPDOWN_CONFIG.defaultRateProfile supplies both slices explicitly (updown-config.ts:268-270) so the fallback is not taken on the live path, and any divergence it could create is bounded by the same 100% clamp. Flagged, not claimed.

cleared.claim: LEAD G as stated: "No production money-invariant job exists."
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/lifecycle.ts:14 ("run the nightly wallet↔ledger trial balance (daily)"), :82-120 `maybeReconcileLedger` on a 24h cadence inside the leader-leased pass, called at :443. Plus .github/workflows/backup-nightly.yml:20 (`cron: "15 0 * * *"`) → scripts/db-backup.mts:539-541, which runs the platform's own `trialBalance()` against the PRODUCTION database every night.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The first half of the lead is WRONG and must not be repeated as a finding. TWO production money-invariant jobs exist and both actually execute against the live database. The real defects are different and more specific: (a) the in-app one cannot tell anybody (LEAD-G.1), (b) it fails-forward on a throw (LEAD-G.2), (c) the nightly one's adjacent alarm channel is deaf to its result (LEAD-G.3), and (d) what BOTH of them check is narrower than "the books" (LEAD-G.4). Reporting 'the job does not exist' would send someone to write a third job beside two that already run — the wrong fix for all four.

cleared.claim: The whole lifecycle pass could skip the trial balance because an earlier chore throws.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/lifecycle.ts:413-450 — every chore is individually wrapped: `await maybeReconcileSchedules().catch(...)`, `await healUpDownRounds().catch(...)`, `await maybeSendUpDownDigest().catch(...)`, `await reapStuckGenerations().catch(...)`, `await expireActiveGrants().catch(...)`, `await maybePaymentSweeps().catch(...)`, `await maybeReconcileLedger().catch(...)`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The per-chore contract is real and correctly implemented. A throw in an earlier chore cannot prevent the trial balance from being attempted. The defect is what happens INSIDE `maybeReconcileLedger` on a throw (LEAD-G.2), not the pass structure.

cleared.claim: The 24-hour timer plus frequent Railway deploys means the trial balance rarely runs.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/lifecycle.ts:84-85 — `const tickerStartedAt = Date.now(); let lastReconcileAt = 0;` are module-scope and re-initialise on every boot; :89-90 gate on a 5-minute boot grace and then the 24h interval.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Backwards. Because both stamps reset on boot, a redeploy makes the trial balance run ~5 minutes later — MORE often, not less. Frequent deploys are a mitigation here, not a hazard. (The only degenerate case is a container crash-looping faster than the 5-minute grace, which has its own loud symptoms.)

cleared.claim: Two Railway containers would double-run the trial balance, or race it.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/lifecycle.ts:393-401 — `if (!(await acquireLeadership(LIFECYCLE_TASK))) { ... return; }`, documented at :382-392 as failing CLOSED; proven cross-process by ci.yml:105-107 (`s12-leader-contention.mts`).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The pass is leader-leased and fails closed, and `trialBalance()` is read-only anyway (ledger.ts:802 "Read-only"). No defect.

cleared.claim: `postLedgerEntries` swallows its failures, so a lost ledger group is invisible.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/ledger.ts:140-163 — three attempts, then `console.error` plus `void audit({ category: "COMPLIANCE", action: "ledger.post_failed", ... })`; and inside a money tx (:135-138) a failure THROWS and rolls the wallet move back with it.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The DETECTION of this case is genuinely sound: a lost group on the non-tx path moves the wallet without the ledger, which is exactly the divergence the per-wallet trial balance measures. The header claim at ledger.ts:86-89 holds. The gap is delivery (LEAD-G.1) — `ledger.post_failed` has no consumer either — not detection.

cleared.claim: `Wallet.pending` is excluded from `walletReal = balance + hold`, so money in `pending` is unreconciled.
cleared.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:546 declares `pending Decimal @default(0)`; ledger.ts:766 computes `walletReal = w.balance + w.hold`. A repo-wide grep for a production writer of that column found only src/lib/server/store.ts:1128 (`pending: w.pending + (deltas.pending ?? 0)`) in the in-memory store, with no caller passing `deltas.pending`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: No production code path was found that ever makes `pending` non-zero — deposits credit `balance` on confirm and withdrawals use `hold`. Excluding an always-zero column is not a money defect. Flagging it would be a speculative smell; if a future path starts writing `pending` it becomes real, and a production read of `SELECT SUM(pending) FROM "Wallet"` settles it in one query.

cleared.claim: The backup watchdog is itself a guard that cannot fail.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/backup/watchdog.ts:43-58 — `describeBackupAlert` has four distinct alerting arms (none/failed/unverified/stale) against one non-alerting arm; :69-75 takes injectable `now`/`run`/`notify` overrides expressly so the suite can drive the RED path without waiting 36 hours.
cleared.whyNotADefect: It is a correctly-built alarm for the thing it covers, and it does reach a human (bell + Postmark, notification-service.ts:1588-1624). The defect is its INPUT — `backupHealth()` never reads `sourceWarnings` (LEAD-G.3) — not the watchdog's own construction. Blaming the watchdog would put the fix in the wrong module.

cleared.claim: `/api/health` hides a stalled lifecycle ticker.
cleared.evidence: src/app/api/health/route.ts:95 `ticker: lifecycleTickerHealth(),` exposing `running / runningForMs / skippedConsecutive / skippedTotal` (lifecycle.ts:63-75).
cleared.whyNotADefect: It genuinely surfaces the stall counters, and honestly. What it does NOT carry is any ledger fact — no `trialBalanceOk`, no `lastTrialBalanceAt` — which is reported inside LEAD-G.1/G.2 rather than as a separate finding. Whether anything external actually polls and parses `ticker.skippedConsecutive` is a production question, not a repo fact.

cleared.claim: Sentry is a delivery channel for ledger drift.
cleared.evidence: `captureServerError` callers are exactly src/instrumentation.ts:132, src/lib/server/admission.ts:182 and :198, and src/lib/server/updown-scheduler.ts:310. Neither ledger.ts nor lifecycle.ts calls it. monitoring.ts:102 sets `maxBreadcrumbs: Number(process.env.SENTRY_MAX_BREADCRUMBS ?? 0)`, so console output is not collected either.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Not a defect in itself — Sentry is scoped to uncaught request errors by design and is correctly PII-scrubbed (monitoring.ts:59-70, 90-98). Recorded here only to close the question: it is definitively NOT a channel the ledger alarm reaches, which is load-bearing for LEAD-G.1's claim that no channel exists.

cleared.claim: CI does not run the money suites, so nothing gates a deploy on them.
cleared.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:74-75 runs `node scripts/test-all.mjs --skip responsive,motion`; scripts/test-all.mjs:44-46 enumerates every `test:*` script in package.json, which includes `test:money-invariants`, `test:ledger`, `test:pool-residual`, `test:trial-balance`.
cleared.whyNotADefect: CI does run them, on every push to main and on every PR. The finding is narrower and is reported as LEAD-G.5: they all run against the in-memory store with no DATABASE_URL, so they are fixture proofs, not production coverage. (`test:pool-residual` and `test:trial-balance` being absent from the `predeploy` chain is noted there rather than raised separately.)

cleared.claim: The config-change audit payload is DROPPED — not written or not persisted, so the record does not exist at all.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/audit.ts:201 — `payload:    canonicalize(entry.payload ?? null),` and the durable selects at :271, :526, :591, :663, :894 all include `payload: true`. The Prisma AuditLog row carries it, and the payload is part of the HMAC input (`entryHash = HMAC(prevHash || category || action || createdAt || payload, …)`).
cleared.whyNotADefect: The record IS durable and complete. Claim 1 is purely a rendering failure, which is a materially different (and more dangerous) fault than data loss: a DB read answers 'who changed the fee rate and to what' perfectly, so the remedy is a UI change, not a data recovery.

cleared.claim: settleMarket's earlier read `const allMarketPositions = await listPositionsForMarket(m.id);` is also outside the lock's transaction and therefore also wrong.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/market-service.ts:3289 — that call runs BEFORE the settlement loop writes anything in this scope, and its consumer is `winnersForAllocation(allMarketPositions, opts.outcome)`, which must see the committed WIN+OPEN set (payout.ts:653-657, ALLOCATABLE_WINNER_STATUSES).
cleared.whyNotADefect: Reading committed state is exactly what this call needs — including on a resume, where the previous run's committed WIN rows must be counted so the largest-remainder allocation reproduces identical amounts. Only the post-write read at :3699 is affected.

cleared.claim: The zero totals from settleMarket are consumed downstream as money, so a payment or accrual is wrong.
cleared.evidence: Every caller was checked: `market-scheduler.ts:265` uses only `r.ok` and the refusal code; `updown-service.ts:966` and `:1183` use only `s.ok`; `market-service.ts:1765` (demo) and `api/dev-test/seed-player-portfolio` are non-production. `settleMarketAction` (admin/settlement/actions.ts:71) renders them as a confirmation string. Referral commission is priced from `settleLevies.operatorNet`, not from the totals.
cleared.whyNotADefect: No money is misdirected by the zeros. That is why LEAD-C.3 is filed as a permanent-record and officer-confirmation defect rather than a blocker — but it is not 'harmless': the false figure is written into an append-only chain that cannot be corrected.

cleared.claim: The stranded residual means winners are underpaid relative to what RULES entitles them to.
cleared.evidence: payout.ts:700-706 — each winner receives floor(exact share) plus at most one shilling from the largest-remainder top-up, and `assertWinnerFloor` re-checks every allocation. Σ payouts is exactly floor(netPool), the largest integer distribution the pool can support.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Integer shillings cannot pay a fractional net pool exactly; no player is short of any amount the rules promise. The defect is where the leftover LANDS (POOL escrow, not HOUSE) and the fact that payout.ts states the opposite — not that a player lost money.

cleared.claim: RULES §1's production evidence — 'residual 0.00' on two real settlements — disproves Claim 3.
cleared.evidence: Both cited settlements have integral fees: Gold round #267, fee 1,820 = 13% x 14,000; poll mkt_3254d2723f3443358300, fee 1,690 = 13% x 13,000. 0.13 x L is an integer exactly when 100 divides L (13 is coprime to 100), and both losing pools are multiples of 1,000.
cleared.whyNotADefect: The production evidence is fully consistent with the mechanism rather than contradicting it — it only shows that both audited fees happened to be whole. It does not, and cannot, disprove a residual that only appears when the losing pool is not a multiple of 100. Neither settlement was capable of exercising the failing case.

cleared.claim: /admin/house/[marketId] failing to render the config payload is a fourth instance of the same defect.
cleared.evidence: src/app/admin/house/[marketId]/page.tsx:329-333 renders only 'yes'/'no' from a regex over the raw payload, with a deliberate `⛔ THE RAW PAYLOAD IS NEVER RENDERED` note explaining the choice, and its column header is 'Touched a rate?'.
cleared.whyNotADefect: That page answers a narrower question ('did a config change price this market?') and answers it correctly and deliberately. It is not a defect — but it does mean there is no third surface an officer can fall back to, which is why LEAD-C.1 is a console-wide gap rather than one page's bug.

cleared.claim: `npm run test:pool-residual` and its RED harness prove the escrow closes at zero, so Claim 3 is refuted.
cleared.evidence: scripts/pool-residual.test.mts:88 inserts `Math.round(feeRate * loserPool)` — a rounding step settlement does not perform — before computing netPool, so its fee is always integral and `grossPool - poolOut` is 0 by construction. pool-residual-red.mjs's two mutations target only the ledger's `Math.round(share * opts.fee)` fallback and the `commissionAmount:` wiring.
cleared.whyNotADefect: This is not a cleared claim — it is the reason the defect survives. The guard is genuine for the 2026-08-11 commission-rounding defect it was written for and structurally blind to the fractional-fee residual; its own 'seven odd winners / 3331' case is the one that would have caught it, neutralised by that Math.round.

cleared.claim: The TRA/GBT per-winner `Math.round` in settlementPayoutEntries also strands money in the pool.
cleared.evidence: src/lib/server/ledger.ts:367-368 — `const traLevyAmt = Math.round(commAmt * opts.rates.traTaxOnCommissionRate);` and the GBT twin; both are booked as HOUSE:COMMISSION debit + HOUSE:TRA_LEVY / HOUSE:GBT_LEVY credit, with no POOL line.
cleared.whyNotADefect: Out of this lane (it is MONEY-GATE-REMEDIATION §3.3's separate 'GBT can book ZERO' lead) and it cannot affect the pool residual — the levies move only between house accounts after the pool has already given up payout + commission. Reported here only so the settlement-arithmetic lane does not assume it was covered by LEAD-C.4.

prodQ.q: Are AZAMPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET and/or MIXX_WEBHOOK_SECRET actually set on the production Railway service? boot-checks.ts warns when they are missing, which pushes an operator to set them; if either is set, MO-6.c is live and the Selcom money path can be settled from a request body by anyone holding that secret.

Are any PAYMENT_DISBURSE_* overrides (URL / API_KEY / API_SECRET / VENDOR_ID / PIN) set in production? If yes, MO-6.d moves from latent to live and needs to be judged against what the collection host answers for a disburse transid.

What exactly does GET /v1/walletcashin/query return for a transid this vendor never sent — the HTTP status AND the resultcode? This decides whether MO-6.a works with an arbitrary string (a 200 + fail code) or only with a genuinely-failed transid the attacker already owns, and it is the same read that settles how often MO-6.b fires.

Does the wallet-cashin query envelope spell the field `resultcode` or the documented-typo `resulcode` (SELCOM-API-DIGEST.md:107 records the typo on the callback body), and does it carry an `amount`? The first decides whether MO-6.b already misreads successful payouts as FAILED; the second decides whether MO-6.e is fixable at all without a change from Selcom.

Is /api/webhooks/payments rate-limited, IP-allow-listed or otherwise restricted at the edge (Railway / Cloudflare)? Nothing in the repo restricts it — src/proxy.ts does not protect it and the route has no rate check — but an edge rule would change how fast MO-6.a can be repeated.
How many WITHDRAWAL rows are currently in PROCESSING on production, and for how long? That is the live attack surface for MO-6.a and the population that MO-6.b would refund in a single sweep.

Have any withdrawals been auto-reversed with reason `reconcile-verified-failed` where the stored providerStatus reads `FAILED: HTTP 200` with no resultcode in it? That string is the fingerprint of MO-6.b having already fired.

Are there any Wallet rows with `hold < 0` today? That is the direct fingerprint of MO-3.a or MO-3.c having already fired, and the nightly trialBalance() cannot report it (walletReal = balance + hold nets it to zero). Query: SELECT id, "userId", balance, hold FROM "Wallet" WHERE hold < 0;

Are there Wallet rows with `hold > 0` that have NO Transaction of type WITHDRAWAL in status PROCESSING or AML_REVIEW? That is MO-3.e's fingerprint — money frozen with no transaction row, invisible to every sweep and to /admin/payments. Query: wallets where hold > 0 LEFT JOIN transactions on (userId, type='WITHDRAWAL', status IN ('PROCESSING','AML_REVIEW')) with a null match.

Is there any Transaction of type WITHDRAWAL still in status PROCESSING whose age exceeds the 30-minute sweep cutoff, and how many `payments.reconcile_sweep` audit rows carry withdrawalsReversed > 0? A transaction that appears as reversed in more than one sweep is a completed double refund.

What are the LIVE values of `withdrawalFeeRate` and `withdrawalGatewayShareRate` in the SystemConfig row that market.config hydrates? The repo only shows the cold-start defaults (payout.ts:120-122, 0.015 / 0.005); configuration overrides them via { ...defaults, ...restored } and the live numbers cannot be asserted from source.

Has `getEffectiveConfig()` ever failed during a withdrawal confirmation in production (MO-3.f)? Symptom to look for: a `wdr_` ledger group with a HOUSE:COMMISSION line equal to the full fee and no HOUSE:AGGREGATOR line, on a payout whose `withdraw.initiated` audit row recorded a non-zero gatewayShare.

How many application instances run the lifecycle ticker concurrently on Railway? The advisory lock serializes settleWithdrawalFailed correctly across instances, so this does not change the verdict, but it multiplies how often the 5-minute sweep re-enters a still-PROCESSING withdrawal, which sets the blast radius of MO-3.a.
Does the SIGTERM handler on the Railway container drain in-flight requests, and for how long? The width of the MO-3.a/c crash window on a redeploy is a deployment fact, not a source fact.

What is the live balance and entry count of HOUSE:RG_SUSPENSE, and for which userIds/txnIds? (house-book.ts:79 claims "Measured 0 on production 2026-09-05"; scripts/live/ops/house-money-census.cjs:313 has the query. A non-zero balance means MO-5.a/b have already cost real players money.)

How many Transaction rows have type=DEPOSIT and amlReason LIKE 'rg_refund_due%', broken down by status? AML_REVIEW rows are unpaid debts still visible; FAILED or CANCELLED rows are debts an officer has already been told were paid.

What do the live RoleDomainGrant rows say for (AUDITOR, compliance) and (SUPPORT, compliance)? The code default is canAct:false, but the Owner can edit the matrix at /admin/roles and a code default is not a live setting.

Is PAYMENT_AGGREGATOR set to selcom on the live deployment and is NODE_ENV=production with TEST_FUNDING unset — i.e. does `isLiveMoneyMode()` return true? That decides whether the reconcile sweep's never-terminalise arm (MO-5.d) is the branch actually running.

How many DEPOSIT rows are PROCESSING and older than 24 hours, and how many of those have providerRef NULL? Each one is permanently consuming its owner's RG deposit cap and 30-day SOF sum with no operator route to clear it.

Has any 'Deposit reversed' email actually been sent on production (Postmark tag "deposit", subject prefix "Deposit reversed")? Each one is a written refund promise with a 5-working-day trace SLA that no code path can honour.

Does approveAmlAction's outer `withLock('aml-txn:…')` transaction (30s Prisma timeout, locks.ts:143) ever abort mid-dispatch on the live Selcom rail ladder? If it does, the advisory lock is released while the action continues, and the mutual exclusion the two-person gate relies on is gone. Needs a P2028 count from production logs; the double-pay consequence is MO-2's lane.

What is the live `withdrawalFeeRate` in the `market.config` SystemConfig row RIGHT NOW? Every figure above is computed at 0.015 because RULES §0 and §2.7 assert 1.5% is live, but market-config.ts:530-532 shows `persist()` writes the WHOLE global snapshot, and the CONFIG_VERSION v3 note (market-config.ts:444-450) records production sitting on a stale `minStake` of 500 for weeks while the code default read 1,000. A code default is not a live setting. If the live rate is not 0.015 then minWithdrawalForRate returns something other than 1,016 and MO-9.a's gap changes size (at the 0.05 ceiling it would be 1,053 against a displayed 1,000).

How many accounts currently hold a spendable `balance` in the band 1,000…1,015 (or, at whatever the live rate is, in [WITHDRAW_MIN_TZS, minWithdrawalForRate(liveRate) − 1])? Those are the accounts MO-9.a strands today, and the number sizes the finding.

How many `withdraw_below_min` refusals have actually been served since the gateway floor check landed on 2026-07-31? The service returns rather than audits on that branch (wallet-service.ts:1583-1596 writes no audit row), so this may only be answerable from application logs or from the absence of WITHDRAWAL txns against attempted amounts — worth knowing whether the repo can answer it at all.

Is `payoutStatus` currently `operational`, `delayed` or `unavailable`? If `unavailable`, page.tsx:125 dims the form and swaps `WithdrawConfirm` for a disabled SubmitButton (page.tsx:251), so the minimum-disagreement path (MO-9.a, MO-9.g) is not currently exercised by players and MO-9.d is instead the dominant experience. Read AuditLog on production for `action = 'config.global.updated'`: does any row exist, and what does its `payload` JSON actually contain (before/after/changes)? This is the only way to confirm what an officer would be unable to read, and to recover any rate change already made.

Read the persisted `SystemConfig['market.config']` row: what are the LIVE `platformFeeRate` and `operatorFeeRate`? `defineConfig` hydrates `{ ...defaults, ...restored }`, so the 0.03 / 0.10 constants prove nothing about production, and LEAD-C.1's whole point is that the console cannot tell you when they last moved.

Read the last 20 `market.settled` and `market.resolved` audit payloads on production: do they record `winnersPaid: 0` / `positionsSettled: 0` against non-zero `netPool` and `fee`? My analysis says yes on every first-run settlement; a single row settles LEAD-C.3 empirically.

Read the 16 `UpDownChain.rateProfile` rows: are live chains on `loser-share` or still on the frozen `capped-commission`? RULES §2.1 says chains do NOT inherit `defaultRateProfile`, and this decides whether LEAD-C.4's residual applies to live Up & Down rounds (it applies under BOTH models — the capped arm's `feeCeilingRate * smaller` with a 1/3 ceiling is fractional far more often).

Query settled markets for `SELECT marketId, SUM(amount) FROM LedgerEntry WHERE account LIKE 'POOL:%' GROUP BY marketId HAVING SUM(amount) <> 0` since the 2026-08-11 fix: how many closed at exactly +1, and is the losing pool of each a non-multiple of 100? That converts LEAD-C.4 from arithmetic to a measurement.

Read production `Position.stake` values: how many settled markets have a losing pool that is NOT a multiple of 100? This bounds LEAD-C.4's real frequency, and it also tells you whether the stake UI in practice offers only round presets or a free integer field.

Is the production deployment multi-container, and how often does it restart? That sets how much of the audit trail is visible on /admin/audit at any moment (LEAD-C.2) — the ring is per-process and starts empty.
